title: Director, Global Software Development
description:
Call to Action

Are you ready to unlock your potential? At Straumann Group we’re on an exciting journey of growth, innovation, and impact - driven by our mission to improve oral health and transform millions of lives worldwide. United by purpose, we bring our best selves to work every day, embracing a high-performance, player-learner culture that inspires collaboration, curiosity, and ambition. Here, you’ll have the opportunity to take charge of your own career, harnessing your skills, passion, and enthusiasm for learning to continually grow and progress. Together, we’re not just shaping brighter smiles, we’re unlocking the potential of people everywhere, including our own.

Intro

As Director, Global Software Development – Straumann Digital Platform, you will lead the development and delivery of a strategic technology platform at the heart of Straumann’s digital dentistry ecosystem.

You will oversee a distributed software engineering organization and help shape how our teams build, deliver, and operate scalable cloud services, connected workflows, AI-enabled capabilities, integrations, and data-driven products.

Working closely with Product Management, Architecture, Quality, Regulatory Affairs, Cybersecurity, Privacy, Operations, and other business partners, you will combine technology leadership with delivery execution and people development. A key part of the role will be helping growing engineering teams establish clear structures, effective practices, and the capabilities they need to succeed at scale.Your Role

You will:

  • Lead the end-to-end develo/pment and delivery of the Straumann Digital Platform, translating strategy into roadmaps, technical milestones, and measurable outcomes.
  • Lead and develop distributed engineering teams, creating clear accountability, effective ways of working, and strong collaboration across locations and functions.
  • Partner with architecture leaders to evolve a secure, modular, scalable, and maintainable platform architecture.
  • Strengthen engineering practices across cloud development, DevOps, continuous integration and delivery, test automation, observability, API-based integration, and secure-by-design development.
  • Balance near-term product priorities with long-term platform sustainability, including the active management of technical debt.
  • Embed quality, cybersecurity, privacy, and regulatory requirements into everyday engineering practices, including relevant medical-device software standards.
  • Improve delivery predictability, platform reliability, engineering productivity, and operational maturity through meaningful metrics and feedback loops.
  • Develop engineering managers, technical leaders, and emerging talent while helping build the capabilities required for future growth.
  • Champion responsible adoption of automation, AI-assisted development, and modern engineering tools.
  • Communicate progress, risks, dependencies, trade-offs, and investment needs clearly to senior stakeholders.

Your Profile:

  • Significant experience leading distributed software engineering teams or organizations in a complex environment.
  • Strong experience with software platforms, cloud-based architectures, enterprise software, or connected digital ecosystems.
  • Experience working in a regulated or quality-critical environment such as medical devices, healthcare, automotive, aerospace, or financial services.
  • Practical understanding of modern software engineering approaches, including DevOps, CI/CD, test automation, cybersecurity, cloud operations, and API-based integration.
  • Experience improving software delivery, quality, collaboration, and engineering effectiveness.
  • A track record of developing teams, leaders, engineering practices, and organizational capabilities.
  • Ability to communicate technical decisions and trade-offs clearly to technical and non-technical senior stakeholders.
  • Strong business perspective, with the ability to connect technology investments to customer value, scalability, quality, compliance, and lifecycle considerations.
  • Experience with medical-device software standards such as IEC 62304 or quality systems aligned with ISO 13485.
  • Experience scaling platform engineering capabilities, AI-enabled development practices, or global software operating models.

What Makes You a Great Fit

You create clarity when priorities, technologies, and stakeholder needs are complex. You give teams appropriate ownership while establishing clear expectations and accountability.

You are motivated by developing people and helping growing engineering organizations mature. You make decisions transparently, use evidence to guide priorities, and are comfortable balancing delivery speed with quality, security, compliance, and long-term technical sustainability.

You collaborate effectively across functions, cultures, and locations and build trust through clear communication, thoughtful decision-making, and consistent follow-through.


All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, or disability.

Alternative Locations: Spain : Madrid

Travel Percentage: 0 - 20%

Here, you'll find more than a job - you'll find a place that invests in your well-being, your growth and your future.

title: Community Engagement Manager, DE&I
description:
Position Summary:

As Community Engagement Manager, DE&I, you join an exclusive team of leaders responsible for the implementation of the Alzheimer’s Association Portfolio of Community Program Offerings. The Portfolio brings awareness, education and support to all communities in the United States and activates a grassroots network of individuals and community leaders to work toward a world without Alzheimer’s and all other dementia.

Utilizing your proven leadership, networking and relationship building skills to cultivate key community connections, you will drive success and expand the reach of our community offerings by strategically identifying and engaging community partners and activating and empowering volunteers, especially in new, underrepresented and rural communities. The position not only manages and supports their team but also actively contributes to day-to-day work and deliverables

As a successful community mobilizer who will manage multiple program delivery volunteers annually, you will generate excitement and enthusiasm in the community for the cause, coach and inspire your volunteers to implement proven strategies and best practices that result in increased community presence and serving more people with awareness, education and support year over year.

This position is grant funded.

Responsibilities:

  • Recruit, coach, and manage volunteers to build grassroots movements that meet organizational goals. Apply Association best practices in community engagement and volunteer activation, leveraging strong relationship-building skills to drive successful outcomes.
  • Activate and support volunteers using Association methods such as peer coaching, Mission Conversations, and quality improvement strategies. Manage a balanced, volunteer-led Portfolio of Community Program Offerings with measurable growth, stepping in as needed to ensure delivery.
  • Cultivate and manage community partnerships, including with underrepresented groups, using a relationship-based, results-driven approach that enhances awareness, education, support, and brand visibility in all communities. Manage a portfolio of high-impact community partners to host Association Community Program reaching new audiences year after year by securing and managing Community Partner agreements.
  • Develop and execute data-informed community impact plans and secure Community Partner Agreements using a relationship-sales method aligned with local needs.
  • Demonstrate cross-functional collaboration - with revenue, advocacy, leadership, and other stakeholders - to identify and qualify awareness opportunities, strategically engaging supporters to expand reach and impact. Foster a collaborative, inclusive culture that sustains long-term community impact and volunteer engagement.
  • Evaluate and improve volunteer performance as needed, and manage budgets, grants, and timelines with precision.
  • Inspire urgency and support for the Alzheimer’s Association’s full mission, advancing care, fundraising, and advocacy across all communities with an emphasis on reaching underrepresented communities with limited access to diagnosis and treatment.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience
  • 3 – 5 years of proven experience in recruiting and mobilizing volunteers to achieve goals

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

  • Confident, goal-oriented, positive self-starter able to work independently with limited supervision and collaboratively with internal and external partners
  • Demonstrated ability to develop and nurture community relationships and partnerships
  • Ability to manage and coach large numbers of volunteers at different experience levels with diplomacy
  • Ability to work with diverse communities and demonstrate inclusion coupled with the ability to work in a highly matrixed organization
  • Excellent interpersonal skills including verbal and written communication and follow-through
  • Ability and willingness to travel up to 60% within the assigned territory by car. Travel in this case is considered time spent away from the office, in the community, to fulfill the job goals. While most such travel is on the same day, occasionally overnight travel or air travel may be required. Must have valid driver’s license, access to reliable vehicle, good driving record and proof of automobile insurance
  • Ability and willingness to work some evenings and weekends as required for volunteer mentoring and coaching and attending events.
  • Strong computer skills, proficient with Microsoft Office products; experience with, or ability to rapidly learn CRM software
  • Bilingual (English/Spanish) preferred

Title: Community Engagement Manager, DE&I

Full Time: Based on 37.5 hours per week

Position Grade & Compensation: Grade 405 The Alzheimer's Association’s good faith expectation for the salary range for this role is between $66,300 – $78,800

The Alzheimer’s Association is the leading voluntary health organization in Alzheimer’s care, support and research. Our mission is to lead the way to end Alzheimer's and all other dementia– by accelerating global research, driving risk reduction and early detection, and maximizing quality care and support.

The Alzheimer’s Association announced a landmark $100 million investment in research for 2023. This unparalleled commitment is illustrative of the momentum we are building in dementia research — our investments today will lead to breakthroughs tomorrow.

At the Alzheimer’s Association, our employees are at the core of all we do. Our network of more than 1,750 employees across the United States makes a difference each and every day for those impacted by Alzheimer’s and those at risk for the disease.

title: Entry Level Technician
description:
Do you want to learn a skilled trade in the oil and gas industry? Would you love a new career with a company offering training, opportunities to advance, and the potential for multiple pay increases in your first year? Apply for our Entry Level position with Alliance! As a Monitoring Technician, you will work in a recession-proof industry protecting the environment and have the opportunity to learn and advance within our rapidly growing company. We offer a starting pay rate of $20.00 with a clear career path for upward mobility, paid time off, great benefits, and annual profit-sharing bonuses. Apply now!

During our comprehensive training process, you will learn the following responsibilities for the Entry Level Monitoring Technician (LDAR) position which are located onsite at our client sites:

  • Daily monitoring of components to detect leaking equipment (valves, pumps, connectors, etc.) which can be a source of emissions and volatile hazardous air pollutants
  • Perform and record calibrations on analyzers before use

  • Love being outdoors, working safely in all weather conditions

title: Senior Computer Technician
description:
Senior Computer Technician (On-Site) Tampa, FL

Finding the right fit:

The Senior Computer Technician provides primary in-person technology support for the Tampa and Melbourne Florida offices while serving as a senior escalation and technical leadership resource for the broader Helpdesk team. The position resolves complex issues, guides technicians through advanced troubleshooting, improves support practices and documentation, and completes advanced technology projects as assigned. Practical knowledge of artificial intelligence tools and experience applying AI to improve support, documentation, automation, or employee productivity are required.

The right candidate is an experienced Level 3 support professional who can independently resolve complex technical issues, provide dependable in-person support to the Tampa and Melbourne offices, and serve as a trusted remote resource for the broader Helpdesk team. The candidate must be comfortable leading, by example, coaching other technicians, handling confidential information, managing competing priorities, and adapting to a fast-paced environment.

On any given day, you’ll:

  • Install, configure, and troubleshoot hardware systems and software.
  • Diagnose and resolve technical issues and malfunctions with on-premises and remote devices.
  • Provide technical support and guidance to users, clients and partners, following best practices and internal IT policies.
  • Diagnose hardware issues and open manufacturer tickets as necessary to fix or replace equipment.
  • Lead or contribute to advanced technology projects assigned by Helpdesk Leadership, the System Administration team, or the Director of IT, including planning, testing, deployment, documentation, user communication, and post-implementation support.
  • Serve as a senior escalation resource for the Helpdesk team by taking ownership of complex incidents, guiding technicians through troubleshooting, identifying recurring issues, and helping ensure support requests are documented, prioritized, and resolved consistently. Provide remote technical leadership through coaching, knowledge sharing, peer review, and coordination during high-impact incidents or periods of elevated support demand.
  • Support, maintain, and ensure compliance with software licenses.
  • Participate in software and hardware evaluations.
  • Assist in performing maintenance on enterprise systems as assigned.
  • Document complex problems, root causes, and resolutions; create and maintain technical procedures and knowledge articles; and coach Helpdesk technicians on using and improving the shared knowledge base.
  • Provide reliable in-person technology support for employee owners in the Tampa and Melbourne offices, including workstation, mobile device, conferencing, printing, connectivity, and office technology issues.
  • Onboard, monitor and enforce compliance with mobile security policies.
  • Own and resolve support requests through the ticketing system for employee owners working in person or remotely, escalating or coordinating with other IT teams when an issue requires specialized access or expertise.
  • Provide printer (MFP and wide format) and copier support.
  • Maintain inventory of computer equipment and supplies.
  • Follow security policies and procedures to protect data and systems.
  • Travel to remote offices (out-of-state) as scheduled to work on end user systems or assist the administrators with projects at those locations.

Required Qualifications:

  • Five or more years of progressive IT support experience, including demonstrated success resolving Level 3 incidents, supporting multiple office locations, handling confidential information, and guiding or mentoring other support technicians.
  • Demonstrated ability to own complex incidents from initial diagnosis through resolution, coordinate with infrastructure, security, application, and vendor resources, and communicate status and business impact to affected Employee Owners.
  • Experience with MDM and MAM platforms and policies is required.
  • Demonstrated knowledge and practical experience using artificial intelligence tools in a business or IT support environment. Candidates must be able to evaluate AI-generated output, protect confidential information, follow company AI and security requirements, and apply AI responsibly to improve troubleshooting, documentation, automation, knowledge management, or Employee Owner productivity.
  • Advanced working knowledge of Microsoft 365, Windows desktop and server operating systems, Entra ID, Active Directory, Intune, Defender, Teams, SharePoint, OneDrive, and common SaaS platforms in a hybrid enterprise environment.
  • Demonstrated experience with Intune and MS Defender platforms.
  • Ability to lift, handle, and carry computer material or equipment of moderate weight (50 pounds or less). Team lifts for heavier objects if 50 pounds or greater.
  • Physical ability to occasionally push, pull, reach, bend, twist, stoop, and climb ladders.

    Desired Skills and Experiences:

    • Associate degree in an IT-related field or an equivalent combination of education, technical training, certifications, and at least five years of progressive IT support experience.
    • Excellent communication skills and strong interpersonal skills.
    • Experience in a remote environment using online diagnostic tools.
    • Strong analytical, evaluative, and problem-solving abilities.
    • Experience administering and troubleshooting Microsoft desktop and server operating systems in a business environment; relevant Microsoft certifications are preferred.
    • Familiarity with Autodesk, Bentley, and other engineering software is a plus.
    • Experience using PowerShell, Chocolatey, Microsoft Graph, or comparable scripting and automation tools to diagnose issues, deploy software, gather information, and reduce repetitive support work.
    • Desire and ability to research, learn, and utilize new technologies.

At CGI, we empower the next generation of innovators to shape the future of technology and security. As part of #GenerationCGI, you’ll join a community of graduates who are turning ambition into action and possibility into progress.

This opportunity is designed for graduates who have completed their studies and are ready to begin their CGI journey in January 2027. If you’re still at university, we’d love you to explore our other graduate opportunities and find the intake that best matches your graduation date.

As a Cloud Engineer Graduate in our Space, Defence & Intelligence business unit, you’ll help build, operate and improve secure cloud platforms that support services of national importance. You’ll work with experienced specialists across cloud, infrastructure, networking and security, developing practical skills while contributing to projects that protect national interests and deliver intelligence solutions that matter.

From your first day, you’ll be trusted to take responsibility, solve problems and contribute ideas. You’ll receive the support and development needed to build your cloud engineering expertise and define the direction of your career.

Your future duties and responsibilities:

In this role, you’ll help develop and support secure, reliable cloud environments for projects that keep the UK and its global partners secure. You’ll combine cloud technology with infrastructure, networking and automation skills to help deliver resilient services.

You may:

  • Build cloud environments: Help design, configure and maintain secure, scalable cloud infrastructure for live projects.
  • Support systems and platforms: Work with operating systems, virtualisation, networking and platform services that underpin critical applications.
  • Automate technical processes: Use scripting and automation to make the deployment, configuration and management of cloud services more efficient and reliable.
  • Monitor and troubleshoot: Investigate technical issues, support service availability and help improve the performance and resilience of cloud environments.
  • Apply security controls: Follow established processes and contribute to the secure configuration and operation of systems handling sensitive information.
  • Collaborate across disciplines: Work with cloud engineers, software developers, infrastructure specialists, security teams and client stakeholders to deliver effective solutions.
  • Innovate alongside other graduates: Take part in early careers initiatives that go beyond your day-to-day role.

Every contribution you make will help deliver outcomes with lasting impact.

Locations

This role is based in Belfast and starts in January 2027.

As CGI is a consultancy, you may be required to work in different locations, so flexibility and a willingness to travel are key.

Required qualifications to be successful in this role:

We’re seeking an ambitious graduate who is curious about cloud technology and motivated by the challenge of building secure, reliable services. You’ll bring a practical approach to problem-solving, strong attention to detail and the adaptability needed to work across different technologies and project environments.

Due to the sensitive nature of projects within the Space, Defence & Intelligence sector, candidates must meet security-clearance requirements. Applicants must typically have 5–10 years of continuous residency in the UK and be a UK national holding only a UK passport.

You should have:

  • A minimum 2:2 degree in computer science, information technology, computer engineering, engineering, mathematics or another relevant STEM subject (some roles may require a 2:1).
  • A strong interest in cloud computing, infrastructure and technology operations.
  • Good problem-solving skills and the ability to approach technical issues methodically.
  • Strong attention to detail and the ability to follow technical and security processes accurately.
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills.
  • The ability to work collaboratively as part of a technical team.
  • Adaptability and a willingness to learn new technologies and ways of working.
  • Availability to begin the role in Belfast in January 2027.

Technical skills we value include:

  • Cloud computing: Exposure to a public cloud platform such as AWS, Microsoft Azure or Google Cloud.
  • Networking: An understanding of network concepts, protocols, connectivity and secure communications.
  • Systems administration: Familiarity with configuring, maintaining or troubleshooting operating systems and technical services.
  • Virtualisation: An understanding of virtual machines, containers or virtualised infrastructure.
  • Python and automation: Experience using Python or another scripting language to automate technical tasks.
  • Security: An awareness of secure configuration, access management and the importance of protecting sensitive systems and information.

Why Join Us?

At CGI, you’ll be part of a culture that celebrates diversity, inclusion and collaboration, where your perspective is valued and your ideas contribute to meaningful outcomes.

Your journey starts with a structured Early Careers Induction Programme, giving you the foundations to succeed, along with 24/7 e-learning and opportunities to gain professional certifications that build your expertise. You’ll also join our Student Kick-start Initiative, where you’ll collaborate with other graduates on creative projects that deliver impact beyond your day-to-day role.

CGI is an unconditionally inclusive workplace where you are respected, your voice is heard and you can be yourself. We were recognised in the Sunday Times Best Places to Work List 2025 and named a UK ‘Best Employer’ by the Financial Times. We proudly hold a Gold Award in recognition of our support of the Armed Forces Corporate Covenant.

Benefits

Along with a competitive salary and a £1,000 joining bonus, you’ll enjoy benefits that support every stage of your journey. You’ll share in CGI’s success through our matched share scheme, have access to private healthcare, well-being programmes and professional training, and build financial security with a competitive pension. Beyond the day job, you’ll connect with others through graduate networks, diversity groups and social clubs that make your time at CGI both rewarding and enjoyable.

What you can expect from us:

Together, as owners, let’s turn meaningful insights into action.

Life at CGI is rooted in ownership, teamwork, respect and belonging. Here, you’ll reach your full potential because…

You are invited to be an owner from day 1 as we work together to bring our Dream to life. That’s why we call ourselves CGI Partners rather than employees. We benefit from our collective success and actively shape our company’s strategy and direction.

Your work creates value. You’ll develop innovative solutions and build relationships with teammates and clients while accessing global capabilities to scale your ideas, embrace new opportunities, and benefit from expansive industry and technology expertise.

You’ll shape your career by joining a company built to grow and last. You’ll be supported by leaders who care about your health and well-being and provide you with opportunities to deepen your skills and broaden your horizons.

That same commitment to fairness extends to how we use technology. To support our recruitment team, AI tools may be used to help assess applications though they never replace human judgement. All hiring decisions remain entirely in the hands of our recruitment professionals.

Come join our team—one of the largest IT and business consulting services firms in the world.

title: Admission Coordinator
description:
Position Title: Admission Coordinator

Department: Admission

FLSA Classification: Non-Exempt

Employee Reports to: CAO

Employment Status: Full Time

Job Description?

Summary/objective

The admissions Coordinator manages the overall admission process, referral intake, and coordinates patient admissions while following corporate policies and procedures.


Essential functions

Admissions, Referrals, and Department Coordination

  • Manages facility intake functions competently and professionally.
  • Take responsibility for tracking each referral from initial receipt through final disposition, including admission or denial.
  • Receives and records telephone inquiries, responds promptly, and directs callers to the appropriate individuals.
  • Receives, documents, and forwards referrals to the clinical team for acceptance or denial.
  • Ensures admission calls are answered by a live person Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.
  • Confirms coverage for after-hours, weekends, and holiday admissions and referrals before leaving each workday.
  • Coordinates admission of workflows, records, and statistics.
  • Completes the referral sheet at initial contact to expedite processing.
  • Ensures compliance with policies governing Medi-Cal, Medicare, commercial insurance, and other payers to minimize financial risk.
  • Directs patients and families to appropriate agencies or counselors for financial counseling.
  • Communicate admission decisions verbally and in writing to referrals and families.
  • Arrange tours of Colusa Medical Center for patients and families.
  • Initiates all admission forms, including Consent to Treat, according to written procedures and ensures they are fully completed with timely, valid signatures.
  • Scan complete admission packets to support timely billing for all discharged patients.
  • Submits an accurate midnight census daily and coordinates with accounting to ensure an error-free month-end close.
  • Maintains accurate referral and conversation statistics in the patient's Referral Tracking System.
  • Maintains complete files for all patients referred to for admission.
  • Tracks and maintains all inquiry statistics.
  • Prepares daily facility for census data and projections.
  • Prepares and submits a monthly referral report to the CAO.
  • Maintains regular communication with discharge planners.
  • Provides referring physicians, families, and other healthcare facilities with brochures and information about Colusa Medical Center programs.
  • Participates in individual outreach, referral development, and educational presentations as directed by the Administration.
  • Documents relevant patient referral information and forward it to the Clinical Liaison(s), as appropriate.
  • Coordinates with nursing and providers to arrange appropriate placement in specialty units.
  • Distributes daily census projections and admission schedules to all departments.
  • Distribute evaluation sheets and face sheets to all departments.
  • Help prepare admission materials, including cards, forms, and related documents.
  • Assists with patient admissions and obtains required signatures and consents.
  • Introduce patients and families to Colusa and its procedures.
  • Inform staff of anticipated needs, including participation and discharge-planning considerations.
  • Collaborates closely with clinical and non-clinical departments.
  • Organizes liaison calls.
  • Marketing tools to achieve customer, referrer, and payor satisfaction; ensure appropriate market penetration; maintain a positive public image; Average Daily Census goals.
  • Verifies insurance coverage before admission.
  • Notifies departments of specific requirements, IV needs, Wound care, Bariatric equipment, etc.

Supervisory responsibilities

None


Work environment

  • Be able to stand, sit, and walk for a prolonged period.
  • Be able to communicate with the doctors and the patients in a professional manner.
  • Ability to understand cultural differences.

Physical demands

  • Walk or sit for a long time.
  • Use their hands to handle, control, or feel objects, tools, or controls.
  • Use muscles to push, pull, or carry heavy objects.

Travel Required

  • None

title: Community Education Instructor – Childbirth and Breastfeeding
description:
Interested in helping expectant parents prepare for childbirth and breastfeeding? Educational Services is seeking current Woman’s Hospital team members to teach community education classes through a PRN second-job opportunity.

Instructors may teach childbirth classes, breastfeeding classes, or both, depending on experience and certifications.

What you’ll do:

  • Prepare for and teach assigned classes using approved curricula and materials.
  • Lead discussions, demonstrations, and skills practice, helping families prepare for childbirth, postpartum recovery, and breastfeeding.
  • Create a welcoming learning environment and respond to questions within your area of expertise.
  • Work closely with the Community Education Coordinator on scheduling, supplies, class logistics, and participant concerns.
  • Share participant feedback and recommendations for improving class content.

Class opportunities and typical schedules:

Class

Typical schedule

Preparing for Delivery

One Sunday per month, 1:00 PM – 5:00 PM

Lamaze: A Labor of Love

One Saturday per month, 9:00 AM –4:30 PM

Breastfeeding Basics

One Sunday per month, 1:30 PM – 5:00 PM

After Baby Comes

One Sunday per month, 12:30 PM – 5:30 PM

Complete Childbirth Series (6 classes)

Tuesday evenings, 6:00 PM – 9:00 PM

The Complete Childbirth Series combines information from other classes and may be taught by multiple instructors, dependent on instructor certifications. Assignments will be coordinated based on class needs and availability. Instructors are expected to prepare for and reliably cover agreed-upon assignments.

  • Associate or bachelor’s degree in nursing
  • At least two years of maternal-child health experience
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to explain information clearly to patients and families

title: Spa Director
description:

title: Logan University - Assistant Manager (Part-Time)
description:
Come Live Life Larger with Megaplex!

Hey there, future leader! Ready to direct your career into something epic? At Megaplex, we're not just about showing movies; we're about crafting larger-than-life memories for every guest. If you're a fanatical enthusiast for unforgettable experiences and you're ready to make every moment count, then you belong on our crew.

Why You’ll Love Working at Megaplex:

  • It's Fun! We eat, sleep, and breathe film and entertainment. If you’re a fanatical enthusiast, you’ll fit right in.
  • It's Rewarding! There’s nothing like seeing our guests light up, and you’ll be a big part of creating those awesome memories.
  • It's Exciting! We’re not just about the show; we’re growing! With 18 locations and more on the way, you're joining a team that's making things happen.
  • Great Perks! Get ready for freebies and discounts on Megaplex, Salt Lake Bees, Real Salt Lake, and Utah Royals Football Club experiences.

What You’ll Be Doing:

As an Assistant Manager, you’ll be at the heart of it all, ensuring our guests and team have a larger-than-life experience. You’ll oversee operations, make sure our service is top-notch, and bring our group events to life! This means everything from keeping the team staffed and happy, to handling the numbers, to making sure every show is picture-perfect. Most of all, you’ll be working with a team to create an atmosphere that’s pure magic for both our guests and your fellow employees.

Your Responsibilities Include:

  • Being the face of Megaplex, always ready to deliver quality guest service.
  • Overseeing all the action in the Megaplex.
  • Keeping things clean and safe for everyone.
  • Making sure our inventory is on point.
  • Planning, forecasting, and tracking sales like a pro.
  • Staying savvy with digital cinema software
  • Tackling any projection issues that come up.
  • Ensuring our building and public areas sparkle.
  • Leading and developing our awesome team.
  • Acting as Manager on Duty (MOD).
  • And other duties as assigned.

What You’ll Need to Bring to the Show:

  • 2+ years of experience in theatre management and/or guest service.
  • Exceptional guest service, leadership, and motivational skills.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication & organization skills.
  • Proficient computer skills and a working knowledge of AV equipment and POS systems.
  • The ability to deliver results with minimal supervision.
  • A passion for teaching and developing your team.
  • The ability to handle high levels of stress (it's a fast-paced environment!).
  • Physical stamina (think walking, standing, and twisting).
  • Willingness to work long hours, including evenings, weekends, and holidays (we’re open 365 days a year, and the show goes on!).

The Pay:

Assistant Managers start at $16/hour.

Showtime Hours:

Our theatre hours can run from 6 am to 2 am, with morning shifts typically starting between 8 am and 10 am and ending around 5 pm or 6 pm. Evening shifts usually start between 3 pm and 6 pm, and you might be working until midnight or even 2 am on those busy nights (like Discount Tuesdays!).

title: Training & Education Manager BeLux
description:
ABOUT STRAUMANN GROUP

Headquartered in Basel, Switzerland, the Straumann Group employs approximately 5700 people worldwide. Its products, solutions and services are available in more than 100 countries through a broad network of distribution subsidiaries and partners, featuring the global brands Straumann, Anthogyr, Neodent, Medentika, and other fully or partly owned partner companies.

Main Purpose of the Role

The T&E Manager Belgium is responsible for developing and executing a customer-centric education and KOL strategy that supports business growth across the full customer journey in Belgium. This includes aligning education, KOL engagement and partnerships with commercial priorities to support customer acquisition, development and loyalty.

The role serves as a central point for education excellence, KOL strategy, speaker management and university partnerships in Belgium. It works closely with the Head of Marketing Benelux, Marketing, Sales and Product Management, as well as Belgian academic institutions and education partners, including ITI Belgium. It adapts regional and global resources to local needs and supports activities in both Dutch- and French-speaking communities.

Key Responsibilities

1. Customer Education

  • Develop and deliver a Belgium-wide education programme aligned with commercial priorities and supporting every stage of the customer journey across relevant customer segments

  • Own the full education lifecycle, including annual planning, budgeting, execution, and assessment of customer and commercial impact

  • Link education activities to lead generation, conversion, customer development, and long-term loyalty

  • Use and further develop the Straumann education programme, adapting regional and global curricula and partner content from ITI, universities, and KOLs to Belgium’s market and language needs

  • Continuously improve education programmes and formats using customer feedback and performance insights

2. Education Delivery & Operations

  • Maintain the annual education plan and course calendar for Belgium; identify curriculum gaps and create clear learning pathways from introductory to advanced education

  • Brief and support trainers, speakers, KOLs, and lecturers; prepare faculty materials and confirm venue, product, and demo readiness before each course

  • Coordinate course-day logistics and delivery, including learner communications, attendance, feedback, and timely follow-up

  • Manage course-related purchase orders and contracts, and monitor spend against approved budgets and internal processes

3. KOL Management

  • Define and implement a Belgium KOL programme with the T&E Benelux T&E Manager aligned to business priorities

  • Identify, support, develop, and retain high-potential KOLs across brands, clinical areas, customer segments, and language communities in Belgium with the sales team and Product Managers

  • Build and maintain a structured KOL database, with clear segmentation and purposeful deployment across brands and clinical areas

  • Engage KOLs, lecturers, and clinical mentors to build credibility, gain customer insight, and strengthen the education faculty over time

  • Ensure KOL engagement supports education, customer insight, campaigns, and commercial priorities

4. Speaker Programme & Database Management

  • Maintain an up-to-date speaker database for Belgium

  • Collect speaker information such as CVs, portrait pictures and other useful information

  • Coordinate speaker agreements with ASM and the relevant internal stakeholders

  • Coordinate speaker activities and availability for Belgium education programmes

  • Align with internal stakeholders and speakers on presentation topics

  • Update speaker profiles and help to select speakers according to their profile

  • Brief speakers before the event and de-brief after the event


All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, or disability.

Alternative Locations: Belgium : Brussels

Travel Percentage: 0 - 100%

title: CMT Department Manager
description:
NOVA Engineering is seeking a Department Manager for our Construction Materials Testing and Special Inspections Divisions in our Panama City Beach and Tallahassee, FL locations. title: Order Expediter
description:
Position Summary

The Order Expediter is responsible for coordinating and monitoring customer orders to ensure timely and accurate fulfillment. This role works closely with Customer Service, Production, Planning, Procurement, and Shipping to identify and resolve delays, prioritize orders, and maintain efficient workflow throughout the order fulfillment process. The Order Expediter plays a key role in improving operational efficiency, meeting customer delivery expectations, and supporting overall customer satisfaction.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Monitor and track customer orders throughout the fulfillment process to ensure timely processing, production, and shipment.
  • Coordinate with Production, Planning, Procurement, Customer Service, and Shipping to prioritize orders and meet delivery commitments.
  • Identify potential delays, material shortages, production constraints, and other bottlenecks that may impact order fulfillment.
  • Proactively communicate with appropriate departments to resolve order-related issues and expedite critical or time-sensitive orders.
  • Monitor inventory availability, production schedules, and shipment status to ensure alignment with customer requirements.
  • Maintain accurate and up-to-date order information within company systems.
  • Provide timely updates to internal stakeholders regarding order status, delays, and anticipated delivery dates.
  • Responsible for ordering containers and raw materials from off-site warehouses to keep production supplied.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to improve order processing efficiency and streamline workflows.
  • Escalate unresolved issues or potential delivery risks to appropriate leadership.
  • Analyze order fulfillment trends and identify opportunities for process improvements to reduce delays and improve on-time delivery performance.
  • Support continuous improvement initiatives focused on operational efficiency, order accuracy, and customer satisfaction.
  • Perform additional duties and responsibilities as assigned.

Qualifications and Requirements

  • High school diploma or GED required; associate degree in Supply Chain Management, Business Administration, Logistics, or a related field preferred.
  • Previous experience in order management, customer service, production planning, logistics, or manufacturing operations preferred.
  • Working knowledge of manufacturing processes, inventory management, and order fulfillment workflows.
  • Experience using ERP systems and Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel, preferred.
  • Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills with the ability to collaborate effectively across departments.
  • Strong problem-solving skills with a proactive approach to identifying and resolving issues.
  • High attention to detail and accuracy in tracking orders and maintaining records.
  • Ability to work independently, exercise sound judgment, and meet established deadlines.

Key Competencies

  • Sense of Urgency: Proactively identifies and addresses potential delays to ensure timely order fulfillment.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Builds effective working relationships across departments to achieve shared objectives.
  • Problem-Solving: Identifies root causes of order delays and implements practical solutions.
  • Accountability: Takes ownership of assigned responsibilities and follows through to resolution.
  • Communication: Provides clear, accurate, and timely updates to stakeholders.
  • Continuous Improvement: Identifies opportunities to streamline processes and improve operational performance.

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

  • On-time order fulfillment and delivery performance.
  • Reduction in overdue and delayed orders.
  • Timeliness of issue identification and resolution.
  • Order accuracy and completeness.
  • Effectiveness of communication and coordination across departments.
  • Improvements in order processing efficiency and workflow.

Physical and Work Environment Requirements

  • Operates in an office and manufacturing environment.
  • Requires periodic presence in production and warehouse areas to coordinate order fulfillment activities.
  • Must comply with all company safety policies and required personal protective equipment (PPE) standards when entering designated areas.
  • Ability to manage competing priorities and respond to changing operational demands.

title: General Surgeon
description:
Woman’s Hospital is seeking a Board Certified/Board Eligible General Surgeon to join our established general surgery practice in Baton Rouge, Louisiana.

This opportunity offers a diverse general surgery practice combined with a highly collaborative surgical environment. In addition to managing an independent general surgery patient population, the surgeon will work closely with more than 60 OB/GYNs, GYN oncologists, breast surgeons, and other specialists practicing on the Woman’s campus.

A meaningful component of the practice involves combined surgical cases with OB/GYN and GYN oncology physicians, providing general surgery expertise during complex abdominal and pelvic procedures. This collaborative model creates a unique opportunity for a general surgeon who enjoys working alongside other surgical specialists and playing an important role in the multidisciplinary care of women.

The practice encompasses a broad range of procedures, including:

  • Robotic and minimally invasive surgery
  • Abdominal surgery
  • Hernia repair
  • Soft tissue procedures
  • Endoscopy
  • Thyroid surgery
  • Bariatric surgery
  • Combined and complex surgical cases with OB/GYN and GYN oncology physicians

All surgeries are performed at Woman’s Hospital, allowing physicians to practice primarily at a single hospital campus. The surgical program offers access to three da Vinci Xi robotic surgical systems.

The position is well suited for a surgeon who values a broad clinical practice, strong physician collaboration, an interest in women’s health, and a practice environment designed to support an excellent work/life balance.

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation
  • Productivity and quality bonus opportunities
  • Comprehensive benefits package
  • CME allowance

Qualifications:

  • MD or DO degree
  • Board Certified/Board Eligible in General Surgery
  • Robotic surgery capabilities

About Woman’s Hospital

Woman’s Hospital is a private, nonprofit specialty hospital located in Baton Rouge, Louisiana, dedicated to the care of women and infants. Woman’s has been recognized by Newsweek as one of the World’s Best Hospitals for three consecutive years.

title: SuccessFactors Solution Architect
description:
Role Overview

The SuccessFactors Solution Architect is responsible for designing and governing the overall integration architecture for SAP SuccessFactors and providing Employee Central (EC) functional support. This is a non-developer role with focus on architecture, process understanding, data modelling, and ensuring that SuccessFactors integrates seamlessly with the broader HR and enterprise landscape. The architect interacts with internal and external stakeholders and implementation partners, ensuring scalable, compliant, and future-proof solutions. This role also supports SuccessFactors Employee Central in the areas of business configuration, business rules, permissions, data loads and general support.


Key Responsibilities:

Integration Architecture

  • Support the end-to-end integration architecture for SuccessFactors and connected HR or enterprise systems.
  • Focus on integration concepts, data flows, and interface specifications based on business and technical requirements.
  • Ensure integration solutions follow best practices for security, performance, error handling, and monitoring.
  • Maintain integration documentation, standards, and architectural guidelines.

SuccessFactors Employee Central Expertise

  • Serve as the subject-matter expert for Employee Central, including:

- Core HR processes (hire, termination, job changes, position management)

- Business configuration (data models, workflows, business rules, picklists)

- MDF objects and effective-dated data structures

  • Provide functional guidance on EC configuration and its impact on integrations and downstream systems.
  • Support data load activities (e.g., mass changes, cutover loads) by defining templates, validation rules, and data quality checks.
  • Ensure data consistency, accuracy, and compliance across all integrated systems.


Stakeholder Collaboration

  • Work closely with HR, IT, external vendors, and implementation partners to translate business needs into scalable solution designs.
  • End-to-end responsibility from #Tech side during project phases such as blueprinting, testing, cutover, and hypercare.

Quality Assurance & Compliance

  • Ensure all integrations and EC configurations comply with data privacy, security, and audit requirements in close collaboration with the SAP Basis team
  • Review functional and technical specifications, test plans, and integration test results.
  • Maintain clear documentation of solution architecture, data flows, and key design decisions.


Required Qualifications:

  • Proven experience as a SuccessFactors Solution Architect, Integration Architect, or similar HRIS role.
  • Deep knowledge of SuccessFactors Employee Central, including processes, configuration, business rules, and data structures.
  • Strong understanding of the SuccessFactors data model and effective-dated data handling.
  • Experience with SAP Integration Suite / CPI or similar SAP middleware platforms.
  • Ability to design integration concepts without performing hands-on development.
  • Strong analytical, conceptual, and problem-solving skills.
  • Excellent communication skills for both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with additional SuccessFactors modules (e.g., Recruiting, Compensation).
  • Familiarity with HR data governance, GDPR, and security best practices.

Personal Attributes

  • Structured and strategic thinker with strong architectural discipline.
  • Able to translate complex technical topics into clear business language.
  • Collaborative, proactive, and comfortable driving cross-functional discussions.
  • Detail-oriented with a strong sense of ownership and accountability.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, or disability.

Technical Industrial Placement roles are available in London, Leatherhead, Chippenham, Reading, Bristol, Birmingham. As CGI is a consultancy, you may be required to work in different locations, so flexibility and a willingness to travel are key.

At CGI, you’ll be part of a culture that celebrates diversity, inclusion, and collaboration, where your perspective is valued and your ideas contribute to meaningful outcomes.

Your journey starts with a structured Early Careers Induction Programme, giving you the foundations to succeed, along with 24/7 e-learning and opportunities to gain professional certifications that build your expertise. You’ll also join our Student Kick-start Initiative, where you’ll collaborate with other Industrial Placements on creative projects that deliver impact beyond your day-to-day role.

CGI is an unconditionally inclusive workplace where you are respected, your voice is heard, and you can be yourself. We were recognised in the Sunday Times Best Places to Work List 2025 and named a UK ‘Best Employer’ by the Financial Times. We proudly hold a Gold Award in recognition of our support of the Armed Forces Corporate Covenant.

Benefits

Along with a competitive salary and a £500 joining bonus, you’ll enjoy benefits that support every stage of your journey. You’ll share in CGI’s success through our matched share scheme, have access to private healthcare, well-being programmes, and professional training, and build financial security with a competitive pension. Beyond the day job, you’ll connect with others through early careers networks, diversity groups, and social clubs that make your time at CGI both rewarding and enjoyable.

Required qualifications to be successful in this role:

We’re seeking ambitious students who are passionate about technology and eager to apply their skills to projects that make a real difference. You’ll bring a strong academic background in STEM, curiosity to explore new ideas, and flexibility to take on diverse projects across the UK.

  • Flexible to travel and work on projects across the UK.
  • Eligible for Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) clearance, with many roles requiring higher National Security Vetting (typically 5–10 years of continuous UK residency).

Technical skills we value include:

  • Programming Languages: Proficiency in one or more of C++, Java, Python, JavaScript, or C#.
  • Systems & Tools: Familiarity with Linux/Unix, version control systems (e.g., Git), and DevOps tools (e.g., Docker, Kubernetes).
  • Cloud Technologies: Exposure to platforms such as AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud.
  • Software Development Practices: Understanding of Agile and DevOps methodologies.

What you can expect from us:

Together, as owners, let’s turn meaningful insights into action.

Life at CGI is rooted in ownership, teamwork, respect and belonging. Here, you’ll reach your full potential because…

  • You are invited to be an owner from day 1 as we work together to bring our Dream to life. That’s why we call ourselves CGI Partners rather than employees. We benefit from our collective success and actively shape our company’s strategy and direction.

That same commitment to fairness extends to how we use technology. To support our recruitment team, AI tools may be used to help assess applications though they never replace human judgement. All hiring decisions remain entirely in the hands of our recruitment professionals.

Come join our team—one of the largest IT and business consulting services firms in the world.

  • Innovate alongside other industrial placements, taking part in early careers initiatives that go beyond your day-to-day role.

Every contribution you make will help deliver outcomes with lasting impact.

Locations

Business Industrial Placements are available in London, Reading, Birmingham, Manchester, Chippenham, Newcastle, Leeds, Leatherhead, Cardiff and Telford. As CGI is a consultancy, you may be required to work in different locations, so flexibility and a willingness to travel are key.

Why Join Us?

At CGI, you’ll be part of a culture that celebrates diversity, inclusion, and collaboration, where your perspective is valued and your ideas contribute to meaningful outcomes.

Your journey starts with a structured Early Careers Induction Programme, giving you the foundations to succeed, along with 24/7 e-learning and opportunities to gain professional certifications that build your expertise. You’ll also join our Student Kick-start Initiative, where you’ll collaborate with other Industrial Placements on creative projects that deliver impact beyond your day-to-day role.

CGI is an unconditionally inclusive workplace where you are respected, your voice is heard, and you can be yourself. We were recognised in the Sunday Times Best Places to Work List 2025 and named a UK ‘Best Employer’ by the Financial Times. We proudly hold a Gold Award in recognition of our support of the Armed Forces Corporate Covenant.

Benefits

Along with a competitive salary and a £500 joining bonus, you’ll enjoy benefits that support every stage of your journey. You’ll share in CGI’s success through our matched share scheme, have access to private healthcare, well-being programmes, and professional training, and build financial security with a competitive pension. Beyond the day job, you’ll connect with others through early careers networks, diversity groups, and social clubs that make your time at CGI both rewarding and enjoyable.

Required qualifications to be successful in this role:

We’re seeking ambitious candidates who are passionate about technology and eager to apply their skills to projects that make a real difference. Whatever your degree subject if you’re eager to learn, collaborate, and innovate, we want to hear from you

You should be on track to achieve:

  • A minimum 2:1 degree.

And have:

  • Passion for technology and innovation, with a problem-solving mindset.
  • Flexibility to travel and work on projects across the UK.
  • Eligibility for Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) clearance, with many roles requiring higher National Security Vetting (typically 5–10 years of continuous UK residency).

What you can expect from us:

Together, as owners, let’s turn meaningful insights into action.

Life at CGI is rooted in ownership, teamwork, respect and belonging. Here, you’ll reach your full potential because…

  • You are invited to be an owner from day 1 as we work together to bring our Dream to life. That’s why we call ourselves CGI Partners rather than employees. We benefit from our collective success and actively shape our company’s strategy and direction.
  • Your work creates value. You’ll develop innovative solutions and build relationships with teammates and clients while accessing global capabilities to scale your ideas, embrace new opportunities, and benefit from expansive industry and technology expertise.
  • You’ll shape your career by joining a company built to grow and last. You’ll be supported by leaders who care about your health and well-being and provide you with opportunities to deepen your skills and broaden your horizons.

That same commitment to fairness extends to how we use technology. To support our recruitment team, AI tools may be used to help assess applications though they never replace human judgement. All hiring decisions remain entirely in the hands of our recruitment professionals.

Come join our team—one of the largest IT and business consulting services firms in the world.

title: House Attendant
description:
At Moody, we believe that people are the most important ingredient of any business. It’s the people who ultimately determine what can be achieved. That’s why creating a culture based on trust, respect, and hard work is our top priority. We encourage our people to always reach higher, learn more, and live up to their potential, delivering our customers the best real estate solutions possible.

The Hampton Inn Houston I-10W Energy Corridor, managed by Moody National Management LP is currently looking for a House Attendant to join our team.

All associates are offered competitive pay, flexible scheduling opportunities, paid holidays and 401(k) with Employer Match. Full-time associates also enjoy paid time off and comprehensive benefits (including medical, dental, and vision).

Summary:

The House Attendant contributes toward high levels of guest satisfaction by achieving or exceeding the Company’s and Hotel Brand’s standards regarding the cleanliness and safety of all public areas and hallways and by providing professional, courteous, and prompt responses to guest inquiries and concerns.

Essential Functions:

• Clean all public areas in accordance with established procedures, including lobbies, hallways, elevators, service areas, stairwells, public restrooms, etc.; dust and polish furniture, fixtures, and window frames; vacuum carpeting, upholstery and drapery; clean and shine all glass and metal surfaces; clean offices as assigned.

• Patrol hallways and remove newspapers and service trays, remove trash and/or soiled linens. May strip guest rooms.

• Empty ash urns and pick up trash outside.

• Stock public restrooms with supplies and maintain assigned housekeeping cart with all necessary supplies.

• Respond to guest inquiries in a courteous manner; professionally resolve issues, promptly report lost/missing guest possessions; assist guests with luggage.

• Deliver, put away, or retrieve supply orders, cribs, roll-aways, and other room items.

• Promptly report any unsafe, broken, or missing furnishings, equipment, or fixtures to the Executive Housekeeper or Shift Supervisor.

• Assist Room Attendants as needed, especially with moving heaving items.

• Other duties as assigned by management.

Skills:

• Excellent time management skills and ability to multi-task and prioritize work.

• Strong customer service skills with a friendly and approachable demeanor.

• Ability to work independently as well as in a team environment.

Competencies:

· Action Oriented - Takes initiative. Enjoys working hard; is action oriented and full of energy for the things he/she sees as challenging; not fearful of acting with a minimum of planning; seizes more opportunities than others.

· Dependability - The extent to which the employee can be depended upon to be available for work, do it properly, and complete it on time with minimal supervision. The degree to which the employee is reliable, trustworthy, and persistent.

· Guest Relations - Communicates with guests in a professional and courteous manner. Puts their needs and wants first.

· Productivity - Manages workload, works efficiently, meets goals and objectives.

· Work Quality - Is dedicated to providing the highest quality products and services which meet the needs and requirements of internal and external customers; is committed to continuous improvement through empowerment and management by data; is willing to re-engineer processes from scratch; is open to suggestions and experimentation; facilitates a learning environment leading to the most efficient and effective work processes.

Education and Experience:

• High School education or equivalent work experience

· All positions must also complete any additional training required by manager or as assigned by the Brand or Moody.

Physical Demands & Work Environment:

· Thisjoboperates primarily indoors inahotelenvironment with occasional work outdoors.

· This role routinely uses standard housekeeping equipment.

· Exposure to and frequent use of commercial and household chemicals and cleaning solutions.

· Physical stamina to stand, walk, bend and lift for extended periods of time.

· Ability to occasionally lift products and supplies, up to 25 pounds.

title: Audio-Visual Project Manager
description:
Position Summary

Summary
This position is responsible for overseeing the successful completion of Systems Integrations projects from point-of-sale through completion and customer signoff.

Hybrid 75k-85k


Essential Functions
• Communicate efficiently and effectively between internal and external customers.
• Attend in-person project management and onsite project related meetings as necessary.
• Perform site visits on projects, as outlined in the PM manual, to verify Scope of services, equipment list accuracy, and site conditions/readiness to ensure proper installation and systems functionality.
• Develop project plan(s) in conjunction with the project team with the goal of delivering a successful installation within the goals of project timeline, budget, and other project success indicators.
• Facilitate customer Change Orders.
• Coordinate and/or verify installation logistics.
• Solve problems in a calm and orderly fashion as they arise to ensure quality and satisfaction. Follow up with the customer to make sure that the problem was solved appropriately.
• Aid Sales Engineers, Sales Representatives, Systems Integration Sales Support staff, other Project Managers, and Installers as required by each project.
• Provide Systems Installers all necessary information to complete equipment installation, including a handover meeting prior to the start of each installation.
• Review completed projects, making sure that the project is completed accurately and to the customer’s satisfaction.
• Answer or facilitate the answer to technical questions and concerns on current and completed System Integration installations.
• Provide Sales Support Staff and Management with up to date project billing information and project status updates.
• Verify and coordinate the creation and/or updating of all relevant project closeout documentation (as-builts, user-guides, signoffs, etc.) at project completion.
• Provide basic system training to customers as needed.
• Update project tracker and other internal measurable documents.
• Recognizing and channeling potential future sales opportunities.


Qualifications
• Excellent organizational skills.
• Exceptional time management and prioritization skills. Ability to effectively manage multiple projects and timelines simultaneously.
• Ability to communicate clearly in written and verbal form. Ability to write clear and timely emails.
• Ability to write reports, business correspondence, and procedure manuals. Ability to effectively present information and respond to questions from groups of managers, clients, customers and the general public.
• Ability to work under pressure with minimal supervision, while additionally demonstrating expertise in handling difficult or escalating situations in a calm and professional manner.
• Ability to calculate figures and amounts such as discounts, interest, commissions, proportions, percentages, area, circumference, and volume.
• Ability to define problems, collect data, establish facts, and draw valid conclusions.
• Ability to read and mark-up blueprints of installation projects. Ability to interpret an extensive variety of technical instructions in mathematical or diagram form and deal with several abstract and concrete variables.

Required Education & Experience
• Secondary diploma required, Bachelor’s degree is preferred.
• PMP Certification a plus. Candidates will be expected to pursue PMP certification as a condition of any employment offer for this position.
• 2 years’ related experience and/or training in audio/visual design or full life-cycle project management.
o An equivalent combination of education and experience totaling five years may be substituted for the degree.
• Knowledge of audio/video systems to include video (projection, production, switching and distribution methods)

title: Technical Graduate - Cyber Security 2027
description:

At CGI, we empower the next generation of innovators to shape the future of technology and security. As part of #GenerationCGI, you’ll join a community of graduates who are turning ambition into action and possibility into progress.

As a Technical Graduate specialising in Cyber Security, you’ll help protect the systems, services and information that organisations depend on. You could be supporting security operations, managing vulnerabilities, improving identity and access controls or helping clients understand and manage security risk.

You’ll be trusted with responsibility from the start, developing broad cyber security experience across technical security, cloud security, information security and governance, risk and compliance. Working alongside experienced CGI and client security teams, you’ll contribute to solutions that protect critical services and make a real difference.

Your future duties and responsibilities:

In this role, you’ll develop experience across different areas of cyber security while helping clients protect their technology, information and services. The work will vary by project, giving you opportunities to build both technical security expertise and an understanding of cyber risk and governance.

You may:

  • Support security operations: Help monitor systems, investigate security events and contribute to effective incident detection and response.
  • Manage vulnerabilities: Identify, assess and help address vulnerabilities across applications, infrastructure and cloud environments.
  • Protect identities and access: Support identity and access management processes that ensure users have appropriate and secure access to systems and information.
  • Understand security risk: Help assess risks, maintain security controls and support governance, risk and compliance activities.
  • Build security into delivery: Work with technical teams to apply DevSecOps practices and strengthen security throughout the development lifecycle.
  • Support secure platforms: Contribute to the development and operation of secure cloud, Linux and data-engineering environments.
  • Explore emerging threats: Develop your understanding of areas such as cloud security, data security and the secure use of artificial intelligence.
  • Innovate alongside other graduates: Take part in early careers initiatives that go beyond your day-to-day role.

Every contribution you make will help deliver outcomes with lasting impact.

Locations

Opportunities are available in Chippenham, London, Manchester and Reading.

As CGI is a consultancy, you may be required to work in different locations, so flexibility and a willingness to travel are key.

Required qualifications to be successful in this role:

We’re seeking ambitious graduates who are passionate about cyber security and motivated by the challenge of protecting technology, information and services. You’ll bring a strong technical foundation, an analytical mindset and the curiosity to keep learning as threats and security technologies continue to evolve.

You should have:

  • A minimum 2:2 degree in cyber security, computer science, information technology, computer engineering or another relevant STEM subject (some roles may require a 2:1).
  • A strong interest in cyber security, information security and technology risk.
  • Analytical thinking and a methodical approach to investigating problems.
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain security matters to different audiences.
  • Curiosity and a willingness to keep up to date with emerging threats, technologies and security practices.
  • Flexibility to travel and work on projects across the UK.
  • Eligibility for Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) clearance, with many roles requiring higher National Security Vetting. This typically requires 5–10 years of continuous UK residency.

Why Join Us?

At CGI, you’ll be part of a culture that celebrates diversity, inclusion and collaboration, where your perspective is valued and your ideas contribute to meaningful outcomes.

Your journey starts with a structured Early Careers Induction Programme, giving you the foundations to succeed, along with 24/7 e-learning and opportunities to gain professional certifications that build your expertise. You’ll also join our Student Kick-start Initiative, where you’ll collaborate with other graduates on creative projects that deliver impact beyond your day-to-day role.

CGI is an unconditionally inclusive workplace where you are respected, your voice is heard and you can be yourself. We were recognised in the Sunday Times Best Places to Work List 2025 and named a UK ‘Best Employer’ by the Financial Times. We proudly hold a Gold Award in recognition of our support of the Armed Forces Corporate Covenant.

Benefits

Along with a competitive salary and a £1,000 joining bonus, you’ll enjoy benefits that support every stage of your journey. You’ll share in CGI’s success through our matched share scheme, have access to private healthcare, well-being programmes and professional training, and build financial security with a competitive pension. Beyond the day job, you’ll connect with others through graduate networks, diversity groups and social clubs that make your time at CGI both rewarding and enjoyable.

What you can expect from us:

Together, as owners, let’s turn meaningful insights into action.

Life at CGI is rooted in ownership, teamwork, respect and belonging. Here, you’ll reach your full potential because…

You are invited to be an owner from day 1 as we work together to bring our Dream to life. That’s why we call ourselves CGI Partners rather than employees. We benefit from our collective success and actively shape our company’s strategy and direction.

Your work creates value. You’ll develop innovative solutions and build relationships with teammates and clients while accessing global capabilities to scale your ideas, embrace new opportunities, and benefit from expansive industry and technology expertise.

You’ll shape your career by joining a company built to grow and last. You’ll be supported by leaders who care about your health and well-being and provide you with opportunities to deepen your skills and broaden your horizons.

That same commitment to fairness extends to how we use technology. To support our recruitment team, AI tools may be used to help assess applications though they never replace human judgement. All hiring decisions remain entirely in the hands of our recruitment professionals.

Come join our team—one of the largest IT and business consulting services firms in the world.

title: Counselor (BIPS)
description:
PHMC serves as both a direct service provider to individuals, families, and communities across the region and an intermediary agent—managing large-scale contracts, government and philanthropic partnerships, and multidisciplinary initiatives that require operational sophistication, strategic leadership, and deep mission alignment.

Primary Location: 4601 Market St., Philadelphia, PA 19139.

Work Schedule: Monday to Friday from 10:00 a.m.–6:30 p.m

FTE: Full-Time

Job Overview:

The Bridge Intensive Prevention Services (BIPS), an after-school program serving at-risk youth ages 10–19 and their families in West Philadelphia, seeks a master’s-trained Counselor skilled in providing trauma-informed support to youth facing challenges at home, in school, and in the community. Reporting to the BIPS Program Director, the Counselor provides coordinated care guided by each youth’s treatment plan, conducts behavioral health screenings, provides regular individual counseling, facilitates group sessions, and connects youth and families with additional services, including individual and family therapy, as needed.

Responsibilities:

  • Maintain an approximate caseload of 17 youth and their families, providing weekly family-focused counseling and case coordination.
  • Collaborate with the Case Manager to deliver coordinated, family-centered treatment on-site and in participants’ homes.
  • Provide trauma-informed support to youth facing challenges at home, in school, and in the community.
  • Assist with intake and assessment using the Bridge biopsychosocial assessment form.
  • Conduct behavioral health screenings at intake and as additional concerns emerge.
  • Develop individualized, comprehensive treatment plans informed by psychological evaluations and other assessments.
  • Participate in service plan meetings with the Case Manager, youth, and families to establish treatment goals and discharge criteria, incorporating discharge planning from admission.
  • Build and maintain relationships with community organizations throughout Philadelphia to connect youth and families with appropriate resources.
  • Facilitate psychoeducational, life skills, and other structured educational groups for BIPS youth.
  • Coordinate with behavioral health providers and other professionals involved in each youth’s and family’s care.
  • Refer youth and families to additional treatment and support services as needed.
  • Attend required case consultations, staff meetings, and trainings.
  • Maintain accurate, timely records of contacts, services, and progress toward treatment goals in accordance with Department of Human Services (DHS) documentation requirements.
  • Enter progress notes and maintain current case records in the CBPS database.
  • Perform additional administrative duties assigned by the Program Director to support program operations and growth.

Work Habits:

  • Demonstrates strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
  • Maintains confidentiality and adheres to ethical standards.
  • Works independently while also collaborating effectively with team members.
  • Practices cultural humility and fosters an inclusive, supportive environment.
  • Exhibits empathy, patience, and a nonjudgmental approach to client interactions.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

  • Knowledge of and experience supporting at-risk youth ages 10–19, including those affected by substance use, trauma, and mental health challenges.
  • Competence in individual, group, and family therapy, with an emphasis on strengths-based practices and empowerment.
  • Ability to apply trauma-informed therapeutic approaches to support youth facing challenges at home, in school, and in the community.
  • Knowledge of adolescent development, family systems, mental health disorders, and substance use.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills.
  • Ability to incorporate strengths-based, recovery-oriented principles into care.
  • Cultural responsiveness and sensitivity to racial, cultural, and socioeconomic differences, with the ability to adapt interventions to meet diverse needs.
  • Knowledge of Philadelphia’s social service system and community resources for youth and families.
