title: Principal Cost & Pricing Analyst
description:
Principal Cost & Pricing Analyst

Location: Monroe, NC

Department: Finance

Reports To: Senior Director of Finance

Position Summary

The Principal Cost & Pricing Analyst serves as a strategic partner to Finance, Program Management, Engineering, Supply Chain, and Operations in developing and analyzing pricing strategies for complex U.S. Navy programs. This role is responsible for leading proposal pricing, cost estimating, government compliance, and profitability analysis for engineered-to-order pump manufacturing operations.

The successful candidate will possess deep expertise in FAR, DFARS, Cost Accounting Standards (CAS), Truthful Cost or Pricing Data (formerly TINA), and government contract pricing requirements. The position plays a critical role in securing profitable business while ensuring compliance with all government regulations and company policies.

KEY RESPONSABILITIES

Government Contract Pricing

  • Lead development of certified cost or pricing data packages and support Truthful Cost or Pricing Data compliance.
  • Support Defense Contract Audit Agency (DCAA) and Defense Contract Management Agency (DCMA) audits and reviews.
  • Develop, maintain, and support Forward Pricing Rate Proposals (FPRPs), including coordination with Finance, Operations, DCAA, and DCMA to establish compliant labor, overhead, G&A, and material burden rates used in government contract proposals.

Cost Analysis & Financial Modeling

  • Develop and maintain detailed pricing, estimating, and financial models.
  • Analyze manufacturing costs, labor standards, material pricing trends, overhead absorption, and production efficiency.
  • Perform variance analysis comparing estimated versus actual program costs.
  • Identify cost reduction initiatives and continuous improvement opportunities.

Cost Accounting

  • Partner with Operations and Finance to maintain accurate labor routings, bills of material, and standard costs.
  • Support annual standard cost updates and inventory valuation reviews.
  • Provide financial guidance on make-versus-buy decisions and sourcing strategies.
  • Assist in the development of strategic planning, annual operating plans, and forecast updates.
  • Ensure that all journal entries related to allocations are posted as part of monthly close and are accurate and auditable.

Compliance & Governance

  • Ensure estimating practices comply with applicable government regulations, company procedures, and internal controls.
  • Support contractor business system compliance requirements.
  • Maintain documentation supporting cost estimates and rate decisions.
  • Assist with internal and external audits relating to pricing, estimating, and government contracts.
  • Monitor regulatory changes affecting government contracting and proposal pricing activities.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS & ABILITIES

  • Strong understanding of:
    • Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR)
    • Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS)
    • Cost Accounting Standards (CAS)
    • Truthful Cost or Pricing Data requirements
    • Government proposal and contract compliance
  • Advanced financial modeling and analytical skills.
  • Strong understanding of manufacturing cost structures and standard costing methodologies.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, including complex formulas, Power Query, and financial modeling.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to translate complex financial information into executive-level recommendations.

EDUCATION & EXPERIENCE

  • Bachelor's degree in Accounting or Finance.
  • Master's degree or MBA preferred.
  • Minimum 8–12 years of progressive experience in cost estimating, pricing, government contracts, or manufacturing finance.
  • Experience supporting U.S. Government, DoD, Navy, defense, aerospace, industrial equipment, or engineered manufacturing environments.
  • Demonstrated experience with complex forward pricing rate development and project costing.
  • Experience supporting DCAA and DCMA audits preferred.

title: Case Manager (BIPS)
description:
PHMC serves as both a direct service provider to individuals, families, and communities across the region and an intermediary agent—managing large-scale contracts, government and philanthropic partnerships, and multidisciplinary initiatives that require operational sophistication, strategic leadership, and deep mission alignment.

Primary Location: 4601 Market St., Philadelphia, PA 19139.

Work Schedule: Monday to Friday from10:00 a.m.–6:30 p.m.

FTE: Full-Time

Job Overview:

The Bridge Intensive Prevention Services (BIPS), an after-school program serving at-risk youth ages 10–19 and their families in West Philadelphia, seeks a Case Manager to provide person-centered, strengths-based, and trauma-informed support. Reporting to the BIPS Program Director, the Case Manager coordinates intake appointments, conducts home visits, obtains school records, connects families with services, and advocates for youth and families at court hearings. The role also facilitates life skills groups, supports on-site activities, and maintains administrative systems aligned with program and payer requirements. Candidates must hold at least a bachelor’s degree and have experience providing trauma-informed care to at-risk youth and their families.

Responsibilities:

  • Maintain an approximate caseload of 17 adolescents and their families, providing weekly family-focused case management and service coordination, including home-based support.
  • Collaborate with the Therapist/Counselor to provide coordinated, trauma-informed services to youth ages 10–19 and their families across program, school, community, and home settings.
  • Assist with scheduling intake appointments.
  • Conduct at least two home visits per month for each case.
  • Obtain and review school records, including grades and attendance, at least monthly.
  • Accompany youth and families to court hearings and advocate for their needs and access to appropriate services.
  • Submit monthly case updates to the Department of Human Services (DHS), District Attorney’s Office, and Philadelphia Police Department, as needed.
  • Facilitate life skills groups, support groups, workshops, and educational sessions as needed.
  • Educate youth and families on harm reduction strategies, coping skills, and wellness practices.
  • Participate in service plan meetings with youth and their families.
  • Build and maintain relationships with community organizations throughout Philadelphia to connect youth and families with appropriate resources.
  • Incorporate discharge planning into treatment planning and case management beginning at admission.
  • Attend required case consultations, staff meetings, and trainings.
  • Maintain accurate, timely case records and enter progress notes in the CBPS database.
  • Perform additional administrative duties assigned by the Program Director to support program operations and growth.

Work Habits:

  • Demonstrates strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
  • Maintains confidentiality and adheres to ethical standards.
  • Works independently while also collaborating effectively with team members.
  • Practices cultural humility and fosters an inclusive, supportive environment.
  • Exhibits empathy, patience, and a nonjudgmental approach to client interactions.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

  • Knowledge, understanding, and experience working with at-risk youth, substance abuse, trauma, and/or mental illness.
  • Strong knowledge of community resources relevant to this population.
  • Strong oral and written communication skills .
  • Sensitivity to racial, cultural, and economic differences and willingness to adopt interventions that work for different groups.
  • Understanding of a strengths-based, recovery-oriented approach and a willingness to adopt this approach.
  • Knowledge of high-risk youth, family systems, mental health disorders, and substance abuse.

Work Environment and Location:

  • Primary Location: 4601 Market St., Philadelphia, PA 19139.
  • Work Schedule: Monday to Friday from10:00 a.m.–6:30 p.m., supporting an after-school program serving youth.
  • Travel Requirements: Travel to homes and schools is required. Candidates must have a valid Pennsylvania driver’s license, current auto insurance, access to a vehicle, and a good driving record.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in social work, psychology, counseling, or a related human services field required.
  • At least two years of case management experience required.
  • Experience working with diverse populations, including at-risk youth and their families.
  • Experience applying trauma-informed care principles in direct services.

PHMC is an Equal Opportunity and E-Verify Employer.

title: Global Transportation Manager (m/f/d)
description:
Are you ready to unleash your potential? At the Straumann Group, we're on an exciting journey of growth, innovation, and impact – driven by our mission to improve oral health and transform millions of lives worldwide.

United by a shared goal, we give our best every day and cultivate a performance-oriented, player-learner culture that fosters collaboration, curiosity, and ambition. Here, you have the opportunity to actively shape your career and further develop your skills, passion, and willingness to learn. Together, we not only create more beautiful smiles but also unlock the potential of people – including our own.

As a Global Transportation Manager (m/f/d), you will take the lead in building and shaping our newly established global transportation function. Based in Madrid, you will define the global transportation strategy and operating model, establish our Logistics Control Tower, and drive greater visibility, resilience, and cost efficiency across our international transportation network. Working closely with regional supply chain teams and key functions across the organization, you will play a pivotal role in transforming and digitalizing transportation at Straumann Group while building scalable capabilities that support our continued growth.

Your responsibilities:

Transportation Strategy & Governance

  • Build and lead the new global transportation function, taking ownership of the transportation strategy, governance, standards, and operating principles
  • Define the target operating model and develop transportation roadmaps aligned with our end-to-end Supply Chain and GLD strategy
  • Establish clear governance and KPI review routines while monitoring freight cost development, service quality, and relevant business priorities
  • Act as the key subject matter expert for intercompany/primary transportation, network performance, service resilience, and cost transparency

Logistics Control Tower

  • Lead the design, build, and stabilization of the Logistics Control Tower (LCT), covering organizational design, workflows, service catalogue, escalation model, and operating routines
  • Establish standards for milestone tracking and visibility, as well as playbooks and case management processes for effective end-to-end shipment exception management
  • Partner with IT, SAP/TMS, Data, and Analytics teams to implement the required digital capabilities, interfaces, dashboards, and reporting solutions
  • Build capabilities, standardized ways of working, and training programs to enable sustainable adoption across the LCT and regional teams

Transportation Partners, Performance & Cost

  • Define transportation service models, routing principles, carrier segmentation, preferred provider setups, backup solutions, and requirements for transportation tenders
  • Manage the performance of carriers and logistics service providers through scorecards, business reviews, escalations, corrective actions, and continuous improvement initiatives
  • Take ownership of freight management principles, cost-to-serve, analytics standards, and transportation KPI performance across the global network
  • Develop carrier risk management and business continuity strategies and ensure resilient transportation structures, including contingency solutions for specific lanes and regulated goods flows
  • Support transportation procurement activities in close collaboration with Procurement and Finance

Transformation, Digitalization & Continuous Improvement

  • Drive transportation network optimization, process standardization, automation, and the TMS and LCT roadmap while improving reporting automation and data quality
  • Identify and implement initiatives to improve service quality, lead times, carrier reliability, visibility, and freight cost performance
  • Support broader logistics transformation programs, including S/4HANA, transportation management capabilities, and the evolution of the operating model
  • Translate global and regional business requirements into scalable transportation solutions that deliver measurable value
  • Support Straumann Group’s sustainability and Net Zero ambitions through relevant transportation initiatives

Regional Collaboration & Leadership

  • Support regional Supply Chain teams through standards, visibility, escalation routines, and improvement forums, while local import/export execution and last-mile management remain within the regions
  • Lead global and regional transportation forums and coordinate major transportation incidents, capacity constraints, delayed shipment escalations, and other time-critical situations
  • Define strategic guardrails for intra-regional intercompany transportation and ensure effective alignment between global design and regional execution
  • Recruit, lead, coach, and develop the Logistics Control Tower team, establishing clear objectives and accountabilities while building long-term capabilities and succession plans
  • Build effective partnerships across regions, functions, and external partners, and represent the transportation function in discussions with senior stakeholders

Your profile:

  • A Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Supply Chain, Logistics, Business Administration, Engineering, or a related field
  • Extensive experience in transportation, logistics, distribution, or supply chain roles with increasing leadership responsibility; as a guide, the original role profile indicates more than 10 years of relevant experience
  • Demonstrated experience leading transportation organizations in a regional or global environment
  • Strong experience managing international transportation networks, logistics service providers, and carrier performance, as well as transportation spend and service levels across multiple geographies
  • Experience leading transportation transformation, digitalization, and automation initiatives
  • Hands-on knowledge of Transportation Management Systems (TMS), SAP, analytics and reporting tools, and digital transportation solutions
  • Strong project/program management, stakeholder management, and change management skills
  • Excellent written and spoken English

What makes you a great fit:

  • You combine strategic thinking with a strong focus on execution and enjoy building new structures, capabilities, and ways of working
  • You bring clarity to complex, international matrix environments and are effective at bringing different stakeholders together around shared objectives
  • You can translate complex business and operational requirements into clear actions and measurable outcomes
  • You take an analytical and data-driven approach while maintaining a strong understanding of business, customer, and service requirements
  • You set clear priorities in dynamic operational environments and approach change and ambiguity in a structured and pragmatic way
  • You take ownership of outcomes, communicate transparently, and collaborate effectively across functions, regions, and external partners
  • You bring curiosity and a continuous improvement mindset, with a willingness to challenge and evolve existing ways of working
  • You are motivated by the opportunity to shape and further develop Straumann Group’s global transportation organization

title: Process Technician 2 (TEMP-REQ-2026-0184)
description:
Kyocera has a temp-to-hire position for a Process Technician 2 at our San Diego, CA facility.

Candidates selected for hire will be hired through one of Kyocera’s approved staffing partners.

This position may lead to a direct hire offer with Kyocera International, Inc.

Pay is $21.00 per hour

With nearly 80,000 employees globally, Kyocera is a leading manufacturer of high-tech ceramics in various industries, including aerospace, automotive, medical applications, and semiconductor processing. Our innovative materials are found in everything from smartphones to space shuttles!


Exempt: No
Safety Sensitive: Yes

GENERAL DESCRIPTION OF POSITION

A Process Technician 2 performs a variety of functions associated with manufacturing operations, including working with engineers and operators in set-up and calibration tasks, as well as performing rework and quality testing related to the production of parts, components, subassemblies and final product. Uses programs to collect and evaluate operating data to conduct in-line adjustments to parts, instruments or equipment. Updates and may assist in developing methods and procedures to control or modify the manufacturing process.

REQUIREMENTS

High school diploma or GED required.
2+ years of technician experience required in a manufacturing/production environment.
Ability to read, write and comprehend instructions in English.
Ability to add, subtract, multiply, divide all units of measure including common and decimal fractions.
Ability to use a microscope, depending on the specific function.
Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, color vision and depth perception.
20/20 corrected vision may be required - varies by division
Willingness to wear PPE (examples: goggle, gloves, apron, finger cot, masks, and/or cleanroom apparel.
Ability to grab small parts or hand tools with hands.
Eligible to work in an ITAR environment


ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  1. Monitors and documents the operation of machines in a production environment. Maintains flow of production parts; reports inconsistencies, and suggests improvements in the production process.
  2. Troubleshoots complex or troublesome equipment, may work with facilities team or outside vendor or repair or modification.
  3. May run engineering tests prescribed by engineer. Perform periodic calibration checks.
  4. May recommend process improvements based on test and process results and experience. Troubleshoot machine set up.
  5. Visually inspects parts at required steps in the process with attention to detail, ensuring the parts are within specified tolerances. May disposition of reject parts and train operators and inspectors to improve efficiency.
  6. Maintains and orders/tracks tools according to safety and vendor recommendations. Will use measuring devices, such as micrometers, calipers, CMM and other optical tools.
  7. Participates in the 5S program.
  8. Knowledgeable of Excel and able to accurately enter data into spreadsheets and create graphs. Experience in basic CNC and CMM is helpful.
  9. Complies with applicable requirements of Kyocera International, Inc. policy, ISO 9000, ISO 14001 requirements, ITAR regulations.
  10. May setup/program production or test machinery.
  11. Reads specifications and mechanical drawings.
  12. May assign and check work of lower-level technicians and operators. Perform the duties or an operator or material handler on occasion as needed.

Perform any other related duties as required or assigned.

QUALIFICATIONS
To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty mentioned satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required.


PHYSICAL ACTIVITIES
The following physical activities described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions and expectations.

While performing the functions of this job, the employee is continuously required to talk or hear; regularly required to stand, use hands to finger, handle, turn, twist, or feel; frequently required to walk, sit; and occasionally required to reach with hands and arms, stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl.

The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 50 pounds, frequently lift and/or move up to 25 pounds, regularly lift and/or move up to 10 pounds.

ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITIONS
The following work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

While performing the functions of this job, the employee is occasionally exposed to work near moving mechanical parts, work in high, precarious places, fumes or airborne particles.

The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate.

Position Title: Operator

Our Core Values: Guided by Safety. Focused on Communities. Powered by Care.

Essential Functions:

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential functions.

The Operators primary duty is to assist line crew or network crew members by working on the ground, handing tools and heavy materials to workers. To dig holes and pad ditches, and to perform other similar work in connection with the construction and maintenance of overhead and underground power lines. This position is the highest of a multi-step progression and is expected to know all aspects of Operator duties for the Company. Lower steps in this classification are expected to progress into all aspects of these duties. Operators are never permitted to work on energized conductors without direct/immediate supervision at all times. An Operator is also responsible for his/her own safety at all times and is expected to learn and follow all company guidelines and safety procedures. It is the responsibility of the operator to report any and all accidents to the foreman immediately and ensure the safety of his fellow crew members by following all safety guidelines.

Roles and Responsibilities:

  • Passes tools to line crew or network crew members by acting as a general helper on the ground. Handles cables, conduit and other materials as directed. Glues conduits together. Assists in setting transformers.

  • Clears undergrowth from right-of-way by using hand tools or saws. Piles debris to clear path. Performs general clean-up of job sites following completion of work.
  • Positions reels of electric cable beside trenches and lays heavy residential underground distribution (URD) cables in ditches and pads by shoveling fine sand around cable.
  • Assists network crew top man with lowering and raising molten metals and other heavy materials to the cable splicer working below in the vault.
  • Operates roto hammer to access vaults.
  • Notifies customers of impending disruption of service while lines are under repair.

title: Business Graduate - Project Manager - January 2027

At CGI, we empower the next generation of innovators to shape the future of technology and security. As part of #GenerationCGI, you’ll join a community of graduates who are turning ambition into action and possibility into progress.

This opportunity is designed for graduates who have completed their studies and are ready to start their CGI journey in January 2027. If you’re still at university, we’d love you to explore our other graduate opportunities and find the intake that best matches your graduation date.

As a Project Management - Business Graduate, you’ll help turn plans into successful outcomes. You’ll support the delivery of complex projects, coordinate activities and work with colleagues and clients to keep delivery on track.

You’ll be trusted with responsibility from day one, helping teams manage priorities, risks, dependencies and stakeholder expectations. Your organisation, communication and problem-solving skills will contribute to projects that make a real difference.

  • Support project planning: Help develop delivery plans, schedules, milestones and success measures.

  • Manage risks and governance: Identify and record risks and issues, support project reporting and help maintain effective governance.

  • Support continuous improvement: Use evidence, feedback and lessons learned to help improve how projects are delivered.
  • Innovate alongside other graduates: Take part in early careers initiatives that go beyond your day-to-day role.

Every contribution you make will help deliver outcomes with lasting impact.

Locations

This opportunity is available in Bristol, London and Leatherhead.

As CGI is a consultancy, you may be required to work in different locations, so flexibility and a willingness to travel are key.

Required qualifications to be successful in this role:

We’re looking for organised and motivated graduates who are ready to begin their careers in project management. You’ll bring strong communication and problem-solving skills, an interest in delivering successful projects and the confidence to work collaboratively with colleagues and clients. This opportunity is intended for candidates who have already completed their degree and are available to start in January 2027. If you’re still studying, please explore our other graduate opportunities with later start dates.

You should have:

  • A minimum 2:2 degree in any subject.
  • Strong organisation and time-management skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities.
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills.
  • A collaborative approach and the confidence to build positive working relationships.
  • Strong attention to detail and a proactive, problem-solving mindset.
  • An interest in project management, project delivery and using technology to create meaningful outcomes.
  • Flexibility to travel and work with teams and clients when required.
  • Eligibility for Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) clearance, with some projects requiring higher levels of National Security Vetting.

It would be useful, but not essential, to have:

  • An understanding of project management approaches such as Agile or Waterfall.
  • Experience of coordinating activities, deadlines or stakeholders through university, employment, volunteering or extracurricular activities.
  • Familiarity with tools such as Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, Project, Jira or similar project-planning software.

Previous professional project management experience is not required—we’re interested in your potential, transferable skills and enthusiasm to learn.

At CGI, you’ll be part of a culture that celebrates diversity, inclusion and collaboration, where your perspective is valued and your ideas contribute to meaningful outcomes.

Your journey starts with a structured Early Careers Induction Programme, giving you the foundations to succeed, along with 24/7 e-learning and opportunities to gain professional certifications that build your expertise. You’ll also join our Student Kick-start Initiative, where you’ll collaborate with other graduates on creative projects that deliver impact beyond your day-to-day role.

We were recognised in the Sunday Times Best Places to Work List 2025 and named a UK ‘Best Employer’ by the Financial Times. We proudly hold a Gold Award in recognition of our support of the Armed Forces Corporate Covenant.

Along with a competitive salary and a £1,000 joining bonus, you’ll enjoy benefits that support every stage of your journey. You’ll share in CGI’s success through our matched share scheme, have access to private healthcare, well-being programmes and professional training, and build financial security with a competitive pension. Beyond the day job, you’ll connect with others through graduate networks, diversity groups and social clubs that make your time at CGI both rewarding and enjoyable.

What you can expect from us:

Together, as owners, let’s turn meaningful insights into action.

Life at CGI is rooted in ownership, teamwork, respect and belonging. Here, you’ll reach your full potential because…

You are invited to be an owner from day 1 as we work together to bring our Dream to life. That’s why we call ourselves CGI Partners rather than employees. We benefit from our collective success and actively shape our company’s strategy and direction.

Your work creates value. You’ll develop innovative solutions and build relationships with teammates and clients while accessing global capabilities to scale your ideas, embrace new opportunities, and benefit from expansive industry and technology expertise.

You’ll shape your career by joining a company built to grow and last. You’ll be supported by leaders who care about your health and well-being and provide you with opportunities to deepen your skills and broaden your horizons.

title: Senior Data Platform / Data Engineer
description:
Straumann Group
At Straumann Group we’re on an exciting journey of growth, innovation, and impact - driven by our mission to improve oral health and transform millions of lives worldwide. United by purpose, we bring our best selves to work every day, embracing a high-performance, player-learner culture that inspires collaboration, curiosity, and ambition. Here, you’ll have the opportunity to take charge of your own career, harnessing your skills, passion, and enthusiasm for learning to continually grow and progress. Together, we’re not just shaping brighter smiles, we’re unlocking the potential of people everywhere, including our own.

About the role
We are looking for a Senior Data Platform / Data Engineer to join our ML Platform team and help build and scale the data infrastructure that powers our AI products in dentistry. Our platform supports the full AI development lifecycle, from raw data ingestion and annotation workflows to dataset versioning and model training pipelines. You will work closely with Machine Learning Researchers (MLRs), MLOps engineers, and product teams to ensure our data infrastructure is reliable, scalable, and easy to use.
A key focus of the role is improving our Data Lakehouse (DLH) and dataset management workflows, including dataset versioning (DVC) and improving how data is prepared, extracted, and consumed across research and production systems.

What you will work on:
You will play a key role in shaping the next generation of our data platform.
Typical responsibilities include:
Data platform ownership

  • Design and evolve the Data Lakehouse (DLH) architecture used across our ML teams.
  • Improve the reliability and structure of data ingestion, extraction, and transformation pipelines.
  • Ensure datasets used for training and evaluation are consistent, reproducible, and well documented.

Dataset lifecycle management

  • Improve workflows for dataset versioning and reproducibility using tools such as DVC.
  • Design solutions for managing multiple versions of datasets and annotations across experiments and models.
  • Improve the ability for researchers to retrieve the correct dataset versions reliably.

Data pipelines and infrastructure

  • Build and maintain scalable data pipelines in Python.
  • Improve metadata management, dataset validation, and data quality monitoring.
  • Optimize data workflows across AWS-based infrastructure.

Collaboration with ML teams

  • Work closely with ML researchers and ML engineers to understand their data needs.
  • Support research workflows with reliable and efficient data access patterns.
  • Help translate research requirements into robust platform capabilities.

Data governance and quality

  • Implement practices for data quality, reproducibility, and traceability across the ML lifecycle.
  • Ensure our data infrastructure meets the requirements of regulated AI development.

What we’re looking for:
Must have:

  • Strong Python engineering skills
  • Experience building data pipelines or data platforms
  • Experience working with AWS
  • Experience working with large datasets used in ML workflows
  • Strong software engineering practices (testing, CI/CD, documentation)
  • Experience collaborating with ML teams or working in AI environments

Nice to have:
• Experience with dataset versioning tools such as DVC
• Experience with Kubernetes
• Experience with data lakehouse architectures
• Experience working with annotation pipelines or ML training datasets
• Experience with PostgreSQL, Metabase, or similar data tooling
• Experience working in regulated environments (medical / healthcare AI)

Our stack

  • AWS
  • Python
  • Kubernetes
  • PostgreSQL
  • Metabase
  • DVC for dataset versioning
  • Internal Data Lakehouse infrastructure

description:

title: Sr. Solutions Architect, ServiceNow (CMDB)
description:

The Role
As a Sr. Solutions Architect, CMDB at Presidio, you will lead the design, implementation, optimization, governance, and remediation of ServiceNow CMDB and CSDM solutions for enterprise clients. You will serve as a strategic advisor for customers, helping them establish scalable data models, improve CMDB data quality, mature CSDM adoption, and connect configuration data to measurable business outcomes. This position requires deep hands-on ServiceNow CMDB expertise, strong command of CSDM and ServiceNow Data Foundations, and a proven ability to lead workshops, guide technical teams, and mentor less experienced architects.

Travel Requirements:

This is a remote role within the Continental United States and will require 10% travel.

Responsibilities include:

Leadership & Strategy:

  • Lead and mentor teams of Associate, Staff, and Senior Solution Architects to deliver world-class CMDB and CSDM solutions.
  • Serve as a senior ServiceNow CMDB and CSDM subject matter expert, shaping architecture, governance, remediation strategy, and delivery quality across customer engagements.
  • Develop and maintain repeatable methodologies, accelerators, and service offerings for CMDB implementation, CMDB remediation, CSDM adoption, and data governance.
  • Support and influence the architectural direction of products, projects, and the CMDB Center of Excellence, with a focus on measurable business outcomes and scalable delivery.
  • Review and refine statements of work, estimates, and solution approaches to ensure alignment with customer objectives and value-based deliverables.

Customer Engagement:

  • Lead CMDB, CSDM, and ServiceNow Data Foundations workshops with BPC support, ensuring technical, process, governance, and business requirements are addressed.
  • Guide customers through CMDB maturity assessment, CSDM roadmap development, service awareness, data ownership, and adoption of sustainable governance practices.
  • Translate complex customer requirements into actionable architecture, technical designs, data models, user stories, and implementation plans.
  • Field complex and difficult questions related to CMDB health, data quality, class models, CI relationships, duplicate remediation, IRE behavior, and authoritative data sources.
  • Lead executive and practitioner-level demos, design reviews, readouts, and roadmap presentations that connect CMDB and CSDM capabilities to customer outcomes.

Technical Leadership:

  • Architect scalable ServiceNow CMDB solutions aligned to CSDM, customer-specific operating models, and ServiceNow best practices.
  • Design CMDB data models, CI class structures, relationship models, service models, data ownership processes, and governance controls.
  • Define integration, identification, reconciliation, normalization, and remediation approaches that improve data quality and reduce duplicate or conflicting CI data.
  • Drive CMDB integration with key business processes including Change, Incident, Problem, Asset, ITOM, ITAM, Service Mapping, AIOps, reporting, and operational risk management.
  • Develop measurable and repeatable processes for CMDB data remediation, data certification, health reporting, exception management, and continuous improvement.
  • Oversee technical reviews, peer reviews, unit testing, UAT support, and solution quality controls to ensure deliverables meet company standards.

Mentorship & Collaboration:

  • Actively mentor Associate and Staff Solution Architects, providing practical guidance on CMDB architecture, CSDM strategy, technical design, and customer communication.
  • Collaborate with BPCs, PMs, technical consultants, sales, and cross-functional delivery teams to ensure smooth implementation of architectural solutions.
  • Provide leadership during project escalations, risk reviews, and technical decision-making where CMDB, CSDM, or data governance issues may impact delivery success.
  • Participate in technical interviews for potential new hires, helping ensure the team continues to grow with top CMDB and CSDM talent.

Certifications & Continuous Learning:

  • Maintain a high level of technical proficiency, achieving and maintaining certifications in ServiceNow CMDB, CSDM, Data Foundations, and other relevant platform areas.
  • Stay current on ServiceNow releases, CSDM updates, CMDB Health capabilities, Discovery, Service Graph Connector patterns, ITOM/ITAM dependencies, and industry best practices.

Required Skills and Professional Experience:

  • Minimum of 5-8 year's proven experience leading ServiceNow CMDB architecture, implementation, optimization, and remediation for enterprise-scale customers.
  • Deep hands-on experience with ServiceNow CSDM, ServiceNow Data Foundations, CMDB Health, CI class hierarchy, relationship modeling, and service-oriented data design.
  • Strong understanding of IRE concepts, identification rules, reconciliation strategies, duplicate remediation, data normalization, and authoritative source strategy.
  • Experience integrating CMDB data with ITSM, ITAM, ITOM, Change, Incident, Problem, Asset, Service Mapping, reporting, and operational processes.
  • Track record of successfully guiding customers through complex technical questions, data quality challenges, CSDM adoption, and CMDB maturity improvements.
  • Experience leading workshops, technical design sessions, executive readouts, peer reviews, unit testing, and customer presentations.
  • Expertise in ServiceNow CMDB, CSDM, Data Foundations, CMDB Health, Discovery concepts, data governance, and platform architecture.
  • Ability to develop and maintain complex technical designs, data models, integration strategies, testing approaches, and remediation plans.
  • Strong understanding of ServiceNow best practices, delivery methodologies, agile execution, and enterprise architecture principles.
  • Excellent problem-solving, leadership, facilitation, and communication skills, including the ability to simplify complex CMDB and CSDM concepts for technical and business audiences.
  • Ability to mentor and guide junior team members in both technical and professional growth.

Required Certifications:

  • ServiceNow Certified System Administrator required or equivalent hands-on platform expertise.
  • ServiceNow Certified Implementation Specialist - Data Foundations (CMDB and CSDM) required or strongly preferred.
  • At least two ServiceNow Certified Implementation Specialist certifications from SNow Learning or equivalent professional experience.
  • Additional certifications in ITSM, HAM, ITOM, Discovery, Service Mapping, ITIL, Agile, or related technologies are a plus.

Preferred Qualifications and Professional Experience:

  • Experience leading or contributing to a CMDB Center of Excellence, governance board, or enterprise configuration management program.
  • Experience creating repeatable CMDB/CSDM implementation methodologies, delivery accelerators, standards, documentation, and internal intellectual property.
  • Experience with ServiceNow domain separation, large-scale data remediation, multi-source CMDB environments, and complex integration landscapes.
  • Experience with Service Mapping, tag-based service modeling, AIOps, Discovery, ITAM, HAM, SAM, or other ServiceNow capabilities that depend on high-quality CMDB data.
  • Experience supporting pre-sales scoping, solutioning, SOW review, estimate validation, and executive-level customer advisory conversations.
  • Proven ability to drive product development, delivery quality, and strategic initiatives in a technology-focused services organization.

Your future at Presidio
Joining Presidio means stepping into a culture of trailblazers - thinkers, builders, and collaborators - who push the boundaries of what's possible. With our expertise AI-driven analytics, cloud solutions, cybersecurity, and next-gen infrastructure, we enable businesses to stay ahead in an ever-evolving digital world.

title: IT Specialist
description:
The IT Specialist provides skilled technical support to end users across a unique BYOD (bring-your-own-device) research environment, and supports the endpoint, identity, and collaboration services that environment depends on.

The position independently identifies, researches, and resolves technical problems across endpoints, accounts, collaboration services, connectivity, and workplace technology. It documents, tracks, and monitors work to ensure timely resolution, and works to the account provisioning, security, and endpoint configuration standards owned by the Senior and Lead IT Specialists.

Because the Institute is a research organization, the role extends beyond conventional corporate end-user support. It includes supporting specialized scientific workstations and laboratory computers, access to high-capacity research storage, research and scientific applications, instrument-attached systems, and conference-room and collaboration technology.

Who We Are

The Salk Institute is an internationally renowned research institution that values all members of our scientific community. We seek bold and interactive leaders passionate about exploring new frontiers in science. Our collaborative community embraces perspectives across discipline, professional acumen, and unique life experiences, fostering innovation, and a sense of belonging. Together, we strive to improve the wellbeing of humanity through groundbreaking research.

Founded by Jonas Salk, developer of the first safe and effective polio vaccine, the Institute is an independent, nonprofit research organization and architectural landmark: small by choice, intimate by nature, and fearless in the face of any challenge. Salk's vibrant community has many talented individuals from varied backgrounds, each playing a crucial role in driving our mission forward. From visionary leaders to dedicated administrators and brilliant faculty members, the Institute is united by a shared passion for scientific exploration and innovation.

What Your Key Responsibilities Will Be

  • End-User Technical Support — Tier 1 and Tier 2
    • Serves as first point of contact for end-user requests received by telephone, email, ticket, remote tools and in person, and provides second-line resolution for issues requiring deeper diagnosis.
    • Troubleshoots hardware, software, operating system, application and network connectivity issues across macOS, Windows, Linux and mobile platforms.
    • Troubleshoots Microsoft 365, business and scientific applications, printers, peripherals, VPN, Wi-Fi and mobile-device issues.
    • Installs, configures and maintains desktops, laptops, mobile devices and peripheral equipment.
    • Supports specialized scientific workstations, laboratory computers and instrument-attached systems; provides access to high-capacity research storage; installs and troubleshoots research and scientific applications.
    • Provides support across the main campus and remote Institute sites, including scheduled site visits.
    • Provides user training and guidance in supported technologies and applications, and communicates technical concepts clearly to non-technical users.
  • Endpoint, Identity, Collaboration and Workplace Technology Administration
    • Configures and deploys laptops, desktops, mobile devices and peripherals to the Institute’s standard configurations, and applies operating system and application updates.
    • Supports endpoint-management platforms such as Intune, Jamf or SCCM/MECM under established configuration standards.
    • Supports existing user accounts, including passwords, lockouts, multi-factor authentication, group membership, and permissions in Active Directory and Entra ID, working to the provisioning standards owned by the Senior and Lead IT Specialists.
    • Supports Exchange Online and Outlook, Teams, OneDrive, SharePoint, Office applications and collaboration services, including mailboxes, calendars, room calendars and distribution lists.
    • Supports mapped drives, shared folders, OneDrive, Box, SharePoint and external storage, and assists with user data migrations.
    • Supports telephony extensions, voicemail and call routing, printers, scanners, conference-room systems, displays and AV equipment.
    • Verifies that endpoints carry required security controls and remain compliant with institutional configuration standards.
  • Diagnosis, Root Cause and Tier 3 Escalation
    • Diagnoses unfamiliar and intermittent faults, and determines whether an issue originates in the endpoint, application, account, network or upstream infrastructure.
    • Recognizes and reports suspected phishing, malware, and compromised-account activity, and follows the defined escalation procedure to the Cybersecurity Engineer.
    • Diagnoses wired and wireless connectivity, DNS, DHCP, VPN and basic network problems, and escalates infrastructure-level issues with supporting diagnostic detail.
    • Escalates work that exceeds Tier 2 scope to the Systems & Storage, Network or Cybersecurity teams in accordance with criteria set by the Lead IT Specialist.
  • Standards, Knowledge Sharing and Peer Support
    • Works consistently to the technical standards, checklists and procedures maintained by the Senior and Lead IT Specialists, and identifies where those standards require revision.
    • Shares troubleshooting knowledge with colleagues and contributes resolutions to the team knowledge base.
    • Participates in team reviews of recurring issues and service improvement discussions.
  • Projects, Automation, Vendor and Asset Management
    • Participates in application deployments, hardware refreshes, migrations, relocations, infrastructure upgrades and security initiatives.
    • Manages endpoint hardware lifecycle and asset records — receipt, inventory, deployment, tracking, repair, replacement, secure wipe and retirement.
    • Coordinates with hardware and software vendors on warranty repairs, returns, licensing questions and technical support cases.
    • Identifies repetitive support work and contributes to reducing it through scripting, configuration policy or endpoint-management automation.
  • Documentation, Knowledge Management and User Lifecycle
    • Documents incidents, service requests, troubleshooting steps and resolutions in the Institute’s IT service management platform, and meets defined service targets.
    • Creates and maintains knowledge base articles, installation procedures, troubleshooting guides and configuration documentation.
    • Prepares equipment and accounts for new employees and coordinates application access; delivers new-hire IT orientation.
    • Executes terminated-user offboarding to the defined checklist, ensuring accounts, licenses, access and Institute equipment are properly handled and recorded.
    • Monitors personal backlog and alerts the supervisor to unusual situations, ageing items or workload spikes.
  • Performs other related duties as assigned by management.

What we Require

  • Minimum two years of desktop, laptop, mobile and peripheral support experience in a multi-platform environment.
  • Minimum two years supporting macOS and Windows operating systems and business applications; working familiarity with Linux.
  • Minimum two years providing IT support services using a ticketing system, with demonstrated ownership of a personal queue.
  • Demonstrated experience administering user accounts, group membership and permissions in Active Directory or a comparable directory service.
  • Demonstrated experience with endpoint deployment, imaging or provisioning, and secure device disposal.

What We Can Offer

The expected pay range for this position is $31.25-$34.60 hourly. Salk Institute provides pay ranges representing its good faith estimate of what the institute reasonably expects to pay for a position. The pay offered to a selected candidate will be determined based on factors such as (but not limited to) the scope and responsibilities of the position, the qualifications of the selected candidate, departmental budget availability, internal equity, and external market pay for comparable jobs.

Benefits

Salk Institute offers competitive benefits, including medical, dental, vision, retirement, paid time off, tuition reimbursement, patient advocacy services, and transit/parking program.

Salk Values

The Salk Community, both scientists and administrators, worked together to define values that we believe support Salk’s pursuit of excellence. To be truly the best scientific institution requires not only incredible discoveries, but a common understanding of how we should work together to enable those discoveries.

The acronym “I CARE” provides a simple way to remember each of the values and reminds each of us of the importance of what we do each day.

Equal Employment Opportunity Statement

The Salk Institute for Biological Studies is an Equal Opportunity Employer and is committed to providing equal access to opportunities for students, employees, applicants for employment and other visitors. Salk has also adopted and maintains a policy to encourage professional and respectful workplace behavior and prevent discriminatory and harassing conduct in our workplace.

Accordingly, the Institute prohibits harassment and discrimination in employment on the basis of, and considers all qualified applicants for employment without regard to, actual or perceived race (race is inclusive of traits associated with race, including, but not limited to, hair texture and protective hairstyles. Protective hairstyles include, but not limited to, such hairstyles as braids, and twists), color, religion, religious creed (including religious dress and grooming practices), national origin, ancestry, citizenship, physical or mental disability, medical condition (including cancer and genetic characteristics), genetic information, marital status, age, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding, or related medical conditions), reproductive health decision making, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, veteran and/or military status (disabled veteran, veteran of the Vietnam era, other covered veteran status), political affiliation, and any other status protected by state or federal law.

Discrimination is prohibited with any intersectionality of the above-mentioned characteristics, including:

  1. Any combination of characteristics.
  2. A perception that the person has any of the characteristics or any combination of those characteristics.
  3. A perception that the person is associated with a person who has, or is perceived to have, any of those characteristics or any combination of those characteristics.

title: Senior Software Engineer (.NET)
description:
Concord sits at the center of the credit market ecosystem. We provide loan servicing, backup servicing, and capital markets administration for specialty finance lenders, institutional investors, and asset managers. Our clients include originators across fintech, solar, home improvement, equipment finance, and other specialty asset classes. When a lender needs a trusted partner to service their portfolio or a trustee needs real-time reporting, they call Concord.

We're hiring a Senior .NET Software Engineer to design, build and maintain the financial applications our business users rely on every day, working across SQL Server, Snowflake and cloud services.

You'll join a small, senior-leaning team that owns the core applications behind a financial services business. The work is varied: new features on modern .NET services, integrations with internal and third-party systems, and data pipelines feeding analytics. You'll work with Product, Compliance, Security and Data partners, have direct access to the business users you build for, and shape how we design, test and ship.

Responsibilities:

  • Design, build and maintain applications and APIs in C# on .NET (ASP.NET Core, Web API, background services)
  • Write testable, well-documented code and review peers' work against agreed standards
  • Lead technical design for multi-component features and mentor other engineers
  • Build and maintain integrations with internal and third-party systems through APIs and messaging
  • Own features end to end: refine requirements with business partners, estimate, build, test, deploy and support in production
  • Collaborate with Product, Compliance, Security and Data teams to translate business and regulatory requirements into technical solutions
  • Implement security practices that protect sensitive financial data (encryption, authentication, authorization)
  • Apply regulatory and audit requirements, such as data retention and access controls, in system design
  • Troubleshoot production issues, find root causes, and fix the underlying problem rather than the symptoms
  • Keep current with security trends and emerging technologies, and recommend what is worth adopting

Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent experience
  • 7+ years of professional software development, with C# and .NET as your primary stack
  • Hands-on experience with ASP.NET Core, REST APIs, Entity Framework or Dapper, and dependency injection
  • Strong SQL Server skills, including database design, query tuning and indexing
  • Experience with automated testing (xUnit, NUnit or similar)
  • Experience with Git, CI/CD pipelines, and Agile/Scrum methodologies
  • Working knowledge of HTML, CSS and JavaScript
  • Ability to explain a technical trade-off to a non-technical audience and turn business rules into working software
  • A track record of diagnosing and fixing hard problems in production systems, with careful attention to data accuracy
  • Language requirements: fluent English

Nice to Have

  • Cloud experience (Azure or AWS), including containers, serverless functions or infrastructure as code
  • TypeScript experience, including front-end frameworks or Node.js tooling
  • Blazor, Angular or React for front-end work
  • Messaging and integration patterns (queues, event-driven design, SFTP and batch file processing)
  • Experience with Snowflake, ETL/ELT tooling or other data warehouse work
  • Experience in lending, banking, payments, insurance or investment systems
  • A background in operations or another business function, which helps you understand the problems we solve

Benefits

  • Grocery Vouchers
  • Internet Bonus
  • Medical Insurance
  • Life Insurance
  • Dental Insurance
  • Law Benefits

description:

title: Process Technician 2 (TEMP-REQ-2026-0194)
description:
Kyocera has a temp-to-hire position for a Process Technician 2 at our San Diego, CA facility.

Candidates selected for hire will be hired through one of Kyocera’s approved staffing partners.

This position may lead to a direct hire offer with Kyocera International, Inc.

Pay is $19.50 per hour

With nearly 80,000 employees globally, Kyocera is a leading manufacturer of high-tech ceramics in various industries, including aerospace, automotive, medical applications, and semiconductor processing. Our innovative materials are found in everything from smartphones to space shuttles!


Exempt: No
Safety Sensitive: Yes

GENERAL DESCRIPTION OF POSITION

A Process Technician 2 performs a variety of functions associated with manufacturing operations, including working with engineers and operators in set-up and calibration tasks, as well as performing rework and quality testing related to the production of parts, components, subassemblies and final product. Uses programs to collect and evaluate operating data to conduct in-line adjustments to parts, instruments or equipment. Updates and may assist in developing methods and procedures to control or modify the manufacturing process.

REQUIREMENTS

High school diploma or GED required.
2+ years of technician experience required in a manufacturing/production environment.
Ability to read, write and comprehend instructions in English.
Ability to add, subtract, multiply, divide all units of measure including common and decimal fractions.
Ability to use a microscope, depending on the specific function.
Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, color vision and depth perception.
20/20 corrected vision may be required - varies by division
Willingness to wear PPE (examples: goggle, gloves, apron, finger cot, masks, and/or cleanroom apparel.
Ability to grab small parts or hand tools with hands.
Eligible to work in an ITAR environment


ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  1. Monitors and documents the operation of machines in a production environment. Maintains flow of production parts; reports inconsistencies, and suggests improvements in the production process.
  2. Troubleshoots complex or troublesome equipment, may work with facilities team or outside vendor or repair or modification.
  3. May run engineering tests prescribed by engineer. Perform periodic calibration checks.
  4. May recommend process improvements based on test and process results and experience. Troubleshoot machine set up.
  5. Visually inspects parts at required steps in the process with attention to detail, ensuring the parts are within specified tolerances. May disposition of reject parts and train operators and inspectors to improve efficiency.
  6. Maintains and orders/tracks tools according to safety and vendor recommendations. Will use measuring devices, such as micrometers, calipers, CMM and other optical tools.
  7. Participates in the 5S program.
  8. Knowledgeable of Excel and able to accurately enter data into spreadsheets and create graphs. Experience in basic CNC and CMM is helpful.
  9. Complies with applicable requirements of Kyocera International, Inc. policy, ISO 9000, ISO 14001 requirements, ITAR regulations.
  10. May setup/program production or test machinery.
  11. Reads specifications and mechanical drawings.
  12. May assign and check work of lower-level technicians and operators. Perform the duties or an operator or material handler on occasion as needed.

Perform any other related duties as required or assigned.

QUALIFICATIONS
To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty mentioned satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required.


PHYSICAL ACTIVITIES
The following physical activities described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions and expectations.

While performing the functions of this job, the employee is continuously required to talk or hear; regularly required to stand, use hands to finger, handle, turn, twist, or feel; frequently required to walk, sit; and occasionally required to reach with hands and arms, stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl.

The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 50 pounds, frequently lift and/or move up to 25 pounds, regularly lift and/or move up to 10 pounds.

ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITIONS
The following work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

While performing the functions of this job, the employee is occasionally exposed to work near moving mechanical parts, work in high, precarious places, fumes or airborne particles.

The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate.

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION
The above statements are intended to describe the work being performed by people assigned to this job. They are not intended to be an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties and skills required. The duties and responsibilities of this position are subject to change and other duties may be assigned or removed at any time.
This position may require exposure to information subject to US Export Control regulations, i.e.: the International Traffic and Arms Regulations (ITAR) or Export Administration Regulations (EAR). All applicants must be US persons within the meaning of US regulations.

title: Business Graduate - Project Delivery - 2027
description:

At CGI, we empower the next generation of innovators to shape the future of technology and security. As part of #GenerationCGI, you’ll join a community of graduates who are turning ambition into action and possibility into progress.

As a Project Delivery - Business Graduate, you’ll help turn plans into successful outcomes. You’ll be trusted with responsibility from day one, working with colleagues and clients to bring structure, momentum and clear communication to complex projects. Your ideas and contributions will help teams overcome challenges and deliver solutions that make a real difference.

In this role, you’ll help plan, coordinate and deliver projects and services that support organisations across a range of industries. You’ll bring structure to complex work, connect colleagues and clients, and help teams deliver successful outcomes.

You will:

  • Support project delivery: Help develop plans, coordinate activities and monitor progress against agreed milestones.
  • Manage risks and governance: Support project reporting, identify risks and dependencies, and help maintain effective governance.
  • Collaborate with stakeholders: Work with colleagues, clients and delivery partners to maintain clear communication and keep projects moving forward.
  • Improve how we deliver: Use insight and feedback to identify improvements and help teams deliver effective, reliable services.
  • Innovate alongside other graduates: Take part in early careers initiatives that go beyond your day-to-day role.

Every contribution you make will help deliver outcomes with lasting impact.

Locations

Opportunities are available in Birmingham, Edinburgh, Glasgow, Gloucester, Leeds, London, Manchester, Newcastle and Sheffield.

As CGI is a consultancy, you may be required to work in different locations, so flexibility and a willingness to travel are key.

Required qualifications to be successful in this role:

We’re seeking ambitious graduates who are organised, collaborative and motivated by seeing projects through to successful outcomes. Whatever your degree subject, if you’re ready to learn, take responsibility and help teams deliver meaningful work, we want to hear from you.

You should have:

  • A minimum 2:2 degree (some roles may require a 2:1).
  • Strong organisation and planning skills, with the ability to manage priorities and meet deadlines.
  • Clear communication skills and confidence working with colleagues and stakeholders.
  • A collaborative approach and willingness to take responsibility for your work.
  • Good problem-solving skills and attention to detail.
  • An interest in technology, project delivery and improving services.
  • Flexibility to travel and work on projects across the UK.
  • Eligibility for Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) clearance, with many roles requiring higher National Security Vetting. This typically requires 5–10 years of continuous UK residency.

Why Join Us?

At CGI, you’ll be part of a culture that celebrates diversity, inclusion and collaboration, where your perspective is valued and your ideas contribute to meaningful outcomes.

Your journey starts with a structured Early Careers Induction Programme, giving you the foundations to succeed, along with 24/7 e-learning and opportunities to gain professional certifications that build your expertise. You’ll also join our Student Kick-start Initiative, where you’ll collaborate with other graduates on creative projects that deliver impact beyond your day-to-day role.

CGI is an unconditionally inclusive workplace where you are respected, your voice is heard and you can be yourself. We were recognised in the Sunday Times Best Places to Work List 2025 and named a UK ‘Best Employer’ by the Financial Times. We proudly hold a Gold Award in recognition of our support of the Armed Forces Corporate Covenant.

Benefits

Along with a competitive salary and a £1,000 joining bonus, you’ll enjoy benefits that support every stage of your journey. You’ll share in CGI’s success through our matched share scheme, have access to private healthcare, well-being programmes and professional training, and build financial security with a competitive pension. Beyond the day job, you’ll connect with others through graduate networks, diversity groups and social clubs that make your time at CGI both rewarding and enjoyable.

What you can expect from us:

Together, as owners, let’s turn meaningful insights into action.

Life at CGI is rooted in ownership, teamwork, respect and belonging. Here, you’ll reach your full potential because…

You are invited to be an owner from day 1 as we work together to bring our Dream to life. That’s why we call ourselves CGI Partners rather than employees. We benefit from our collective success and actively shape our company’s strategy and direction.

Your work creates value. You’ll develop innovative solutions and build relationships with teammates and clients while accessing global capabilities to scale your ideas, embrace new opportunities, and benefit from expansive industry and technology expertise.

You’ll shape your career by joining a company built to grow and last. You’ll be supported by leaders who care about your health and well-being and provide you with opportunities to deepen your skills and broaden your horizons.

That same commitment to fairness extends to how we use technology. To support our recruitment team, AI tools may be used to help assess applications though they never replace human judgement. All hiring decisions remain entirely in the hands of our recruitment professionals.

Come join our team—one of the largest IT and business consulting services firms in the world.

title: Clinical Director
description:
Salary Starting at $100,000/year, DOE and licensure and Sign on Bonus included.

Do meaningful clinical work and make a real difference!

Sierra Sage Treatment Center provides residential treatment for young women in a safe, supportive, and nurturing environment. Our youth often come to us with complex histories involving trauma, abuse, neglect, substance use, mental health and behavioral challenges. Through individualized treatment, accredited education and a normalized high school experience, we help them build the skills and confidence for healthier futures.

We're looking for a Clinical Director (LPC, LMFT, LCSW) to join our team of compassionate clinicians and youth advocates.

Why Sierra Sage?

Focus on clinical impact.
Unlike private practice and high-volume outpatient settings, your success here isn't measured by how many clients you can fit into a day. You'll have the time and support to build meaningful therapeutic relationships and address needs that go far beyond a 50-minute weekly session.

Work as part of a true treatment team.
You'll collaborate with other clinicians, educators, medical staff, youth care workers, and other professionals working from one integrated treatment plan. Our residential model allows you to see the bigger picture and help shape treatment beyond the therapy room.

Invest in your growth—on our dime.
We provide paid clinical supervision toward licensure, plus training and certification opportunities in evidence-based practices. Build your clinical expertise while advancing your career.

What You'll Do

Provide individual, family, and group therapy.

Conduct clinical assessments and develop individualized treatment plans.

Provide counseling, case management, and treatment coordination.

Collaborate with a multidisciplinary clinical, educational, and residential team.

Build expertise in differential assessment, treatment readiness, stages of change, motivational interviewing, and evidence-based approaches.

Evaluate progress toward treatment goals and maintain timely clinical documentation.

What We're Looking For

Current professional licensure as required in the State of Nevada.

Master's degree in social work, or human services, with four years related experience on residential facility management.

Empathetic, patient, collaborative, and committed to helping young people succeed.

At least one year of experience working with youth or adolescent females.

Commitment to maintaining required CEUs and licensure.

Current driver's license and acceptable three-year driving record.

Ability to complete required background check, drug screen, and TB test.

Compensation & Benefits

Starting at $100,000/year, based on experience and licensure, plus:

Medical, dental, and vision coverage

Company-paid life insurance

403(b) with up to a 6% company match after one year

Paid Time Off and paid holidays

Paid clinical supervision

title: Lifecycle Management Supervisor
description:
We are Neodent, Brazil’s leading dental implant brand. For over 30 years, we have been helping create thousands of new smiles every day. We are part of the Straumann Group and, in Brazil, represent the Neodent, Straumann, ClearCorrect, and Yller brands.

Our purpose is to create new smiles every day. We are guided by a cultural journey and a Protagonist & Learner mindset, empowering our employees to become a high-performance team.

This opportunity is based at our CIC facility in Curitiba, Brazil.


What can you expect from a day with us?

  • Team Leadership: Lead, develop, and coach a team of Product Development Engineers, Design Engineers and Packaging Engineers working on lifecycle management activities. Establish priorities, allocate resources, and ensure timely execution of lifecycle projects, in collaboration with the Product Design & Development team in Basel. Develop technical capabilities within the team, particularly on Critical-to-Quality, GD&T, systematic root cause analysis and problem solving.

  • Product lifecycle management: Lead and coordinate R&D activities for products throughout the post-development and manufacturing lifecycle. Ensure products remain safe, effective, reliable, and compliant following manufacturing transfers and production optimizations.

  • Product and Design Optimization: Identify opportunities to optimize product designs while maintaining required safety, effectiveness, performance, quality, and regulatory requirements, together with your team. Support design-to-cost and design-for-manufacturability initiatives. Accountable for making sure that cost-reduction activities do not compromise product performance, patient/user safety, or regulatory compliance.

  • Manufacturing Transfer & Site Support: Provide R&D leadership and technical support for manufacturing transfers between sites. Identify and manage product risks associated with changes in manufacturing location, equipment, processes, materials, and suppliers.

  • Supporting Technology Management: Supports the evaluation of new technologies in manufacturing that allow reducing COGS and that might allow for new design opportunities.

  • Cross-Functional Leadership: Lead cross-functional projects involving R&D, Manufacturing, Marketing, PMO, Quality, Regulatory, Operations, Supply Chain, Procurement, and other stakeholders. Build strong partnerships with manufacturing sites and act as a trusted R&D partner throughout the product lifecycle.

  • Compliance and Quality: Ensure lifecycle changes are managed in accordance with the Straumann Quality system. Ensure appropriate documentation, traceability, and technical justification for product and process changes. Support regulatory submissions, audits, inspections, and other compliance activities related to lifecycle changes when required.

What do you need to have or know?

  • Fluent English.

  • Development experience in a regulated environment, preferably medical devices. Track record in developing products from conception through transfer to production, or experience in R&D lifecycle management (including manufacturing transfer, post market design changes, etc.)

  • Strong knowledge in Product engineering, Design Controls, Design Verification & Validation (V&V), requirements management, risk management, and manufacturing.

  • Experience applying specific development tools (statistical analysis, root cause analysis, FMEA, analysis of mechanical properties, etc.).

  • Sound knowledge of applicable standards and regulations (ISO 13485, MDR, FDA, ANVISA, and applicable technical standards).

  • Experience managing multidisciplinary technical teams and complex product development projects. Familiar with operating in a complex and changing matrixed environment in international companies.

  • Familiar with project management methodologies and tools applicable to product development.

  • Robust understanding of manufacturing and process technologies and experience in design-to-cost optimization.

  • Work experience in different geographies is an advantage.

title: Installation Rigger (Part Time Casual) - Denver, CO
description:
Position Overview

Installation Riggers will report directly to Lead Installation Riggers and Project Manager of Rigging Installations. Position will perform specific rigging installation activities in accordance with Encore Rigging Installation Standards. They have a shared responsibility in upholding safety and quality standards. Our various point construction methods require great attention to detail, strong mechanical aptitude, as well as great physical stamina. Installation Riggers will perform the majority of their functions at height using safety harnesses to navigate through a ceiling to a work area or by using rope access to climb to a work area when ceilings do not allow direct access. The position is highly team oriented requiring individuals to rely on others for the safety of their well being. Installation Riggers will be responsible for the safety and efficiency of their work in order to maintain project quality, schedule, and budget.

Key Job Responsibilities

Installation Rigging

Installation Riggers will be able to use a variety of tools and construction equipment to build rigging hang-points using a variety of beam clamp designs and concrete epoxy anchors. Will have the ability to work long hours at height in a harness. Installation Riggers must be familiar with a variety of installation procedures and standards including; the setup and use of all required tools on the ground and at heights, safely gain access to point location while carrying a variety of tools, use tied off tools at height to install points, fully visually inspect each point part while installing, mark point areas for future inspections, convey final information on point type to Project Manager of Rigging Installations, ensure final point and hatch end product meets all Encore standards, clean and pack tools and materials for shipping, clean and prepare ballroom for release to hotel and guests. They will install points as designed and engineered with a focus on overall safety and point construction. Position requires extensive travel.

Safety

Responsible for the safety of self, crew, general public and property in a variety of difficult work conditions including but not limited to; confined spaces, rope work at heights up to 240’, truss climbing or walking, use of medium weight power tools from rope or truss or beams at height, driving lifts through or around obstacles, use of heavy machinery on ground, a high degree of dust and dirt, etc. Responsible for maintaining a high standard of quality control ensuring that all installed rigging points meet Encore’s exacting standards before any installed point is used as intended. Will share all knowledge of safety protocol with others while onsite.

Project Management

Position is responsible for tool and material collection and transfer from loading dock to ballrooms. They will be required to set up tools and prepare the job site for the installation including: organization of work space, point installation strategy and identifying and formulating solutions to potential obstructions under the direction of The Project Manager of Rigging Installations. Communicate any issues to Project Manager of Rigging Installations and appropriate team members.

Maintenance and Inspections

Ongoing visual inspection of all tools, hardware, and materials in use including personnel lifts. Escalate any problems with tools, hardware, or materials to the Project Manager of Rigging Installations. Installation Riggers are required to understand a variety of point construction methods. As such they are uniquely qualified to inspect all rigging points installed by Encore or outside contractors. They will be available to the Rigging Inspection Team to conduct annual and “as-needed” inspections on installed rigging points.

Job Qualifications

• Decision Making Responsibility: Subordinate

• Experience Level: 3-4 Years

• Education Level: High School

• Ability to travel extensively

• Will adhere to Encore travel policies

• Will adhere to all Encore dress code and conduct standards

Competencies

Deliver World Class Service

• Hospitality

• Ownership

Do The Right Thing

• Demonstrates Self-Awareness

Drive Results

• Ensures Accountability

See The Big Picture

• Decision Quality

• Manages Complexity

Value People

• Collaborates

Work Environment

Work is performed in a hotel environment that may be under construction and moderately quiet to noisy. Team members may be asked to work in multiple hotel locations. Must be able to work long hours at height in harness and work in a high degree of dust and dirt. Position requires extensive travel and will be required to adhere to Encore’s travel policy. Working times may include days, evenings, weekends and holidays. Team members must adhere to appearance and conduct guidelines as defined by Encore’s Team Member Guidebook and based on an individual hotel or a representation of hotels in that city or area.
