title: Enterprise Customer Experience Manager
description:
At Straumann Group we’re on an exciting journey of growth, innovation, and impact – driven by our mission to improve oral health and transform millions of lives worldwide. United by purpose, we bring our best selves to work every day, embracing a high-performance, player-learner culture that inspires collaboration, curiosity, and ambition. Here, you’ll have the opportunity to take charge of your own career, harnessing your skills, passion, and enthusiasm for learning to continually grow and progress. Together, we’re not just shaping brighter smiles, we’re unlocking the potential of people everywhere, including our own.

The Enterprise Customer Experience Manager strengthens Straumann Group’s partnerships with strategic enterprise customers, particularly Dental Service Organizations (DSOs), by turning customer insight into innovation opportunities and better end-to-end experiences.


The role leads customer discovery and co-creation activities, coordinates reference customer and customer advisory board programmes, and tests how Straumann solutions work together in real customer workflows before launch. It brings the voice of the customer into solution design, product decisions, and commercialization readiness.
The role works with product management, regional teams, and strategic customers.


Key Responsibilities

Customer discovery and innovation

• Identify customer needs, emerging trends, unmet workflow requirements, and opportunities to improve loyalty and deepen strategic partnerships.

• Translate insights into clear opportunity statements, solution concepts, and recommended next steps; coordinate co-creation and innovation workshops and projects with strategic customers.

• For selected opportunities, build a concise case covering expected customer value, business impact, feasibility, and implementation effort.

Reference customers and customer advisory boards

• Build and coordinate a reference customer programme for priority solutions, including identifying suitable customers and agreeing how they can support adoption.

• Establish and coordinate customer advisory boards to explore trends, gather feedback on priorities, and test early solution concepts.

• Synthesize insights from references, advisory boards, and customer engagement into actionable recommendations for internal teams.

Customer experience and solution design testing

• Plan and coordinate end-to-end customer experience and solution design testing before launch, confirming that products, digital solutions, integrations, and workflows work for enterprise customers.

• Capture issues, dependencies, and improvement opportunities; agree owners and follow through with Product, Engineering, Clinical, IT, and other teams.

• Share clear findings and launch recommendations so customer experience risks are addressed before release.

Solution readiness and cross-functional delivery

• Assess existing and upcoming Straumann Group solutions from an enterprise customer perspective, identifying gaps in clinical, operational, technical, and organizational fit.

• Clarify which capabilities are available, which require configuration, and which need further design or development; document requirements, risks, assumptions, and dependencies.

• Shape new or improved solution concepts with customers and internal teams, balancing customer value, feasibility, scalability, and delivery constraints.

• Coordinate actions across Product Management, Engineering, Clinical, IT, Commercialization, Implementation, Marketing, regional teams, and Enterprise Validation.


Your Profile - Qualifications

• 5+ years of experience in customer innovation, solution design, customer experience, product management, enterprise consulting, or a related field.

• Experience facilitating customer discovery, workshops, co-creation, advisory groups, or customer research.

• Experience translating customer needs into structured insights, solution concepts, requirements, or recommendations.

• Understanding of enterprise workflows and the needs of multi-site organizations, ideally DSOs or other healthcare groups.

• Strong project coordination skills and confidence working with senior customer stakeholders and cross-functional teams.

• Excellent written and verbal communication, facilitation, analytical, and presentation skills.

• A practical, customer-centred approach to identifying issues, aligning stakeholders, and following actions through.

• Fluent in English.

Preferred Skills

• Experience in dental, medical technology, healthcare, or another regulated industry.

• Experience developing customer references, testimonials, customer advisory boards, or strategic customer programmes.

• Familiarity with digital dentistry, intraoral scanning, imaging, laboratory workflows, practice-management systems, or dental IT environments is a plus.

• Experience with usability or experience testing, product launches, or commercialization evidence.

How success will be measured

• End-to-end customer experience issues and solution design gaps are identified early, assigned to owners, and addressed before launch where feasible.

• Customer discovery and advisory activities produce clear insights, prioritized opportunities, and agreed follow-up actions.

• Strategic customer innovation projects progress from discovery into co-creation, solution proposals, or delivery plans.

• Customer advisory board input informs trend assessments, solution priorities, and early concept testing.

• Reference customers and testimonials are available for priority solutions and support peer engagement with other customers.

• Customer feedback and innovation strengthen strategic partnerships and support adoption of Straumann Group solutions.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, or disability.

title: Global Product Manager Implant Scanning
description:
Within the Straumann Group, our Tech organization strives to empower dental professionals and partners to make patient care more accessible, predictable, and convenient. As Global Product Manager – Implant Scanning Innovations, you will be part of our highly motivated and dynamic team driving the next generation of digitally enabled implant workflows and treatment innovations.

In this exciting and versatile role, you will develop and lead the product strategy for scanner-enabled implant workflow innovations, focusing on digital full arch solutions, implant scanning workflows, scan body innovations, and integrated treatment experiences powered by Straumann intraoral scanning solutions. You will play a key role in shaping new clinical workflows and digital treatment concepts around Straumann’s core implant business, ensuring seamless integration between scanning, implant systems, restorative workflows, digital services, and software platforms.

A key focus area of the role is the evolution and commercialization of DirectIP™ and future full arch workflow solutions, enabling clinicians to deliver more predictable, scalable, and efficient digital implant treatments. You will work closely with product management, development teams, implant business units, restorative and surgical teams, AI and digital platform teams, as well as external partners and key opinion leaders to bring differentiated workflow innovations to market. This highly cross-functional and collaborative role requires strong ownership, strategic thinking, customer centricity, and the ability to drive innovation and alignment across multiple functions, teams, and brands in a global and multicultural environment.

Key responsibilities

  • Develop and articulate a clear product strategy and vision for implant scanning innovations and digitally enabled implant workflows.
  • Own the roadmap and lifecycle of digital implant workflow innovations, including DirectIP™, digital full arch workflows, and future implant scanning solutions.
  • Identify customer pain points and market opportunities around implant workflows and translate them into differentiated digital solutions.
  • Drive innovation around scanbody-enabled workflows, implant scanning concepts, workflow automation, and AI-supported treatment experiences.
  • Collaborate closely with core IOS product management and development teams to enable clinically excellent and easy-to-adopt implant workflows on Straumann scanning platforms.
  • Partner with implant business units, restorative and surgical teams to ensure successful integration into interdisciplinary treatment protocols and digital workflows.
  • Work closely with AXS and digital platform teams to improve end-to-end workflow integration, case management, and connected digital experiences.
  • Collaborate with product marketing teams on launch readiness, customer adoption, market introduction, and portfolio expansion strategies.
  • Interact regularly with customers, clinicians, and countries to gain deep insight into workflow adoption, clinical requirements, and competitive solutions.
  • Be the product expert and key contact person for implant scanning innovations and digital full arch workflow solutions.
  • Lead cross-functional product initiatives and drive alignment across multicultural teams, brands, and external partners while fostering a strong one-team approach.

Your profile

  • Postgraduate degree in business, marketing, engineering, dentistry or a related field
  • 7+ years of professional experience in product management or related functions.
  • Experience with medical devices required, experience in dental preferred.
  • Experience with software development and agile framework required.
  • Business fluent in English, other languages advantageous.

Your skills

  • Driven and proactive mindset, demonstrating high energy and a strong ability to take initiative to effectively drive projects forward.
  • Capability to create effective working relationship with customers, partners and colleagues across departments and regions.
  • Strong team player, comfortable in working in a fast-paced dynamic environment.

title: Business Coordinator Partner
description:
Be the trusted partner behind one of Straumann Group's global leadership teams.

At Straumann Group, we're transforming dentistry through innovation, digital technologies, and customer-centric solutions. As part of our Integrated Dental Technologies (IDT) business, you'll work alongside senior leaders who are shaping the future of our global organization. We're looking for an experienced Business Coordinator/Collaboration Partner to join our team in Madrid.

This is much more than an administrative role. You'll become a trusted partner to our leadership team, helping them stay organized, connected, and focused on driving the business forward. You'll work directly with Vice Presidents and Global Leaders, supporting strategic priorities while ensuring the day-to-day operations of the leadership team run seamlessly.

If you're proactive, highly organized, thrive in a fast-paced international environment, and enjoy working with senior stakeholders, we'd love to hear from you.


About the Role

As Business Coordinator/Collaboration Partner, you'll provide executive and operational support to the IDT Leadership Team and senior leaders across our global organization.

You'll coordinate complex calendars, international travel, leadership meetings, business events, and key operational activities that enable the leadership team to perform at its best. This is a highly visible position requiring someone who can confidently engage with senior executives, anticipate needs before they arise, and balance strategic thinking with hands-on execution.

No two days are the same, and that's exactly what makes this role exciting.

What You'll Do

Partner with Senior Leadership

  • Support the IDT Leadership Team in their day-to-day activities.
  • Manage complex executive calendars across multiple time zones.
  • Anticipate scheduling conflicts and proactively identify solutions.
  • Act as a trusted partner, ensuring leaders are prepared and focused on business priorities.

Coordinate Global Travel

  • Organize domestic and international travel from start to finish.
  • Manage flights, accommodation, visas, itineraries and logistics.
  • Process expenses and ensure compliance with company policies.

Combining strong analytical capability with business understanding, the role leverages market data, employee insights, HR technology, and benchmarking to generate actionable Total Rewards recommendations that help leaders address key talent and workforce challenges. Working closely with teams across Human Resources, Finance, business leaders, and external partners, the Total Rewards Analyst contributes to competitive pay, effective program administration, regulatory compliance, data governance, and a responsive employee support.


Job Responsibilities:

Compensation Analysis and Program Support
• Conduct market pricing and competitive benchmarking using compensation surveys, labor-market data, internal workforce information, and other relevant market resources.
• Perform job evaluations and support the maintenance of job architecture, career levels, salary structures, geographic differentials, job codes, and compensation guidelines.
• Support the localization of global pay architecture frameworks, salary structures, and compensation guidelines to ensure market competitiveness, regulatory compliance, and organizational consistency.
• Analyze internal equity, pay compression, salary progression, market position, and other compensation trends to identify risks and recommend appropriate actions.
• Support annual and off-cycle compensation processes, including merit increases, promotions, market adjustments, incentive awards, and salary-structure updates.
• Develop compensation models, budget forecasts, and scenario analyses to support workforce planning and compensation decision-making.
• Review proposed pay actions for consistency with compensation philosophy, internal equity, market competitiveness, and approved guidelines.
• Partner with Talent Acquisition and HR Business Partners to provide market data and compensation guidance for new hires, promotions, transfers, and retention situations.
• Support the design, implementation, and evaluation of base-pay, incentive, recognition, and other compensation programs.
• Prepare decision-ready compensation reports, dashboards, presentations, and recommendations for HR and business leadership.


Benefits Analysis and Program Support
• Support the administration and ongoing evaluation of health, dental, vision, retirement, wellness, leave, and other employee benefit programs.
• Analyze enrollment, participation, utilization, demographic trends, claims experience, plan costs, and employee feedback to evaluate program effectiveness.
• Develop reports and insights that identify benefit-plan risks, cost drivers, service issues, and opportunities for program improvement.
• Support annual benefit renewals, open enrollment, plan changes, implementation activities, and employee communications.
• Coordinate with benefit brokers, consultants, carriers, and vendors to support accurate and effective program delivery.
• Monitor vendor service levels, data quality, issue resolution, and contractual performance.
• Review eligibility, enrollment, billing, and vendor data to identify discrepancies and ensure accurate benefit administration.
• Serve as an escalation resource for complex employee benefit questions and coordinate resolution with internal teams and external partners.
• Assist in developing clear, accessible Total Rewards communications that improve employee understanding and use of available programs.

Data Analytics, Reporting, and Technology

• Use enterprise HR systems, compensation platforms, business-intelligence tools, and advanced spreadsheet capabilities to analyze compensation, benefits, and workforce data.
• Develop and maintain dashboards, scorecards, and key performance indicators measuring program competitiveness, cost, utilization, equity, and effectiveness.
• Automate recurring reports, audits, and analytical workflows to improve accuracy, efficiency, and access to information.
• Apply AI responsibly and ethically, ensuring use cases align with data privacy, confidentiality, governance requirements, and organizational policies.
• Demonstrate curiosity by questioning data sources, methodologies, and apparent results to ensure conclusions are accurate, credible, and actionable.
• Maintain the integrity of foundational HR data, including job architecture elements within systems such as SAP SuccessFactors, or comparable HRIS platforms.
• Conduct regular data audits, reconciliations, and quality reviews to ensure information is complete, accurate, and consistent across systems.
• Document analytical methodologies, assumptions, data definitions, procedures, and controls to support repeatability and data governance.
• Identify opportunities to improve Total Rewards processes through automation, system enhancements, self-service reporting, and emerging HR technologies.
• Demonstrate analytical curiosity and sound judgment by validating underlying data, questioning assumptions, investigating anomalies, and ensuring the ethical and appropriate use of AI and sensitive workforce information in accordance with data governance standards.


Compliance, Controls, and Governance
• Support compliance with applicable compensation and benefits laws and regulations, including FLSA, ERISA, ACA, COBRA, HIPAA, equal-pay requirements, and pay-transparency obligations.
• Assist with regulatory reporting, plan audits, internal controls, required notices, filings, and documentation.
• Audit compensation transactions and benefit records for alignment with company policies, approval requirements, and established program guidelines.
• Maintain appropriate confidentiality and safeguards for sensitive employee, compensation, benefits, and health-related information.
• Partner with HR Operations, Payroll, Employer Relations, Finance, and external advisors to address compliance questions and implement required changes.
• Support the development and maintenance of compensation and benefits policies, procedures, process documentation, and governance standards.


Partnership and Decision Support
• Serve as an analytical resource and internal consultant to HR Business Partners, Talent Acquisition, Finance, and business leaders.
• Translate complex compensation, benefits, and workforce information into clear business insights and actionable recommendations.
• Provide analytical support for organizational changes, workforce planning, restructuring, job design, retention initiatives, and other business priorities.
• Partner with Finance on compensation budgets, benefit-cost forecasts, workforce assumptions, and financial-impact analyses.
• Present findings and recommendations to HR leadership and other stakeholders through concise reports, visualizations, and presentations.
• Monitor external market practices, regulatory developments, workforce trends, and emerging Total Rewards strategies.
• Support special projects such as pay-equity reviews, benefit-plan evaluations, job-architecture initiatives, mergers and acquisitions, or HR technology implementations.

Work Environment & Physical Attributes:
• General office environment.
• Sit for extended periods of time.

Minimum Qualifications:

• Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, Finance, Economics, Statistics, Data Analytics, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
• Three to five years of progressively responsible experience in compensation, benefits, Total Rewards, HR analytics, or a related analytical role.
• Experience conducting market pricing, compensation analysis, benchmarking, job evaluation (Mercer exposure as a plus), or salary-structure analysis.
• Working knowledge of employee benefits programs and benefit-administration processes.
• Strong quantitative, analytical, and problem-solving skills, including the ability to identify patterns, evaluate alternatives, and develop recommendations.
• Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel, including pivot tables, lookup functions, conditional formulas, data validation, and analytical modeling.
• Experience working with enterprise HRIS, compensation-management, or benefits-administration systems.
• Ability to interpret complex information and communicate findings clearly to both technical and nontechnical audiences.
• Strong organizational and project-management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and recurring deadlines.
• Demonstrated discretion when handling confidential employee and compensation information.


Preferred Qualifications:
• Experience with SAP SuccessFactors, or a comparable enterprise HR platform.
• Experience with Power BI or similar data preparation and visualization tools.
• Experience supporting annual compensation planning, pay-equity analysis, benefit renewals, or open enrollment.
• Familiarity with AI-enabled analytical tools, workflow automation, and responsible use of generative AI in HR processes.
• Experience with compensation modeling, workforce forecasting, incentive analysis, or predictive analytics.
• Experience transitioning from an analytical, financial, market research, or business intelligence role into Compensation & Benefits or Total Rewards would be an asset.
• Professional certification such as Certified Compensation Professional, Certified Benefits Professional, Certified Employee Benefit Specialist, SHRM-CP, SHRM-SCP, PHR, or SPHR.

title: Research Programmer IV- Machine Learning & Computational Neuroscience, Kennedy Lab
description:
ABOUT US:

Scripps Research is a nonprofit biomedical institute ranked as one of the most influential in the world for its impact on innovation. We celebrated our 100-year legacy in 2024. This significant milestone marks a century of seminal discoveries in immunology, infectious diseases (such as COVID-19, flu, HIV), neuroscience, heart disease, cancer, and more. Located in La Jolla, California, the institute houses six research departments, multiple Nobel laureates, a top-ranked graduate school and a leading postdoctoral training program. Scripps Research encompasses two elite and highly innovative institutes, the Calibr-Skaggs Institute for Innovative Medicines and Scripps Research Translational Institute, which merge foundational studies in biology, chemistry and computer science with translational science to produce pioneering drugs and advances in digital and precision medicine. Together, we cultivate new scientific leaders and expand the frontiers of knowledge to deliver medical breakthroughs impacting human health around the globe. If you have a passion for making a difference, this could be your opportunity to join our transformative team.

POSITION TITLE: Research Programmer IV (Software Engineer)

POSITION SUMMARY:

The Kennedy laboratory is involved in numerous projects to track, quantify, and forecast individual and group behavior and relate it to recorded neural activity. We develop new computational methods to understand how agents (animals, humans, virtual) gather information about their sensory environment, integrate this with internal motivational needs, and execute goal-directed actions in complex, naturalistic environments. We also develop machine learning and computer vision platforms for high-throughput animal phenotyping, with the goal of accelerating drug screening and repurposing efforts at Scripps.

We seek motivated individuals interested in gaining hands-on experience in scientific research projects, with a goal of contributing to scientific papers and participating in an active lab environment. You will also have the opportunity to lead independent research projects on existing datasets from our collaborators (U Penn, UCLA, Harvard, U Utah, Northwestern, and others). This is an ideal position for applicants interested in building their scientific CV ahead of applying to graduate programs in Computational Neuroscience or Machine Learning, or those looking for a longer term position where they can contribute to original scientific research and model development.

REQUIREMENTS:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems or related field or an equivalent combination of education, training and/or experience. A degree in a biological or chemical science may be accepted if applicable to the science developed/performed in the individual lab.
  • Minimum of 8 years experience in software application development or research programming.
  • Extensive experience with software development in Python.
  • Experience building and training deep neural networks for supervised, unsupervised, or reinforcement learning problems.
  • A demonstrated ability to apply the fundamentals of software application development.
  • Experience with version control, including git and github.

Please include code samples and/or a link to a public code repository with examples of your work.

PREFERRED SKILLSET:

Prior experience with the one or more of the following is preferred:

  • Experience with sequence/time series data, control/reinforcement learning problems and environments, time series forecasting.
  • An understanding of generative modeling (hidden Markov models, diffusion models, etc).
  • Familiarity with topics in motor control, robotics, and neuroscience.

As a member of a computational lab working in team projects, the following general skills are also preferred:

  • Experience developing scalable system architectures that adhere to good software engineering principles.
  • Ability to tackle large, open-ended research questions independently and as part of a team.
  • Willingness to be an active participant in a computational lab environment, including taking part in lab meetings, journal clubs, and hackathons.
  • Experience working within a diverse, interdisciplinary team.
  • Experience contributing to open source software projects.

    LOCATION: La Jolla, California.

    PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS: This position works in an office environment, and it is expected that work will be primarily performed in-person.

    COMPENSTAION:

    The expected hiring range for this position is $90,000 to $110,000, commensurate with experience. Consideration will be given to experience that exceeds the listed requirements.

    COMPREHENSIVE BENEFITS INCLUDE:

    • Employer Contributed Retirement Plan – Depending on eligibility, employees receive an employer contributed retirement plan (no employee contribution required) and the option to contribute to a 403(b) (which is similar to a 401(k) using your own pre or post-tax dollars)
    • Full Suite of Health and Welfare plans including three medical plan options (including an HSA available option), dental, vision, life insurance, disability, EAP and more
    • Access to Flexible Spending Accounts (Medical/Dependent Care)
    • Competitive vacation and sick leave policies

title: Parts Outfitter Associate
description:
The Parts Outfitter Associate is responsible for supporting customers, technicians, and internal teams by sourcing, organizing, and distributing RV parts and accessories. This role ensures the right parts are available at the right time, contributing directly to efficient service operations and a superior customer experience. The Parts Outfitter Associate manages inventory, assists customers with product selection, processes orders, and maintains a well-organized parts department.

Key Objectives

  • Quickly locate, source, and distribute parts for service jobs, customer orders, and inventory needs
  • Provide knowledgeable guidance to customers and staff regarding RV parts, accessories, and product compatibility
  • Maintain proper stock levels, ensure accurate counts, and support timely restocking

Responsibilities

  • Assist customers in selecting RV parts and accessories that fit their needs, usage, and budget
  • Support technicians by pulling requested parts, verifying compatibility, and ensuring timely delivery to the service bays
  • Receive, inspect, and stock incoming parts shipments while maintaining accurate inventory records
  • Organize parts shelves, storage areas, and displays for accessibility, cleanliness, and visual appeal
  • Process customer orders in person, by phone, and online, including quotes, invoices, and returns
  • Maintain knowledge of RV brands, systems, and commonly used components
  • Communicate with vendors to check availability, pricing, or track special orders
  • Assist in cycle counts, inventory audits, and resolving discrepancies
  • Provide recommendations on accessories, upgrades, and add-on products that enhance customer experience and increase sales

What you’ll bring

  • Ability to pass a background and drug test
  • Demonstrate alignment with the Company’s vision, mission, and core values in all interactions
  • Strong customer service and communication skills
  • Basic understanding of RV or vehicle systems (electrical, plumbing, HVAC, appliance)
  • Ability to stay organized, multitask, and manage inventory in a fast-paced environment
  • Comfort with computers and parts-management software
  • Attention to detail and willingness to learn the technical aspects of RV components
  • Must be able to lift at least 50 pounds
  • Forklift operation certification
  • Propane Certification
  • Available at least 2 Saturdays a month

Expected Results

  • Accurate and timely delivery of parts to customers and technicians
  • Improved service workflow due to efficient parts management
  • High customer satisfaction through knowledgeable and friendly assistance
  • Reduced inventory errors, stockouts, and service delays
  • Well-organized parts department that supports efficient daily operations

Resources

  • Parts management and inventory software tools
  • Vendor catalogs, OEM parts guides, and technical reference materials
  • Support from purchasing, service, and customer service teams
  • Training on RV systems, product lines, and parts-management best practices
  • Organized storage areas, displays, and equipment for stocking and handling parts

Who we are

Bish’s RV is one of the largest family-owned RV dealers in the country. We are dedicated to providing quality products and services that exceed the expectations of our customers and creating an atmosphere where our customers can enjoy a positive experience as friends of our family business.

Our company is currently experiencing record growth with more expansion on the way. The opportunities to grow within our organization are outstanding and our dedication to each employee’s success is unparalleled.

We are looking for top performers who set high expectations for themselves and are willing to put in the time and effort to achieve them. We are a goal-driven company with a high-performance culture and believe in setting ourselves apart by being “Different with a Purpose.” Our culture is built upon the foundation of our core values: We are Genuine, Fun, and Driven by Results.

Perks

  • Comprehensive benefits package including medical, vision, dental, and other supplemental coverages
  • 401K
  • Employee discounts
  • Company-paid life insurance
  • Gym membership reimbursement
  • Opportunities for advancement
  • Annual Incentive Trip for Top Performers
  • RV Borrowing Program
  • Access to a partner insurance agency for personalized quotes and coverage guidance on home, auto, RV, and specialty insurance products
  • Incredible Team Culture

We are an equal opportunity employer and prohibit discrimination/harassment without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws.

Bish’s RV honors our military service members, veterans, and their family members by being a military friendly workplace. Many of the positions within our organization are transferable from previous military occupations.

title: Chief Engineer
description:
Summary of Job Description

Responsible for the overall maintenance of the building. This position directs and works with property managers to successfully execute all engineering operations, including proper operation, maintenance, and repair of all HVAC, refrigeration, plumbing, electrical, irrigation, life safety, electrical and mechanical equipment/systems. Works to establish a safe and secure environment for all guests and associates. Strives to continually improve guest and employee satisfaction and maximize the financial performance of the department.

title: Shop Technician
description:
PAPE’ MACHINERY, INC. - AGRICULTURE & TURF DIVISION -
OKANOGAN, WA

SHOP MECHANIC:

Are you passionate about working on heavy equipment and enjoy turning wrenches? Are you eager to expand your skills and advance your career as a technician? If you're not just looking for another job—but a long-term career—then Pape’ Machinery has the opportunity for you.

As a premier capital equipment dealer in the West, Pape’ is looking for a dedicated Shop Technician to join our team. At Pape’, we’re committed to your professional growth. We invest in our technicians with top-tier training programs, state-of-the-art resources, and ongoing support.

In return, we offer more than just a paycheck—we provide a career path with competitive compensation, excellent benefits, and a strong work-life balance for you and your family. Join the Pape’ team and build your future with us!

WHAT YOU’LL DO:

As a Shop Mechanic, you will work on all makes and models of agriculture equipment in the shop ensuring equipment repairs are done accurately and timely. All your hard work is geared toward supporting our customers and maximizing their uptime.

Each day, you will be analyzing and diagnosing agriculture equipment malfunctions or failures. You will then repair, replace or rebuild engines, transmissions, carburetors, final drives, steering, clutches, cross shafts, hydraulic components including pump motors, valves, and all related components, electrical systems, and air systems. Additionally, you will assist with pre-delivery setup and installation on all makes and models of John Deere equipment and allied products.

Picture yourself working alongside other trained Mechanics in a shop that has all the support and resources you need to perform top-notch work on equipment and watching your career flourish!

WHAT YOU NEED:

  • 2 or more years of working knowledge of small engines and agricultural equipment including mechanical, electrical, hydraulic systems, and air conditioning systems.
  • A team-oriented personality, with the focus and drive to work without direct supervision.
  • Basic computer knowledge.
  • Self-motivation and assertiveness.
  • Must provide own tools.

Compensation: $25-34/hr (Depending on Experience)

Why work for Pape’:

  • Competitive pay based on your skills, training, and experience level.
  • Outstanding benefits including – 401(k) & Roth 401(k) Retirement Plans with Company Match; Medical, Dental, Vision and Prescription Insurance; Flexible Spending Accounts (Flex Plans); Life Insurance; Short- and Long-Term Disability Insurance; Employee Assistance Program; Online and Instructor-Led Training; Tuition Reimbursement for Training Programs.
  • Progressive Vacation Plans, Sick Leave & Paid Holidays – Members receive 80 hours of vacation (First year is prorated for new hires based on start date), 1 hour of sick leave for every 40 hours worked, and 7 paid holidays each year. Pape’ vacation plans also have tiers based on your seniority, so as your seniority grows, your vacation time off does as well.
  • Advancement – Pape’ is a dynamic, growth-oriented organization with a focus on promoting from within.
  • Stability and reputation — Pape’ is a family-owned, fourth-generation company with over 160 locations, over 4,000 members and 85 plus years of experience. Pape’ is known for their stability, honesty and integrity.
  • Equipment – Pape’ has the largest equipment inventory in the West and an unparalleled parts inventory!
  • Employee impact – Enjoy an open-door policy where your voice will be heard and your opinions will matter.
  • Training – You will be provided with training and mentoring to prepare you for your role and continued learning to grow your skills.

The Pape’ Group maintains a drug-free workplace and as such, requires candidates to successfully pass a pre-employment drug test.

title: Relationship Advisor Full-Time (Bainbridge)
description:

title: Reporting Analyst - Temporary position
description:

In this temporary assignment, you will support reliable reporting and performance-measurement processes while helping us simplify and improve the way reporting services are delivered to users.

  • Group reporting: Support the preparation, compilation, validation, and timely delivery of recurring Finance reports.

  • Performance measurement: Support the review and validation of performance statistics and submitted adjustments around the Group Short-Term Incentive (STI) process, ensuring consistent application of the applicable governance framework.
  • Innovate Reporting process enablement: Improve digital reporting and workflow-enabled services, helping increase process efficiency, governance, and user adoption.

  • Transformation support: Contribute to selected work packages alongside ongoing reporting and Finance transformation initiatives.

  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Business Administration, Accounting, Economics, or a related discipline.
  • Professional experience: 3+ years of progressive experience in FP&A, Accounting, Controlling, Financial Reporting, or a related Finance role.
  • Financial understanding: Sound understanding of financial concepts and confidence working with financial reports and performance data.
  • English: Fluent professional English is required; additional languages are an advantage.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Interpersonal effectiveness: Strong interpersonal skills, professional judgment, empathy, and strong interpersonal and communication skills.
  • Global collaboration: Proven ability to work effectively with diverse stakeholders, ideally in an international or matrix organization.
  • Digital mindset: Comfortable using standard reporting and collaboration tools, with an interest in process automation and digital workflows.
  • Independent problem solving: Comfortable navigating ambiguity, setting priorities, and solving problems independently and pragmatically.

title: Orthodontic Solutions Specialist WA
description:
About Straumann

The Straumann Group unites global reach, experience and innovation with passion and a commitment for uncompromising quality, making enhanced dental healthcare available and accessible to customers and patients around the globe. The group unites global and international brands that stand for excellence, innovation, and quality, including Straumann, Neodent, Anthogyr, Medentika, ClearCorrect, Dental Wings and other fully- or partly owned companies and partners.

In 2017 Straumann entered the highly attractive market for Clear Aligner to support its strategy as becoming the leading provider for esthetic dentistry solutions. To achieve this step, the Straumann Group acquired the US-based company ClearCorrect. With determination, ClearCorrect grew into a viable player in the clear aligner space, which attracted the attention of many customers globally since 2006. Acquiring ClearCorrect has provided Straumann with technology and expertise in orthodontics.

People and culture are the Straumann Group’s greatest assets; they are the keys to high performance and sustainable success. We strive for a culture that builds trust and collaboration, fosters diversity, embraces change, promotes agility, learning and innovation, creates opportunities, allows people to make mistakes and encourages them to take both responsibility and ownership. The fundamental driver of our culture is the player-learner mindset, which we seek to inspire and nurture in every employee.

Summary of position

Whilst Straumann is the market leader in dental implants, we are looking for talents to build a new market segment in Orthodontics across Australia. In this endeavor, the Ortho solutions specialist will focus on gaining and new and developing existing customers for ClearCorrect, generating case submission and production in their designated territory. He/she is responsible for generating new accounts from leads, converting competitive users, developing, and growing existing providers, enhance customer loyalty and utilization rate through providing excellent service and supporting patient growth activities. This is a field-based role which requires travel on a day-to-day basis. The position holder is expected to perform at a high level with limited direct supervision, in other words, a self-starter.

In this role, you are empowered to operate your territory like your own business, while also contributing to the brand and region's overall growth strategy. Your main responsibility is to meet Straumann’s sales objectives for your assigned product portfolio by establishing profitable relationships with targeted practices across the dental community in your territory. This involves driving case production by reaching out to high-performing doctors to secure new business, nurturing existing accounts, assisting with initial case submissions, and fostering referrals. A successful candidate should have existing connections within the dental provider network and a strong dedication to prioritizing customer success, as their achievements directly impact ours. This field-based position requires the ability to independently meet sales targets and thrive with minimal direct supervision.

This position is responsible for, but not limited to, the following:

  • Drive profitable sales growth and maximize sales revenue within a defined territory by developing, maintaining, and advancing existing accounts and prospects
  • Create an unparalleled customer experience by acting as a strategic business partner to existing customers within the defined territory by focusing on customers’ growth goals and how ClearCorrect and Straumann Group can help them achieve these goals
  • Achieve new business targets by proactively identifying, targeting, and converting prospect accounts and new business in the defined territory

  • Collaborate with Product Marketing and Market Communications to support the execution of all marketing launch plans and new product sales objectives
  • Attend and represent ClearCorrect and Straumann at customer events as required, including but not limited to regional events and national trade shows
  • Effectively and efficiently leverage education events to develop existing customers, build brand loyalty and gain new customers. Develop Study Clubs within the territory, actively participate, ensure ClearCorrect presentation is rolled out in study club, and develop customer relationships with existing and new participants
  • Keep abreast of key clinical studies and scientific papers supporting ClearCorrect’s product benefits
  • Regular use of all sales tools, such as SAP CRM, to effectively plan and measure sales activities against territory’s current customer base and prospective customers. Routinely run reports to align trends, customer needs, and opportunities with territory business strategy. All employees with customer facing interactions are required to log quality activities with every ClearCorrect customer and prospect
  • Other related duties as assigned
  • Frequent travel (including overnight travel) is required and will vary depending upon the specific territory

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s Degree OR 3+ years of outside sales, account management or clinical experience in the dental field
  • Must possess a valid, unencumbered Driver’s License

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Effective communication skills with the ability to present and negotiate
  • Ability to type at least 50 words per minute

  • General computer efficiency including ability to operate Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint
  • Strong oral and written communications, including presentation skills

  • Confident in using different insights and adapts selling approach based on customers’ needs and situation
  • Maintains integrity, high ethics, and professional codes of conduct at all times
  • Able to deliver highly complex information in clear, structured, and compelling manner

Job Description

Job Title: Plan Deconversion Specialist

Department: Implementation FLSA Status: Non-Exempt Job Status: FT

Reports To: Manager, Plan Conversions

Positions Supervised: n/a Work Schedule: Monday - Friday, 8:30 am - 5:00 pm

Position Summary

The Plan Deconversion Specialist supports the technical and operational execution of retirement plan exits, deconversions, outgoing transfers, plan terminations, and related asset and record movement activities. This role coordinates and completes assigned conversion-out activities while maintaining accurate records, compliant processing, clear communication, and timely case completion. The position serves as a key point of coordination among clients, successor providers, relationship owners, and internal operational teams by maintaining current case requirements, milestones, risks, status updates, and supporting documentation. Through effective case management, project coordination, and cross-functional collaboration, the Plan Deconversion Specialist helps deliver an orderly transition of plan records and assets from Slavic401k to the receiving provider.

Essential Functions

· Review plan documents, deconversion requests, participant records, census information, loans, notices, transfer instructions, successor-provider requirements, and plan-level considerations.

· Coordinate assigned outgoing plan transfers, deconversions, plan exits, and related asset and record movement activities using established procedures and timelines.

· Confirm the scope and type of exit, required deliverables, responsible parties, key dependencies, and target transfer dates.

· Identify missing, inconsistent, or potentially noncompliant information and escalate concerns as appropriate.

· Research discrepancies and assist with resolving participant record, loan, liquidation, asset, documentation, and transfer-readiness concerns.

· Manage assigned conversion-out cases and support more complex exits as directed by leadership or senior team members.

· Track milestones, blackout periods, notice requirements, liquidation activity, outgoing files, transfer instructions, documentation, and issue resolution.

· Maintain accurate and current case information, including requirements, risks, documentation requests, status updates, owner assignments, and next steps.

· Prepare, coordinate, and validate outgoing participant records, plan data, reports, and deconversion files required by the successor provider.

· Support outgoing asset processing, including liquidation coordination, wire or transfer instructions, asset documentation, and related reconciliation activities.

· Review outgoing files, final reports, participant balances, loan records, liquidation activity, wire details, and accounting support for completeness and accuracy before submission for release or required approval.

· Reconcile outgoing assets and records, investigate differences, and coordinate necessary follow-up with internal teams, clients, and successor providers.

· Coordinate the resolution of residual balances, trailing activity, outstanding loans, forfeitures, and other items that may delay final transfer or case closure.

· Complete and document assigned conversion-out activities in accordance with applicable IRS, ERISA, DOL, plan document, provider, contractual, and internal requirements, and escalate potential exceptions or compliance concerns.

· Validate notice timing, participant records, transfer documentation, approvals, delivery evidence, and audit-ready support.

· Document potential compliance, operational, financial, or participant-impact risks, including required follow-up and escalation.

· Communicate assigned transfer requirements, open items, documented risks, and next steps to clients, successor providers, and internal stakeholders within established communication and escalation guidelines.

· Partner with Client Relationships, Operations, Compliance, Finance, Trading, Participant Services, and other internal teams to resolve issues and improve exit handoffs.

· Maintain accurate and timely case notes, task updates, documentation, delivery confirmations, and supporting records in applicable systems.

· Verify that required records and assets have transferred, document outstanding or trailing items, and complete or recommend operational case closure in accordance with established procedures and approval requirements.

· Participate in ongoing cross-training across deconversion and conversion processes and provide support for incoming plan transfers, conversions, and related team responsibilities as business needs and workload require.

· Complete work in accordance with approved SOPs, templates, checklists, quality standards, privacy requirements, and information-security requirements.

· Handle participant, plan, financial, and transfer data in accordance with applicable privacy, information-security, file-transfer, access-control, and records-retention requirements.

· Contribute feedback that supports process consistency, workflow improvements, and operational initiatives.

· Support additional projects, process initiatives, and related responsibilities as business needs and operational priorities evolve.

Skills & Abilities

· Working knowledge of 401(k) administration, deconversions, outgoing plan transfers, participant records, loans, successor-provider requirements, and asset movement.

· Ability to interpret plan documents, deconversion requests, participant data, final records, transfer documentation, reports, and deadlines.

· Ability to prepare and validate outgoing records and files while protecting data accuracy and maintaining appropriate documentation.

· Ability to identify potential risks, research discrepancies, coordinate resolution, and escalate concerns appropriately.

· Ability to manage multiple assigned exit cases and clearly document requirements, status, risks, owners, and actions.

· Ability to distinguish routine processing issues from matters requiring Compliance, Finance, Trading, relationship-owner, or leadership review.

· Ability to communicate technical requirements and unresolved items clearly to clients, successor providers, and internal partners within established guidelines.

· Ability to manage sensitive participant and financial data using approved transmission, documentation, and information-security practices.

· Ability to reconcile plan-level and participant-level records and document differences, resolution steps, and approvals.

· Ability to prioritize competing deadlines involving notices, liquidation dates, outgoing files, transfers, and residual-asset activity.

· Strong attention to detail, organization, follow-through, problem-solving, and collaboration skills.

· Proficiency with Salesforce, Relius, IQ, Excel, Adobe, provider portals, and internal tools.

Experience

· 2-4 years of relevant 401(k), retirement plan administration, recordkeeping, deconversions, plan exits, plan transfers, or related financial services experience preferred.

· Experience reviewing plan documents, participant data, transfer documentation, outgoing files, asset activity, and final records preferred.

· Ability to research operational issues, manage multiple priorities, coordinate across teams, and escalate complex concerns appropriately.

· Experience supporting retirement plan deconversion, termination, or outgoing transfer projects preferred.

Education

· Bachelor's degree in Business, Finance, Accounting, or related field preferred; equivalent relevant experience accepted.

WE serve the individual saver and investor, know that their savings represents not only money, but the time it took to earn that money, which is forever gone. WE will prudently, cost-effectively and efficiently safeguard and invest that money for a better future for all we serve.

title: Instrumentation and Controls Technician
description:
We are Proud to be SJE!

At SJE, we are more than a company — we are a family of brands with a shared vision and mission to provide industry-leading, innovative, and reliable control and monitoring solutions that improve efficiencies, protect the environment, and deliver dependable solutions to our valued customers. We are looking for an Instrumentation and Controls Technician to support our engineered brands. This role will work out of our Lee, NH location.

The job:

As our Instrumentation and Controls Technician, you will provide hands-on electrical and automation support to customers, including troubleshooting, installation, calibration, commissioning, and maintenance of industrial control systems. You will work directly with customers to diagnose and resolve equipment issues, perform system testing, and ensure electrical and instrumentation components operate safely, reliably, and efficiently.

In this role, you will troubleshoot PLC-based control systems, perform instrumentation calibration and loop checks, and conduct functional testing of electrical and automation equipment. You will interpret and update electrical schematics, control panel drawings, and P&IDs while inspecting electrical connections, instrumentation, and motor control equipment. You will also install and replace control panels, field instrumentation, conduit, wiring, and related electrical components. When field service work is not scheduled, you will support shop operations by assisting with the assembly, wiring, and testing of industrial control panels. Additionally, you will support system startups, preventative maintenance, and ongoing service activities while collaborating with customers and internal teams to resolve technical challenges.

The skills, education, and experience you need:

To succeed in this role, you must have experience with:

  • Troubleshooting, testing, calibrating, and maintaining industrial instrumentation and electrical control systems.

  • Working with PLC-based control systems, including input/output signals, loop checks, and functional testing.

  • Reading, interpreting, and updating electrical schematics, control panel drawings, and piping and instrumentation diagrams (P&IDs).

  • Using electrical testing equipment, field metering devices, and instrumentation calibration tools.

  • Understanding electrical control panels, motor control centers (MCCs), and associated electrical components.

  • Installing, troubleshooting, and replacing field instrumentation, electrical control equipment, conduit, and wiring.

  • Assembling, wiring, and testing industrial electrical control panels using electrical drawings and wiring schematics.

  • Working safely around industrial electrical equipment and various voltage levels, including low- and high-voltage systems.

  • Performing equipment startups, commissioning, preventative maintenance, and troubleshooting of existing systems.

  • Understanding industrial processes and the interaction between field instrumentation, electrical equipment, and automation systems.

  • Strong troubleshooting, problem-solving, communication, and customer service skills.

  • Ability to work independently in the field and collaboratively with shop personnel and internal technical teams.

Answering your questions:

When you are considering a new job, it is normal to have a ton of questions. Here are a few questions we are asked all the time.

  • What is your Paid Time Off and holiday policy? Up to 120 hours of Paid Time Off in your first year plus 8 paid holidays.
  • What benefits do you offer? We offer a robust benefits package including health, life, short-term and long-term disability insurance as well as dental and vision programs you need to take care of your family, along with other benefit options. Check out our full benefits package!
  • What is my commute? Plug this address into Google Maps: 19 Calef Hwy, Lee, NH 03861.

We will answer more of your questions during the first interview. Expect to hear about the next steps if you meet the job requirements.

Why Work With Us
At SJE, we believe in empowering our employees to grow professionally while making a real impact. We offer competitive pay, excellent benefits, and a collaborative culture that encourages creativity and problem-solving. Join us and become a part of something bigger. Join a company where you’re not just working—you’re building a legacy!

title: Admission Counselor
description:
Under the general direction of the Director of Admission, the full-time Admission Counselor position is responsible for recruiting new students to meet the enrollment goals of the college and assisting in the development and implementation of effective strategies that result in the successful recruitment and retention of prospective students.

Essential Duties include the following. Other duties may be assigned.

Student Recruitment (85%)
  • Develop and implement strategies to recruit undergraduate students from assigned geographic territory or population (requires 8 – 12 weeks of regional overnight travel in the fall and 2 – 4 weeks of travel in the spring). Activities include: analysis of past enrollment trends and current projections regarding regions likely to result in increased student enrollment; independently schedule travel and coordinate with recruitment contacts; efficiently plan high school visits and college fair coverage; coordinate with other staff members for fair or high school visit coverage by staff or alumnae, as needed;
  • Develop and implement specific recruitment events in the territory that might include coffee house events, special panel sessions at high schools, talks with honor societies and other high school organizations;
  • Establish and maintain relationships with students, parents, and guidance counselors through travel, e-mail, correspondence, and telephone contact; perform comprehensive follow-up on prospective students, interview prospective students (may require evening hours);
  • Analyze qualifications of prospective students utilizing established admission standards, guidelines and criteria; making recommendations regarding admission decisions and scholarship eligibility for students from assigned territory or population;
  • Provide presentations to groups of varying sizes regarding the admission process, Hood College’s academic and extracurricular offerings, financial aid, and other related topics.
  • Provide detailed assistance for admitted students, including follow-up on financial aid, housing, registration and advising appointments, summer orientation, and all other issues.
General Admission Office Duties (15%)
  • Participate in special admission events (requires evening and weekend hours);
  • Participate in regular admission and enrollment division meetings and assist with daily office functions as necessary;

  • Participate in training and other professional development activities;

title: Shipper Receiver KC - Nights
description:
Shift: D2 -Shift Hours: Wed 11:59pm-6a, Thu-Sat 6p-6a

Operates an industrial sized forklift to receive and transfer product, supplies, and materials to appropriate area while meeting customer regulations and specifications.

ESSENTIAL POSITION RESPONSIBILITIES

Operator is responsible for storing and retrieving goods in the storage area of the workplace. Rotates stock so oldest materials are used first. Notes and reports any damaged cartons, crates or containers. Records items added or removed from inventory.

Prepares products for shipment by retrieving designated products and ensuring it is properly loaded and sealed correctly.

Stores product by using an industrial forklift and uses a hand held scan gun/RFGEN for lot tracking to maintain accurate inventory. Working from written or verbal instructions by operating a forklift to pick up, move, load and unload product on, or from trailers while meeting department, facility, company, and regulatory guidelines.

Performs minor service of equipment and completes written daily safety inspections. Identifies and reports noted problems to the supervisor for further inspection and repair.

Responsible for changing batteries or fuel bottles, refueling forklift or troubleshooting repairs as needed.

Maintains the work area, dock and equipment in a clean and orderly condition, adheres to storage design principles, and recommends improvement.

Creates product labels for inventory purposes. Reads and understands lot numbers, expiration dates, ingredient lists, and production schedules. Completes various reports daily and enters required information into computer program efficiently and timely.

Responsible for using basic tools such as wrenches, tape measures, scales, air and water hoses. Consolidates partial pallets as directed by the production supervisor.

Operators must be able to maneuver forklift in tight spaces, while maintaining a safe work zone for other drivers and team members.

Participates as a member of the Team. Participates in ongoing development, communication and implementation of team concepts, programs and policies; coordinates work to ensure B.E.S.T practices with all team members. Attends appropriate team meetings. As a member of the Team, fosters strong cohesiveness regarding all major issues; e.g., direction, annual plan, budget, policy changes, etc. Accepts responsibility to quickly identify any areas that lack cohesiveness, bringing them to the attention of the team leader and working with the team in a supportive manner to resolve issues and actively look for ways, and reinforces actions needed, to achieve synergy possible within the larger organization.

Simmons Operating systems principles and objectives: Is familiar with Simmons’ established operating systems (e.g. quality, security, office environment, company policies); understands the responsibility to maintain familiarity with the systems and this position’s role in support of these systems - including a consideration of the impact of individual actions on the systems and the responsibility to communicate concerns and improvement ideas.

Performs other duties as necessary in support of business objectives: This position description is intended to guide the activities of the Shipper/Receiver and is not intended to limit the thinking and creativity of the person to the work of this function nor is it intended that this describe all the work that may be required of the person in this position.

Physical Activities: Must be able to climb on and off of the forklift; must be able to back fork-lift up safely which requires turning the neck and body in the opposite direction. Must be able to lift and stack up to 75 lbs from floor to crown, will be required to work in extreme temperatures both hot and cold, wet, dry, dusty environment. Must be able to sit and walk for long periods of time, lift up to 75 pounds multiple times daily, work in temperature extremes.

Personal Protective Equipment (PPE): Safety Glasses, Rubber Gloves, Rubber boots, Rubber Apron, Hearing Protection, and any other PPE as required in appropriate area.

Technical Experience: Knowledge of Julian calendar, FIFO practices, preferred experience in shipping and receiving, working with large moving equipment. Basic computer literacy. Knowledge of military time, RFGEN and JDE.

Industry Experience: Shipping and receiving knowledge preferred.

Minimum Education: High School Diploma or Equivalent. Perform basic math. Must be able to obtain and maintain a company issued forklift license. Must be able to read, write and understand English

title: Connectivity Platform Team Lead
description:
Call to action

Are you ready to unlock your potential? At Straumann Group we’re on an exciting journey of growth, innovation, and impact - driven by our mission to improve oral health and transform millions of lives worldwide. United by purpose, we bring our best selves to work every day, embracing a high-performance, player-learner culture that inspires collaboration, curiosity, and ambition. Here, you’ll have the opportunity to take charge of your own career, harnessing your skills, passion, and enthusiasm for learning to continually grow and progress. Together, we’re not just shaping brighter smiles, we’re unlocking the potential of people everywhere, including our own.

Intro

As Connectivity Platform Team Leader, you will guide the engineering, operation, and continuous improvement of secure, scalable, and resilient enterprise connectivity services across on-premises and hybrid cloud environments.

You will work closely with Enterprise Architecture, Cloud, Cybersecurity, and Platform Engineering teams to strengthen platform availability, security, automation, and operational excellence. This is a key leadership role for someone who enjoys combining technical depth with people leadership, stakeholder partnership, and practical delivery.

Your Role:

  • You will lead and develop a team of connectivity platform engineers, setting clear priorities, supporting performance, and enabling professional growth.
  • You will oversee the engineering, operation, lifecycle management, and continuous improvement of enterprise connectivity services across on-premises and hybrid cloud environments.
  • You will help ensure platform availability, resilience, security, performance, disaster recovery readiness, and effective incident response.
  • You will drive modernization, standardization, automation, and Infrastructure as Code practices using tools such as Terraform, Bicep, CloudFormation, Ansible, or similar technologies.
  • You will support CI/CD pipelines, scripting, and automation to improve efficiency and reliability.
  • You will collaborate with cybersecurity teams on governance, policy enforcement, identity management, vulnerability remediation, and compliance with relevant standards.
  • You will partner with application teams, enterprise architects, vendors, and technology partners to align connectivity services with business and digital transformation needs.
  • You will monitor connectivity consumption, support budgeting and capacity forecasting, and identify opportunities for cost optimization.

Your Profile:

  • You bring experience in enterprise networking, connectivity services, cloud connectivity, network security, and platform automation.
  • You have experience leading or coordinating technical teams, including coaching, prioritization, and stakeholder communication.
  • You are confident working across hybrid cloud and enterprise technology environments.
  • You have hands-on experience with relevant technologies such as Azure, AWS, Cisco networking, Terraform, Ansible, Python, Git, and Azure DevOps, or comparable tools.
  • You communicate complex technical topics clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.
  • A degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or a related field is helpful; equivalent practical experience is also valued.

What Makes You a Great Fit

  • You combine technical expertise with a collaborative leadership style.
  • You bring structure to complex environments and help teams focus on practical, secure, and scalable solutions.
  • You are comfortable balancing strategic planning with hands-on delivery.
  • You build trust with stakeholders, encourage continuous improvement, and support others to do their best work.
  • You are motivated by creating reliable platforms that enable teams across the business to move faster and work more effectively.

Beyond the day job, you’ll connect with others through graduate networks, diversity groups and social clubs that make your time at CGI both rewarding and enjoyable.

Together, as owners, let’s turn meaningful insights into action.

Your work creates value. You’ll develop innovative solutions and build relationships with teammates and clients while accessing global capabilities to scale your ideas, embrace new opportunities, and benefit from expansive industry and technology expertise.

You’ll shape your career by joining a company built to grow and last. You’ll be supported by leaders who care about your health and well-being and provide you with opportunities to deepen your skills and broaden your horizons.

title: Card Specialist I
description:

Key responsibilities include resolving member inquiries, managing card statuses and orders, detecting and preventing fraud, performing file maintenance, processing member requests through workflow systems, handling account adjustments and reconciliations, and performing other critical tasks essential to the success of our card programs.

Why Join SCCU?

  • Hybrid & Flexible Schedule Options
  • Career Growth: We prioritize internal promotions and offer on-the-job training.

Card Specialist I Responsibilities

  • Provides phone support in our General Servicing queue to front-line team members and other departments across the organization that require department-specific assistance, and assist members directly when appropriate.
  • Processes all general servicing debit and credit card requests submitted via various department workflows.
  • Verifies, reviews, and takes appropriate action(s) on automated member debit and credit fraud alerts.
  • Assists with concerns regarding various debit and credit card statuses; such as activations, blocks, and restrictions.
  • Assists with debit and credit card orders; such as new cards, replacement cards, tracking information, and any other aspects pertaining to card orders.
  • Assists with card production documentation, card inventory, supply management, and recurring machine maintenance critical to production operations.

Card Specialist I Minimum Requirements

  • 1 to 12 months of prior experience in credit and debit card services or a similar field preferred.
  • High school diploma or equivalent required.

Card Specialist I Compensation

  • Starting Salary: $17.91 - $18.97/hour or $37,250 - $39,460/year
  • Bonus Opportunity: Eligible for ONE SCCU Annual Bonus.

Work Schedule

  • Monday – Friday: 8:00 a.m. - 7:00 p.m.
  • Rotating Saturdays: 9:00 a.m. - 3:00 p.m.

SCCU Benefits

  • Health & Wellness: Medical, dental, and vision insurance, plus an Employee Assistance Program.

  • Generous Time Off: 20+ days of PTO, birthday PTO, and 11 federal holidays.

About SCCU

Since 1951, Space Coast Credit Union (SCCU) has proudly served our community, growing to over 685,000 members and managing $9 billion in assets.
