title: Salesforce QA Consultant - 4-Month Contract | Remote | Immediate Hiring
description:
About the Role

We are looking for a Senior QA Engineer with strong hands-on Salesforce experience to join our growing team on a 4-month remote contract.

In this role, you will be responsible for ensuring the quality, reliability, and functionality of Salesforce-based solutions throughout the software development lifecycle. You will work closely with developers, Salesforce teams, product owners, and other stakeholders to drive both manual and automated testing efforts and ensure that Salesforce implementations meet business and technical requirements.

Salesforce experience is a must-have for this role.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to ensure quality throughout the Salesforce development lifecycle.
  • Design, develop, and execute comprehensive test cases and test scenarios for Salesforce applications and solutions.
  • Perform functional, integration, regression, system, and end-to-end testing across Salesforce environments.
  • Design, implement, and maintain automated test suites for Salesforce-based applications.
  • Validate Salesforce configurations, customizations, integrations, workflows, and business processes against functional and technical requirements.
  • Review business and technical requirements to ensure consistency, completeness, and testability.
  • Identify, document, track, and verify Salesforce-related defects through to resolution.
  • Test integrations between Salesforce and external systems and validate data flow and system behavior.
  • Perform regression testing following Salesforce releases, configuration changes, and new feature implementations.
  • Conduct post-release and post-implementation testing to ensure product stability and quality.
  • Work closely with Salesforce developers, administrators, product owners, and business stakeholders to identify and resolve quality issues.
  • Contribute to improving QA processes, test strategies, and automation coverage.
  • Suggest product and functionality improvements based on usability, quality, and customer experience standards.
  • Support UAT activities and ensure business requirements are properly validated before release.

Requirements

  • 7+ years of progressive experience in Software Quality Assurance/Quality Control, with at least 2 years in a Senior or Lead QA role.
  • Strong hands-on experience testing Salesforce applications and solutions is a MUST.
  • Proven experience with Salesforce testing, including functional, integration, regression, system, and end-to-end testing.
  • Strong understanding of Salesforce functionality, configurations, customizations, and integrations from a QA/testing perspective.
  • Proven expertise in both manual and automated testing, including hands-on experience with automation frameworks.
  • Experience designing and executing detailed test plans, test cases, test scenarios, and regression suites for complex software systems.
  • Experience testing integrations between Salesforce and external applications or systems.
  • Strong track record of identifying, isolating, and documenting critical bugs and edge cases, with a high level of attention to detail.
  • Experience leading and mentoring QA teams and managing quality processes in Agile or hybrid development environments.
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to translate technical findings into clear business impact.
  • Proficiency with bug tracking and test management tools.
  • Experience working with CI/CD environments and understanding of software release processes is a plus.
  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

title: IT Technical Analyst
description:
Build What Matters Most—Families, Futures, and Your Career

Enjoy meaningful work while contributing to an organization that changes lives every day. US Fertility, the nation’s leading partnership of physician-led fertility practices, is redefining what it means to build a career in reproductive medicine.

Our team members choose to build their career home at US Fertility because of the hope we inspire in our patients, the lives we help bring into the world, and the culture of excellence we foster across our organization. We share a deep commitment to continuously improving the patient experience and advancing research and development in one of the most dynamic and impactful fields of medicine.

Through our national network of premier fertility centers we combine clinical expertise, scientific innovation, and compassionate care. The work we do building families offers purpose, challenge, and personal reward—and we’re just getting started.

Opportunity Overview

We have an immediate opening for an IT Technical Analyst to join our team at US Fertility. This is a hybrid position that combines remote work with in-office support, requiring up to three days per week onsite within an assigned territory. The territory covers our Rockville, Maryland office and locations throughout Northern Virginia and south to Fredericksburg, Virginia.

  • Schedule: Monday through Friday, from 7:00 AM to 4:00PM or 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM Eastern Time; Weekend rotation every 15 weeks
  • Compensation: $55,000 to $60,000 (commensurate with experience)
  • Travel: Up to 25% to other US Fertility locations outside the primary territory, as needed

This role provides the opportunity to grow within a nationally respected organization while remaining closely connected to the patients and teams you support every day.

How You’ll Contribute

At US Fertility, collaboration is fundamental to how we work. There is undeniable strength in numbers—and support is always within reach. Whether collaborating with more than 200 highly respected physicians nationwide or partnering with colleagues who are passionate about solving meaningful problems, you’ll be surrounded by a team committed to shared success.

In this role, the IT Technical Analyst will:

  • Provide onsite and field technical support across US Fertility clinics and administrative offices, with regular travel to locations throughout Rockville, MD, Northern Virginia, and Fredericksburg, VA
  • Maintain proximity within a reasonable driving distance to the Rockville, MD hub and regional clinic locations to support timely onsite service
  • Troubleshoot and resolve escalated hardware, software, network, and system configuration issues
  • Support endpoint domain migrations, equipment replacements, and infrastructure maintenance
  • Provision, configure, deploy, and maintain laptops, desktops, mobile devices, peripherals, and clinical technology
  • Serve as the primary escalation point for complex Tier 1 service desk issues
  • Partner with MSP, infrastructure, systems engineering, and clinic teams to minimize technical and clinical downtime
  • Diagnose recurring technical issues and identify opportunities for process and system improvements
  • Maintain accurate ticket documentation and develop knowledge base resources for technical support
  • Provide clear, responsive technical support and onboarding assistance to physicians, clinical staff, and administrative personnel
  • Protect confidential company and user information while adhering to security standards and company policies
  • Maintain current technical knowledge and stay informed on industry technologies and best practices
  • Provide onsite support at additional locations as needed to support business operations

What You’ll Bring

We’re looking for professionals who bring both technical skill and a deep sense of responsibility to the care experience—individuals who thrive in environments where excellence, empathy, and accountability matter.

Qualifications and Skills Include:

  • Reside within commuting distance of the I-270/I-95 corridor, supporting clinic locations from Rockville, MD to Fredericksburg, VA
  • 3 to 5 years of progressive experience in IT service desk, desktop support, or Tier 2 technical support; healthcare IT experience strongly preferred
  • Advanced troubleshooting skills with Windows 10/11 and Microsoft 365 applications
  • Experience managing users, groups, and permissions in Active Directory and Entra ID/Azure AD
  • Hands-on experience with Microsoft Intune, SCCM, or similar endpoint/MDM management tools
  • Working knowledge of TCP/IP, DNS, DHCP, VPN, Wi-Fi, and basic switch/router troubleshooting
  • Experience using IT service management platforms such as ServiceNow, Freshdesk, or Jira Service Management
  • Valid driver’s license, reliable transportation, and willingness to travel regularly to local and regional clinic locations
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills with the ability to explain technical concepts clearly to non-technical users
  • ITIL 4 Foundation, CompTIA A+, Network+, or Microsoft Certified: Modern Desktop Administrator
  • Experience working with third-party MSPs and familiarity with HIPAA requirements and healthcare clinical environments

More important than any single credential, however, is the right person. Team members who are most successful at US Fertility embrace our mission, live our values, and remain committed to continuous improvement—for themselves, their colleagues, and the patients we serve.

What We Offer

US Fertility is proud to provide a competitive, comprehensive benefits package designed to support our team members—professionally and personally—across all employment types.

Full-Time Employees (30+ hours/week)

  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance
  • 401(k) with company match
  • Tuition assistance and professional development support
  • Performance-based bonus opportunities
  • Generous paid time off, paid holidays, and paid parental leave
  • Life and disability benefits
  • Fertility Discount Program
  • Employee wellness and recognition programs

Part-Time Employees

  • 401(k) with company match
  • Performance-based bonus opportunities
  • Employee wellness and recognition programs

Per Diem Employees

  • 401(k) with company match
  • Employee wellness and recognition programs

Our Commitment to Inclusion and Opportunity

US Fertility and its network partners believe that a diverse workforce is essential to fulfilling our mission of expanding patient access to the highest standards of fertility care. We are committed to equitable and inclusive hiring practices that ensure our clinical and operational teams reflect and support the diverse communities and patients we serve.

Across our national footprint, US Fertility is a leader in offering clinical, administrative, and operational career opportunities at locations throughout the United States. We are equally committed to developing individual strengths, promoting from within, and supporting long-term career growth.

This is a moment of growth, innovation, and impact. Take the next step in your career with US Fertility—and help shape the future of fertility care.

title: Training Specialist II
description:
Job Summary:

The Training Specialist II designs, delivers, and evaluates training that helps credit union staff serve members well and stay compliant. The role covers the full training cycle (needs analysis, design, delivery, and measurement) for new hire onboarding, member service, systems, lending, and regulatory compliance. The role delivers training in person, virtually, and through e-learning. The Training Specialist II also administers the Learning Management System (LMS) and keeps training records audit-ready. The role also serves as the training lead on organizational projects and creates, updates, tests, and delivers launch-ready training content. The role works closely with the Director of Training, department leaders, project teams, and subject matter experts.

Duties & Responsibilities:

Training Needs and Design

  • Collaborates with department leaders to identify skill gaps and training needs using surveys, observations, quality and audit findings, and performance data.
  • Designs and develops instructor-led, virtual, and e-learning content using adult learning principles and a structured model such as ADDIE. Content includes facilitator guides, participant workbooks, job aids, presentations, videos, and assessments.
  • Builds e-learning modules with authoring tools (for example, Articulate 360 or similar).

Delivery

  • Facilitates engaging training sessions in person and virtually for new hires and existing staff on member service, products, core and digital banking systems, lending, and operations.
  • Delivers and tracks required annual and department-specific compliance training (for example, BSA/AML, OFAC, Regulation E, Regulation CC, fair lending, privacy, and information security) in partnership with the Compliance department.
  • Leads or supports onboarding programs, including new hire orientation and role-based training for branch and contact center staff.
  • Trains staff on new products, system upgrades, and policy or procedure changes as they roll out.
  • Coordinates third-party vendor training as a follow-up to core training, including serving as the main vendor contact, scheduling sessions, and tracking attendance and completion.

LMS Administration and Records

  • Administers the LMS: uploads and updates courses, assigns curricula, manages enrollments, and runs completion and compliance reports.
  • Maintains accurate, audit-ready training records for regulatory examinations and internal audit.

Evaluation and Improvement

  • Measures training effectiveness using learner feedback, assessments, and performance or business results to help department leaders determine skill gaps and training needs.
  • Conducts quarterly branch exchange days to evaluate training effectiveness in the live environment. During visits, observes new learners to confirm training is applied on the job, provides follow-up coaching, and observes new or changed processes in the live core system so training content stays current.
  • Keeps training manuals, job aids, and the resource library current.
  • Recommends updates to operational policies and procedures when training reveals gaps or unclear guidance.

Organizational Projects

  • Serves as the lead trainer on organizational projects such as system conversions, core and digital banking upgrades, new product launches, and process or policy changes.
  • Attends project meetings, reviews requirements and workflows, and assesses the training impact on affected staff.
  • Creates and updates training content (courses, job aids, guides, and e-learning) to reflect new or changed systems, products, and procedures.
  • Tests training content and system procedures in test environments before rollout, working with project teams and subject matter experts to confirm accuracy.
  • Delivers launch-ready training on the project timeline so staff are prepared on go-live day and provides refresher training and support.

Program Support

  • Helps prepare and maintain the Training and Development calendar.
  • Supports planning and running large events and meetings.
  • Supports member financial education and volunteer training as assigned.
  • Coaches and supports peer trainers and subject matter experts who deliver training.
  • Performs other duties as assigned.
Skills and Abilities:

  • Ability to lead the full training cycle, from needs analysis through evaluation.
  • Knowledge of adult learning principles and instructional design models (ADDIE, SAM).
  • Strong facilitation and presentation skills for small and large groups, in person and virtual (Teams, Zoom).
  • Clear writing for manuals, job aids, scripts, and e-learning.
  • Working knowledge of credit union products, services, and key regulations (BSA/AML, OFAC, Reg E, Reg CC, privacy), or ability to learn quickly.
  • Ability to measure training results and use data to improve programs.
  • Strong organization and project management; manages multiple projects and deadlines with minimal supervision.
  • Sound judgment, problem-solving, and attention to detail.
  • Build productive relationships with leaders, subject matter experts, and learners at all levels.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office 365 (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Teams) and an LMS.

title: Global Business Insights Analyst
description:
The Straumann Group is a global leader in the field of aesthetic dentistry. We combine expertise, scientific evidence, and innovation with passion, committing to uncompromising quality to provide dentists and patients worldwide with the best possible solutions. As pioneers and market leaders in dental implantology, we have consistently expanded our product portfolio in recent years. Today, we operate in all areas of aesthetic dentistry: from tooth preservation, regeneration, restoration, orthodontics with transparent aligner trays to tooth loss solutions.

The Business Insights Analyst plays a pivotal role in turning customer, market, and business data into insights that accelerate innovation and support sustainable growth within the Straumann Implantology Business Unit. The role owns the development and delivery of customer and market insights, from identifying and managing relevant data sources to translating complex analyses into clear recommendations and measurable business actions. Acting as a strategic partner to senior stakeholders and Product Management, the Business Insights Analyst enables confident, evidence-based decision-making across key business initiatives. Success in this role requires strong analytical expertise, sound business and industry understanding, and the ability to connect cross-functional teams, challenge perspectives, and turn business questions into practical, actionable solutions.


Your responsibilities:

  • Shape and drive the business intelligence and analytics agenda for the Straumann Implantology Business Unit, aligned with strategic priorities and business needs.
  • Act as a trusted business partner to Product Management and other senior stakeholders, using data and market insights to support strategic decisions, identify growth opportunities, and address business challenges.
  • Lead stakeholder engagements to understand business objectives, pain points, and information needs, and build alignment on analytical priorities and expected outcomes.
  • Translate complex business questions into clearly defined analytical objectives, use cases, requirements, KPIs, success criteria, and actionable recommendations.
  • Drive end-to-end analytical projects, from framing the business problem and sourcing the data through to analysis, solution development, stakeholder adoption, and impact measurement.
  • Identify and combine relevant internal and external data sources, and conduct analyses to uncover trends, risks, opportunities, and actionable business insights.
  • Establish KPI frameworks, measurement concepts, business rules, and reporting standards to support consistent and meaningful performance management.
  • Design and deliver executive-ready reports, dashboards, visualizations, and management presentations tailored to different stakeholder groups.
  • Ensure the quality, consistency, usability, and appropriate interpretation of analytical outputs, collaborating with data owners, IT, and technical experts where required.
  • Promote data-driven decision-making by communicating complex findings clearly, challenging assumptions constructively, and influencing stakeholders at different levels.
  • Identify opportunities to standardize, simplify, and automate processes
  • Build Product Managers’ data and analytics capabilities through coaching, training, and knowledge-sharing.


Your Profile - Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s or master’s degree in computer science, economics, business administration, data analytics, or a related field.
  • At least five years of relevant experience in business analysis, business intelligence, data analytics, or a related discipline; experience in healthcare, dental, medtech is preferred.
  • Proven experience partnering with business stakeholders to understand objectives, define analytical requirements, establish KPIs, and translate business questions into actionable insights.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to identify trends, assess business performance, challenge assumptions, and communicate clear recommendations.
  • Proficiency in developing and delivering reports, dashboards, data visualizations, and experience in management presentations.
  • Ability to translate business requirements into clear functional, analytical, data, and technical requirements, and to align stakeholders on expected outcomes and success criteria.
  • Proficiency working with data from multiple sources including extraction, transformation, validation, and preparation for analysis and reporting.
  • Understanding of ETL processes, data models, data quality, and data governance, with the ability to collaborate effectively with data engineers, IT, and data owners.
  • Proficiency in relevant analytics tools, particularly SAP BW, Snowflake, SQL, AWS, Power BI, and advanced Excel. Familiarity with Python is a plus.
  • Experience managing analytical projects from business problem definition through solution development, stakeholder adoption, and impact measurement.

Additional Qualifications:

  • Experience in Voice of Customer (VOC) methodologies and tools is a plus.
  • Innovative mindset with eagerness to learn and adapt to new technologies and methodologies in the field of data analytics and business intelligence.
  • Open-minded and proactive personality with the ability to cultivate effective working relationships in an international matrix environment as well as to motivate and engage stakeholders.
  • Fluent in English; proficiency in other languages is an asset.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, or disability.

title: Director, Frontier
description:
Presidio, Where Teamwork and Innovation Shape the Future
At Presidio, we're at the forefront of a global technology revolution, transforming industries through cutting-edge digital solutions and next-generation AI. We empower businesses - and their internal customers - to achieve more through innovation, automation, and intelligent insights.

The Role

As Director, Frontier, you will build Presidio's partnerships with the companies shaping the next era of enterprise AI, with partners like NVIDIA, OpenAI, Anthropic and SpaceXAI. These are the partnerships we expect to grow into some of Presidio's largest, and you will lead the team that takes them there.
You will bring Presidio's consulting, services and infrastructure capabilities together with each partner's technology, build joint offers our sellers can take to customers, and land the first wins that show the market what we can do together. Then you will scale them into repeatable, growing businesses.
This is a builder's role with a clear focus on results. You will turn new partnerships into pipeline, customer wins and revenue, and use data to guide where Presidio invests next.


What you will own:
• Frontier partner strategy. Build and own the plan for each partner: where Presidio can win, which joint offers to build, which customers to pursue first and what it will take to get there.
• Senior partner relationships. Serve as Presidio's senior relationship owner with each Frontier partner, and build strong alignment between partner leadership and Presidio's senior leaders.
• Joint offers. Work with Presidio's Consulting and AI Platforms, AI strategy and practice leaders to build offers that combine partner technology with Presidio's consulting, services and infrastructure.
• First wins. Run focused pursuits with Presidio account teams to create early, referenceable customer wins, then turn them into repeatable plays.
• Smart investment. Guide where Presidio invests in capability, certifications and joint offers, secure partner investment, and tie each investment to clear milestones and return.
• Connecting across our partner ecosystem. Work with Presidio's partnership leaders for our largest technology partners where solutions come together, such as AI infrastructure built with NVIDIA on Dell or Cisco.
• The joint value story. Give Presidio sellers a clear, compelling story for why Presidio and the partner win together, and make sure they can put it to work with customers.
• Path to scale. Build the business case and track record to grow each partnership from first wins to repeatable offers to one of Presidio's largest partnerships.

Required:
• 5+ years in technology sales, alliances, partner management or business development, including building new partnerships or new businesses from the ground up
• A record of turning early partnerships or new offers into revenue
• A strong grasp of how enterprises are adopting AI and where infrastructure, platforms and services create value
• Executive presence and credibility with partner executives and Presidio senior leaders
• Strong business acumen across revenue, pipeline, investment cases and return
• Energized by building something new, and decisive about where to focus
• Ability to lead through influence across practices, sales teams and partners
• Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience


Preferred:
• Experience at, or partnering closely with, NVIDIA or a frontier AI company
• Experience building joint offers with a consulting or services organization
• Hands-on use of AI tools in your day-to-day work


Reporting and location:
• Reports to: SVP, Strategic Alliances
• Scope: Frontier AI partners like NVIDIA, OpenAI, Anthropic and SpaceXAI
• Location: Remote or hybrid, with regular time at partner and Presidio offices
• Travel: Approximately 30 to 40 percent, including partner executive meetings, AI industry events, customer pursuits and field events

Your future at Presidio
Joining Presidio means stepping into a culture of trailblazers - thinkers, builders, and collaborators - who push the boundaries of what's possible. With our expertise AI-driven analytics, cloud solutions, cybersecurity, and next-gen infrastructure, we enable businesses to stay ahead in an ever-evolving digital world.

Here, your impact is real. Whether you're harnessing the power of Generative AI, architecting resilient digital ecosystems, or driving data-driven transformation, you'll be part of a team that is shaping the future.

Ready to innovate? Let's redefine what's next-together.

About Presidio
Presidio is committed to hiring the most qualified candidates to join our amazing culture. We aim to attract and hire top talent from all backgrounds, including underrepresented and marginalized communities. title: Commercial Banking Market Manager - Fresno Palm
description:
JOB SUMMARY:

The Commercial Banking Market Manager provides leadership and oversight for Commercial Banking operations within an assigned market. This position is responsible for managing commercial lending and business deposit activities while driving growth, profitability, and client retention. The role leads and develops a team of commercial banking professionals, promotes strong relationship management practices, and ensures the delivery of comprehensive financial solutions that meet the evolving needs of business clients and support the Bank's strategic goals.

RESPONSIBILITIES INCLUDE, BUT ARE NOT LIMITED TO:

  • Lead and develop a team of Commercial Banking professionals through ongoing coaching, performance management, training, and mentorship to support individual growth, portfolio development, and achievement of business objectives.
  • Serve as both a producing manager and market leader by managing an individual portfolio of commercial banking relationships while leading and supporting the commercial banking team in achieving market growth, relationship expansion, and profitability objectives.
  • Participate in workforce planning activities and provide significant input into the recruitment, selection, hiring, and onboarding of Commercial Banking team members.
  • Communicate strategic initiatives, business priorities, and performance expectations to team members while providing leadership and direction to support market growth and client acquisition efforts.
  • Monitor and manage key performance indicators established by Bank leadership, taking appropriate action to drive performance, profitability, and overall market success.
  • Develop and execute strategies to achieve individual and team production goals related to commercial lending, business deposits, and overall relationship growth.
  • Promote the delivery of comprehensive banking solutions by identifying opportunities and facilitating referrals to Retail Branches, Treasury Management, Mortgage Warehouse, Merchant Services, and other business lines as appropriate.
  • Manage portfolio performance and profitability by maintaining strong credit quality, relationship returns, and risk management practices consistent with Bank objectives.
  • Establish and maintain a structured calling program focused on acquiring new relationships, strengthening existing client relationships, and expanding wallet share within the assigned market.
  • Maintain oversight of prospect and client pipelines to ensure continuous business development activity and effective management of growth opportunities.
  • Structure, negotiate, and recommend commercial loan requests in accordance with established credit policies, procedures, and underwriting standards while delivering responsive solutions that meet client needs.
  • Demonstrate sound credit judgment by working collaboratively with Credit Administration and other internal partners to evaluate risk, establish appropriate loan structures, and ensure prudent pricing and fee practices.
  • Serve as a trusted advisor to business clients by developing a thorough understanding of their financial objectives and delivering customized banking solutions that support long-term success.
  • Collaborate with internal business partners on joint calling efforts and relationship development activities to identify and maximize cross-sell opportunities across the Bank.
  • Represent the Bank within the community through professional associations, civic organizations, industry events, and community involvement activities to strengthen the Bank's presence, enhance referral networks, and develop centers of influence.
  • Ensure all activities are conducted in compliance with applicable laws, regulations, Bank policies, and risk management standards.
  • Additional duties as assigned.

REQUIRED KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITY:

To perform the job successfully, an individual should demonstrate the following competencies:

  • Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with employees, supervisors, executives, and other departments
  • Ability to complete multiple, diverse tasks of differing priorities without close supervision
  • Ability to perform tasks and achieve results with a high degree of accuracy and precision
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with a specific ability to translate complex financial information into an organized and presentable manner
  • Excellent administrative and organizational skills
  • Proficiency in the use and application of Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, and PowerPoint)
  • Ability to work with specific data management software as required
  • Ability to read, analyze, and interpret financial reports and accounting and regulatory documents
  • Ability to respond to common inquiries from regulatory, accounting, and outside loan review agencies
  • Ability to effectively present information to management both verbally and in writing
  • Ability to work with mathematical concepts such as probability and statistical inference
  • Ability to apply concepts such as fractions, percentages, ratios, and proportions to practical situations
  • Ability to define problems, collect data, establish facts, and draw valid conclusions.
  • Ability to interpret a wide variety of technical instructions in mathematical form and deal with several abstract and concrete variables
  • Ability to exemplify Bank of the Sierra values and culture

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE:

A bachelor's degree (BA or BS) from an accredited four-year university or a minimum of five years of related experience in underwriting business and real estate transactions is required. Must display a strong knowledge of the local market, business development capabilities, and be able to work independently and with a team.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS:

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential functions. While performing the duties of the job, the employee is frequently required to sit; use hands to finger, handle, or feel; and talk or hear. The employee is occasionally required to stand, walk, and reach with hands and arms. The employee must frequently lift and/or move up to 10 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, color vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus.

WORK ENVIRONMENT:

This job operates in a professional office environment. This role routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, scanners, filing cabinets, and fax machines. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate. The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential functions.

title: Operator 2 (TEMP-REQ-2026-0199)
description:
Kyocera has a temp-to-hire position for a Operator 2 at our San Diego, CA facility.

Candidates selected for hire will be hired through one of Kyocera’s approved staffing partners.

This position may lead to a direct hire offer with Kyocera International, Inc.

Pay is $19.50 per hour

With nearly 80,000 employees globally, Kyocera is a leading manufacturer of high-tech ceramics in various industries, including aerospace, automotive, medical applications, and semiconductor processing. Our innovative materials are found in everything from smartphones to space shuttles!


Exempt: No
Safety Sensitive: Yes

GENERAL DESCRIPTION OF POSITION
The Operator 2 position is responsible for the proper preparation, cleaning loading, inspection and running of parts in 1-4 production machines with moderate supervision. Works from written instructions, work orders, standard programs, and instructions given by the supervisor or lead.

REQUIREMENTS:

High school diploma or GED Required
1-2 year experience in a machining environment, Machine Technology certificate
Ability to read and comprehend verbal and written instructions in English
Ability to add, subtract, multiply, divide all units of measure including common and decimal fractions
Familiarity with mechanical drawings/blueprints, including GDT
Vision and depth perception suitable for use of handheld inspection tools
Willingness to wear finger cots, masks, and/or clean-room apparel
Ability to either stand or walk for extended periods of shift
Ability to bend, push, pull, reach, grab, turn, twist, and/or stoop
Ability to grab small parts or hand tools with hands
Ability to lift and/or carry up to 30 lbs. depending on the specific function.
Eligible to work in an ITAR environment

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  1. Maintains the flow of production parts into the assigned machine or process. Work can be highly repetitive but requires attention to machines.
  2. Unload ceramic and/or other parts may inspect them to remove and record any defective parts.
  3. Basic computer operation for recording metrics (weight, length, ID, OD, density or counts etc.) Maintain quality tools and accurate record keeping.
  4. Monitors and documents the operation of the assigned machines including periodic watches every 2 hours; performs minor maintenance and reports major repairs needed, to equipment as required.
  5. Properly records information on production as instructed including pass down information. Keeps work area clean, safe, and organized.
  6. Maintains safety and Quality Assurance standards by knowing and applying proper procedures for operating the machines within the department.
  7. Assists with company 5S program and keeps work area clean or spills.
  8. Read handheld measuring instruments properly and support less experienced operators in measurement.
  9. Transport parts to and from machines without damage. Cross train in CMM and other advanced measurement tools.
  10. Complies with applicable requirements of Kyocera International, Inc. policy, including ISO 9000, ISO 14001, ISO18001, ITAR and any other site-specific regulations.
  11. Produce precision parts within the time constraints on the work order/ traveler. Support machinists as needed.
  12. Ability to use G/M codes at the controller to adjust.

Perform any other related duties as required or assigned.

QUALIFICATIONS
To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty mentioned satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required.

PHYSICAL ACTIVITIES
The following physical activities described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions and expectations.

While performing the functions of this job, the employee is continuously required to talk or hear; regularly required to stand, walk, sit, use hands to finger, handle, or feel, reach with hands and arms; occasionally required to climb or balance, stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl.

The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 50 pounds, frequently lift and/or move up to 25 pounds, regularly lift and/or move up to 10 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision.

ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITIONS
The following work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

While performing the functions of this job, the employee is occasionally exposed to work near moving mechanical parts, work in high, precarious places, fumes or airborne particles, toxic or caustic chemicals.

The noise level in the work environment is usually loud.

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION
The above statements are intended to describe the work being performed by people assigned to this job. They are not intended to be an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties and skills required. The duties and responsibilities of this position are subject to change and other duties may be assigned or removed at any time. This position may require exposure to information subject to US Export Control regulations, i.e.: the International Traffic and Arms Regulations (ITAR) or Export Administration Regulations (EAR). All applicants must be US persons within the meaning of US regulations.

Kyocera International, Inc. values diversity in its workforce, and is proud to be an AAP/EEO employer. Human Resources team directly.

title: Rochester MnPRA CPRS
description:
Work where you matter. If you want to make a difference and have impact where you work, THIS is the role for you.

We're looking for YOU, our next Rochester MnPRA CPRS: (This is an on-call position, with the potential to be full time)

Job Summary

The MnPRA CPRS (Certified Peer Recovery Specialist) is responsible for delivering peer recovery support services. The CPRS will host individual meetings with clients focused on education, advocacy, mentorship and, attending groups and meetings in support of recovery.

This is an hourly on-call position, specifically providing one-on-one peer support services. After 90 days of providing peer support services, while consistently billing 32 hours per week, the MnPRA CPRS will be
offered a full-time, benefit eligible position.

Essential Job Duties/Responsibilities:
To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential job duty satisfactorily. The essential functions include the following:

▪ Provide one-on-one peer recovery support with individuals seeking help in maintaining their recovery, helping clients work through any barriers they may be facing.
▪ Develop Recovery Wellness Plan (RWP), upon initial meeting with client(s) and set meaningful, achievable goals. Ensure ongoing visibility of RWP with client care team.
▪ Connect clients with community resources, including treatment programs, housing support, food assistance, and employment services.
Maintain confidentiality and uphold ethical standards in accordance with MnPRA’s Code of Ethics.
▪ Document client interactions, progress, and services provided. A CPRS can bill up to a maximum of 8 units per client (4 hours) in one day.
▪ Document billing services to submit hours to be paid based on billable services provided.
▪ Attend and participate in weekly meetings with your supervisor and weekly Licensed Alcohol and Drug Counselor (LADC) supervision sessions.
▪ Maintain ongoing relationships with treatment centers, withdrawal management facilities, and other community partners.
▪ Perform basic administrative tasks, including email correspondence, documentation management, and report submissions.


Required Skills & Experience (Minimum Qualifications):
▪ High School Diploma or equivalent required.
▪ Must have a CPRS credential in good standing through the Minnesota Certification Board (MCB).
▪ Must abide by Minnesota Certification Board’s (MCB’s) code of ethics with the ability to maintain professional boundaries while providing compassionate peer support.
▪ Excellent in-person communication, relationship management, and interpersonal skills.
▪ Previous experience with electronic health record (EHR) system, such as Credible preferred.
▪ Must have a personal lived experience related to substance use. (Someone who has their own lived experience related to substance use. Having a friend or family member with this experience does not meet this requirement.)
▪ Must be comfortable working with people with life-controlling challenges, including mental health and addiction.
▪ Must have reliable transportation and be able to travel locally to meet clients.

title: Credit Solutions Associate I - Miramar
description:
At Space Coast Credit Union (SCCU), our members are at the heart of everything we do. Since 1951, we’ve been committed to delivering financial services founded on integrity and a people-first philosophy.

As a Credit Solutions Associate in our Miramar Operations Center, you will empower members with knowledge and provides options to bring their past due accounts current in order to preserve and safeguard the credit union from unnecessary loss. Acts as a representative of SCCU, by providing quality service for our members.

Why Join SCCU?

  • Member-Focused Mission: Be part of a not-for-profit organization that reinvests in its members.
  • Flexible Schedule Options: This position is Hybrid with 2 days per week required in office.
  • Career Growth: We prioritize internal promotions and offer on-the-job training.

Credit Solutions Associate Key Responsibilities

  • Provides solutions which will bring past due accounts current, excluding legal and bankrupt accounts, in order to keep delinquent loans to a minimum. Works all loans to include but not limited to consumer, mortgage, and business loans.
  • Accepts all inbound phone calls to the department, makes payment arrangements, transfers payments, and researches past due loan problems. Sends accurate loan error corrections to the Loan Servicing Department.
  • Attempts telephone contact with all past due members (including all co-makers) as presented on the predictive dialer.
  • Provide the member with solutions to delinquency such as a payment plan to bring the loan current, refinance, modification, loan extension, rewrite, short sale, deed- in-lieu or other local programs that may assist them in bringing their loan current during their time of need.
  • Send letters to all member(s) within established department guidelines.
  • Ensures that all work (i.e., phone calls, promises to pay, updates, etc.) is thoroughly documented, using correct action and response codes on the day the action occurs, to maintain accurate records on past due accounts.

Credit Solutions Associate Requirements

  • 1 to 2 years in a consumer debt collections or sales environment. Experience with Vehicle and Mortgage Collections and Loss Mitigation preferred
  • High School Diploma or equivalency required

Credit Solutions Associate Compensation

  • Starting Salary: $22.18 -$23.48/hour
  • Bonus Opportunity: Eligible for ONE SCCU Annual Bonus.

SCCU Benefits

  • Generous Time Off: 20+ days of PTO, birthday PTO, and 11 federal holidays.

Work Schedule:

About SCCU

Since 1951, Space Coast Credit Union (SCCU) has proudly served our community, growing to over 685,000 members and managing $9 billion in assets. With 67 branches spanning Florida’s east coast, we are the third-largest credit union in the state. In 2025, we expanded into Orange County to better serve the growing East Orlando market.

As a not-for-profit financial institution, SCCU is dedicated to putting our members first. While we offer the same financial products—like checking, savings, and loans—our focus remains on empowering our members and supporting their financial well-being. At SCCU, we also prioritize our team members by fostering a supportive and collaborative environment that encourages career growth and development. As we continue to grow, we are seeking talented, member-focused professionals to join our team and help deliver innovative financial solutions and outstanding service.

title: Customer Experience Representative
description:
SUMMARY

The City of Englewood strives to provide excellent customer service to members of the community and the public. The Customer Experience Assistant (CEA) serves as a critical part of the City of Englewood’s Customer Experience Program. They are often the first point of contact, providing direct customer service to community members and the public in person, over the phone, email, and other communication methods. The position provides directional assistance, answers phone calls, and enters information into the city’s Citizen Response platform on the customer’s behalf as necessary. The CEA will search the Citizen Response platform knowledgebase, city website and other sources to provide fast, effective, and accurate information, as well as mail processing/distribution, filing and other office-related tasks. This position also performs specialized clerical work offering passport services by processing and validating passport applications on behalf of the United States Department of State, while collaborating with other certified staff. The position assists staff with administrative tasks within the City Clerk’s Office.

REPORTING RELATIONSHIPS

Reports to: Deputy City Clerk II

Direct Reports: None

ESSENTIAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES

The listed examples of work are not intended to be all-inclusive. They may be modified with additions, deletions, or changes as necessary.

  • Greet community members and the public with professionalism in person, over the phone, and through a variety of online methods.
  • Provide directional assistance, answer general questions, and connect or provides contact information for appropriate city personnel.
  • Search the Citizen Response (My Englewood) platform for answers to common questions/concerns, the city website, and other resources.
  • Ensures sufficient cross training of staff to meet the needs of the City Clerk’s Office.
  • Accepts payments for common city services.
  • Provides quality service and information, both internally and externally.
  • Processes and distributes mail and packages, tracks postage and run reports for departments.
  • Performs all work duties and activities in accordance with City policies and procedures.
  • Establishes and maintains positive working relationships with the public, coworkers and other City employees using principles of exceptional customer service. Tracks the number of visitors to the Civic Center daily.
  • Collects, organizes, and reviews customer comment cards. Performs data collection and entry related to customer requests.
  • Enters information into the City’s Citizen Response platform on the customer’s behalf as necessary.
  • Receives and maintains permanent records according to legal retention policies on behalf of the City Clerk’s Office.
  • Works in collaboration with Public Works to maintain and distribute City vehicle keys.
  • Provides input for improving existing data entry processes or procedures.
  • Receives and processes applications for United States passports. Processes passport applications, including reviewing forms, proof of citizenship, and other controlled records. Reviews information on applications to determine eligibility according to federal laws and the U.S. Department of State’s policies. Queries applicants to obtain additional or clarifying data. Answers questions of individuals concerning passport applications and related services.
  • Provides digital passport photos which meet the requirements of the U.S. Department of State.
  • Collects, posts, and balances monetary transactions daily for Passport Applications.
  • Ensures Passport Applications are delivered by tracking mailed packages via USPS Click n Ship.
  • Assist with Program Improvements. Work with the City Clerk to update Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) on a regular basis. Periodically provide suggested improvements to the Customer Experience Program to the City Clerk.
  • Assists with the agenda, minutes, and scheduling of meetings for Boards and Commissions as needed. Assist the City Clerk’s office with general office duties, tasks, and projects. Completes common office tasks such as filing, data entry, and producing reports. Performs other duties as assigned and required.
  • Other administrative duties as assigned by the City Clerk, including updates to the city website, document integration, and data entry.

EDUCATION

  • High School diploma or GED required. .

RELATED WORK EXPERIENCE

  • Customer service experience. Preference given to candidates with a solid track record of providing top-notch customer service in a variety of settings.

LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS, or CERTIFICATIONS

  • Required Driver’s License

An equivalent combination of education, training and relevant job experience may be substituted.

Passport Acceptance Agent Certificate must be obtained if not currently held within 3 months.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS & ABILITIES

  • Knowledge of customer service standards Microsoft Office suite of products Standard office equipment including copiers, computers, telephones and printers
  • Must be able to multitask and work under pressure with minimal supervision.
  • Intermediate to advanced computer skills in order to search for and find relevant information quickly and effectively, build and update spreadsheets, conduct data entry, compose documents and emails, and troubleshoot common computer issues independently.
  • Superior written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to be empathetic to all customer concerns and questions. Ability to work with staff from various departments, skills and abilities. Advanced active listening skills.

PHYSICAL EXERTION

☐ Exerting up to 20 pounds of force occasionally, and/or up to 10 pounds of force frequently, and/or a negligible amount of force constantly to move objects.

WORKING CONDITIONS

Work is performed in a standard office environment, requiring sitting or standing for extended periods of time, as well as extended computer use and time on a phone. May involve occasional lifting of boxes and other materials weighing over 20 lbs.

Encounters with hazardous conditions (including electrical currents, heavy equipment, fumes, bodily fluids, extreme temperatures, threatening behaviors, inadequate lighting, restricted movement, or intense noise) is:

x Limited (less than 1% of Time)

☐ Seldom (10%-25% of Time)

☐ Frequent (greater than 50% of Time)

☐ Infrequent (1-10% of Time)

☐ Moderate (26%-50% of Time)

HOURLY PAY RANGE

$17.47 - $26.21/Hourly Pay Rate

BENEFITS

The City of Englewood offers a comprehensive benefits package including but not limited to:

  • Medical, Dental, and Vision Plans
  • Retirement Plans
  • Paid Time Off
  • Paid Sick Leave
  • 12 Paid Holidays

More information about our benefits can be found here

APPLICATION DEADLINE

Open until filled.

title: Vice President Growth & Development
description:
Make a Real Difference, Every Single Day

As a nonprofit leader in aging, Eskaton helps people live well, longer — with trusted guidance at every stage. We believe aging should be a vibrant, supported, and celebrated journey, not an experience to face alone. For over 55 years, Eskaton has been a cornerstone of Northern California, growing a network of 23 communities dedicated to older adults and the people who care for them. When you join us, you're not just starting a job. You're stepping into a career where your work creates a real impact on people's daily lives and strengthening the communities we call home.

We Invest in You (Because You Invest in Others)

We know that to take great care of our residents, we must take great care of you. We are genuinely committed to your health, your happiness, and your future. That’s why we offer:

  • Financial Security: Competitive pay and a 401K matching program to help you plan for your own future.
  • Total Wellbeing: Comprehensive benefits that support your physical and mental health.
  • A Place Where You Belong: We celebrate diversity and equity across the entire aging spectrum, ensuring every team member feels seen and valued.

Our DNA (Core Values)

We’re looking for people who align with our mission and want to grow with us. The successful candidate combines enterprise judgment, technical fluency, humility and a growth mindset; translates complexity into clarity; leads through influence; builds trust; and visibly models Eskaton’s core values and high-performance culture:

  • Welcoming: Creates warmth, belonging and psychological safety; listens first, invites diverse perspectives and designs with residents, team members and operational leaders.
  • Bring (Y)our Best: Sets high standards, comes prepared with data and options, communicates clearly and follows through on commitments.
  • Empowerment: Clarifies expectations and decision rights, removes obstacles, shares information and trusts others to own outcomes.
  • Growth: Seeks feedback, learns continuously, adapts, solves problems and raises the bar through measurable improvement.

The Vice President, Growth and Development is responsible for advancing Eskaton’s strategic growth agenda through enterprise master planning, affiliations, management services, partnerships, acquisitions and expansion opportunities. This leader serves as the enterprise integrator for major growth initiatives—bringing together internal and external subject matter experts, establishing clear workstreams and decision pathways, and maintaining momentum from opportunity identification through evaluation, approval and implementation.

The Vice President, Growth and Development ensures that growth is mission-driven, strategically disciplined and aligned with Eskaton’s organizational priorities, resident and consumer needs, operational capabilities, culture and long-term financial sustainability. This leader models Eskaton’s core values—Welcoming, Bring (Y)our Best, Empowerment and Growth—and advances a high-performance culture grounded in clarity, accountability, collaboration, adaptability, continuous learning and disciplined follow-through. This is not a traditional business development role; it is an enterprise leadership position focused on converting strategic opportunity into well-coordinated, executable growth.

Essential job functions:
Master Planning Leadership & Integration
  • Lead and coordinate Eskaton’s major master planning, campus development and community repositioning initiatives through an integrated roadmap of workstreams, milestones, dependencies, risks and decision points.
  • Align internal and external subject matter experts, clarify roles, stakeholder alignment and deliverables, and preserve functional ownership and executive sponsorship.
  • Ensure plans reflect mission alignment meeting both resident and consumer needs, market demand, operational realities, financial feasibility and Eskaton’s strategic objectives.
  • Drive accountability, eliminate cross-functional barriers and facilitate timely executive and Strategic Board committee decisions to sustain momentum across complex, multi-year initiatives.
Affiliation, Acquisition & Expansion Strategy
  • Establish screening criteria and prioritization processes for identifying and evaluating affiliation, acquisition, partnership and expansion opportunities within California and beyond.
  • Lead preliminary assessments of mission fit, cultural alignment, market potential, organizational capacity, risk and financial feasibility.
  • Coordinate due diligence, negotiations, transaction management and transition or integration planning, synthesizing findings into clear executive and Board recommendations.
  • Maintain a disciplined opportunity pipeline, provide decision-oriented reporting and cultivate trusted relationships with prospective partners, affiliates and strategic collaborators.
Management Services Growth
  • Develop a focused strategy and clear criteria for expanding Eskaton through management, support and advisory service relationships.
  • Proactively identify and evaluate organizations where Eskaton’s operating capabilities, infrastructure and expertise can create mutual strategic and financial value.
  • Partner with executive and functional leaders to define scalable service offerings, operating models, economics and growth priorities.
  • Lead the evaluation, contracting and onboarding of approved relationships, and monitor performance and strategic value to inform future growth.
Growth Strategy, Intelligence & Governance
  • Support the President & CEO in defining enterprise growth goals, priorities and investment theses aligned with Eskaton’s mission and organizational impact.
  • Create consistent evaluation frameworks, scorecards and decision criteria for major growth initiatives.
  • Monitor relevant industry, demographic, consumer, capital-market and competitive trends, translating intelligence into actionable strategic implications and opportunities.
  • Prepare tailored analyses, recommendations and reporting that support executive leadership and Board Strategy Committee decisions on progress, choices, risks and required actions.
Enterprise Collaboration & Executive Communication
  • Serve as a trusted connector across executive, operational, community and support-services leaders, bringing the right expertise into each initiative at the appropriate stage.
  • Establish clear communication and collaboration rhythms that keep stakeholders informed without creating unnecessary meetings or bureaucracy.
  • Synthesize complex information into concise choices, recommendations and actionable next steps for executive and Board consideration.
  • Build alignment across differing perspectives while maintaining clarity, accountability and momentum toward outcomes.
Leadership Profile

The successful candidate will combine seasoned executive judgment with humility, curiosity and a strong growth mindset. Possess the ability to deconstruct complex problems into clear, actionable steps that drive execution. This individual must lead through influence, integrate diverse expertise and create clarity in complex, ambiguous environments while consistently modeling Eskaton’s values and high-performance culture.

  • Welcoming and enterprise-minded: Builds warmth, trust, belonging and psychological safety while aligning diverse perspectives around what is best for Eskaton as a whole.
  • Brings (Y)our Best with discipline: Sets high standards, comes prepared, communicates clearly and translates strategy into accountable milestones, decisions and follow-through.
  • Empowering and collaborative: Provides clarity, authority and support; removes obstacles; invites candid feedback; and enables leaders and subject matter experts to own outcomes.
  • Growth-oriented and adaptable: Challenges assumptions, learns continuously, solves problems and raises the bar while navigating ambiguity and change with sound judgment.

Other Job Functions

  • Models and embodies Eskaton’s core values, including:
    • Creating a sense of warmth, welcoming and belonging for all
    • Fostering excellence in everything we do
    • Seeking consistent improvement, learning and sustainable growth
    • Stepping up, taking ownership and leading with initiative
  • Fully complies with all provisions in Eskaton’s Corporate Compliance Policy and the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA).
  • Maintains attendance as outlined in Eskaton policy.
  • Follows required dress code and Eskaton’s Community Appearance Standards. Maintains a professional image to the public and residents.
  • Works in accordance with established safety guidelines; uses proper body mechanics; follows safe work practices; wears appropriate safety gear.

Starting annual salary ranges from $195,000-$245,000. Factors such as scope, responsibilities, experience, education, job-related skills, internal equity, and market considerations may influence base pay.

Preferred Experience & Qualifications

  • At least 5 years progressive leadership experience in strategy, growth, development, operations, finance, real estate, senior living, healthcare or another complex service environment.
  • Demonstrated success leading cross-functional strategic initiatives involving senior executives, Boards and external advisors, with the ability to produce clear, decision-quality materials.
  • Experience with master planning, real estate development, affiliations, mergers and acquisitions, partnerships or management services strongly preferred.
  • Strong financial and business acumen, paired with demonstrated alignment to Eskaton’s core values and a high-performance culture that balances excellence, accountability, empowerment, learning, stakeholder impact and long-term financial stewardship.
Key Success Measures
Master planning and priority growth initiatives advance against clear milestones, decision points, accountabilities and implementation plans.
  • Eskaton maintains a high-quality, strategically aligned pipeline of affiliation, acquisition, partnership and management services opportunities evaluated through consistent criteria.
  • Executive and strategy decisions are supported by timely, concise and decision-ready analysis, with cross-functional stakeholders clear on roles, dependencies and next steps.
  • Approved growth initiatives strengthen Eskaton’s mission, market position and long-term financial sustainability while visibly reinforcing the core values of Welcoming, Bring (Y)our Best, Empowerment and Growth and the behaviors of a high-performance culture.
Key Relationships
  • Internal: President & CEO and Senior Team and other leadership team leaders; community executive directors; finance, legal, marketing, people and culture, technology and other functional leaders.
  • External: Board Strategy Committee; architects; planners; developers; consultants; financial and legal advisors; healthcare and senior living organizations; potential management clients, affiliation partners and acquisition counterparties.

Role Distinction

This is not a traditional business development position. The Vice President, Growth and Development serves as Eskaton’s enterprise integrator and strategic growth leader—providing the structure, coordination, analysis and momentum required to advance complex master planning initiatives while building a disciplined platform for affiliations, management services, partnerships, acquisitions and future expansion.

Operating Principle

Welcome every voice. Bring our best. Empower ownership. Grow through learning. Deliver measurable transformation.

Work Conditions & Physical Requirements:

Requirements are subject to possible modification to reasonably accommodate individuals with disabilities. Notify the Human Resources team to request any accommodation(s) to perform any of the essential functions of this position.

Light Work: Exerting up to 20 pounds of force frequently, and/or a negligible amount of force constantly to move objects. If the use of arm and/or leg control requires exertion of forces greater than that of sedentary work and if the worker sits most of the time, the job is considered light work.

Application Requirements:

Applicants must submit a cover letter outlining how their experience, skills, and qualifications align with the key responsibilities and requirements of this position.

The final candidate must successfully pass Eskaton's post offer, pre-employment testing which includes a criminal background check, drug test, TB screen test and health screen. All new hires are required to sign an arbitration agreement as a condition of employment.

Eskaton is an Equal Opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, gender identity, sexual orientation or protected veteran status.

title: Senior Software Engineer (3D, Three.js) (m/f/d)
description:

At Straumann Group we’re on an exciting journey of growth, innovation, and impact - driven by our mission to improve oral health and transform millions of lives worldwide. Together, as owners, let’s turn meaningful insights into action.

title: Global Field & Installation Engineer
description:
Spaceflux is seeking a Field & Installation Engineer to build and maintain the physical backbone of our worldwide sensor network. You will install, commission, maintain and repair sensors on site and in-region workshops, traveling to remote sites as needed.

You’ll work directly with our Sensor Development Lead, taking ownership of installations and hardware to enable scalable growth. The role suits practical engineers who enjoy solving real-world problems and learning on the job.

Install and commission sensors worldwide – telescopes, mounts, domes and roll‑off roofs; includes site, power and connectivity interfaces. Get systems working on site in real-world conditions with diverse power, infrastructure and improvisation. Maintain, refurbish and repair deployed estate; provide second-line hardware support. Help set up and run an in-region workshop for plug-and-play deployments. Support systems programs with hands-on build, test and install work. Help write procedures and checklists to scale installations. Hands-on electro-mechanical/mechatronic engineering capability. Comfort with basic IT and networking (PCs, Ethernet, routers/switches, IP connectivity). Basic electrical competence and willingness to learn site/civil interfaces. Willingness to travel internationally for deployments.

title: Project Coordinator-Ballard Link Extension (Direct Hire Temporary)
description:
Salary range is $21.63/hour to $49.52/hour with a midpoint of $33.17/hour. New hires typically receive between minimum and midpoint, however, we may go slightly higher based on experience, internal equity and market.

This is a Direct Hire Temporary position with an anticipated duration of 12 months.

GENERAL PURPOSE:

Under general direction, performs professional and technical level tasks in assigned area of responsibility to assist multiple ST managers in administering the planning, design, and construction phases of capital projects; coordinates resources, design details, planning activities, communication and coordination of work activities, and facilitates exchange of information between Agency staff, consultants, design engineers, local jurisdictions, and the public during all project phases; interprets data and processes and handles sensitive materials; negotiates solutions and develops recommendations with Agency policies.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:

The following duties are a representative summary of the primary duties and responsibilities. Incumbent(s) may not be required to perform all duties listed and may be required to perform additional, position-specific duties:

  • Reviews and provides lead support and coordination on project-related documentation and other project related materials; and manage specific project related tasks as directed.
  • Provides support with the development of projects as assigned; verifies submittals including monthly reporting; monitors schedules; participates in the development of project feasibility studies, site selection, and technical documentation; provides Resident Engineer services as assigned for small projects; manages contractor; and coordinates project relevant public outreach efforts.
  • Provides support in project management of new facilities/stations customer signage including updating and maintaining standards, signage layout, permitting, coordination with ST departments and other agencies, and managing design and construction contracts related to this subject.
  • Provides support during final design phase of larger projects; coordinates assigned tasks and comments during design; participates in design development, review, and project meetings; meets with partner agencies and operations groups; lead and coordinate technical meetings as assigned; assists with permit procurement and submittal; assists with right-of-way needs as directed including coordinating with consultant to obtain legal descriptions, parcel exhibits, and other documentation needed to acquire property.
  • Provides support during the construction phase on larger projects; provides construction bid assistance; coordinates with construction management and Agency purchasing groups regarding bid process and contract negotiations/requirements for construction firm selection; creates procedural checklists; and manages the closing out of construction contracts.
  • Coordinates project elements with a variety of interested parties including Agency staff from various lines of businesses and departments, elected officials, consultants, local/state/federal agencies, and the general public; coordinates and attends project related technical, public, and community meetings to represent the Agency; develops meeting materials including agendas, handouts, and meeting summaries as required.
  • Coordinates scheduling of staff/consultant participation in project related meetings and public hearings; drafts and coordinates review and approval of project related materials and presentations such as change orders, Phase Gate, and staff reports to the Agency Board or Committees; and participates in presentations as necessary; serves as station/project contact and responds to requests for information from other agencies, media, and the general public involving various assigned projects; and provides necessary project status, design information, outreach, and communications with affected businesses, residences, and community groups through design and construction phases.
  • Provides support in administering assigned contracts; reviews and/or comments on consultant submitted progress reports, earned value reports, and schedules.
  • Drafts and monitors project budgets, forecasts, and schedules; obtains and monitors expenditures; prepares and submits Agency required project reports; prepares, coordinates, and processes annual and interim capital project budget updates.
  • Performs technical analysis of various types of data in support of project goals and prepares associated technical and policy reports; prepares maps and visual/presentation materials to support technical analyses; advises project managers on various technical aspects of projects; responds to and researches requests for information and public records as wells as updates on project status.
  • Researches and manages other tasks as assigned for various technical subject areas including such things as landscape and material salvage, sustainability tracking, assessment of materials, product information, and pedestrian and bike access issues.
  • Provides support to the department and others on matters as directed; serves as staff on a variety of committees as assigned; prepares staff reports and other necessary correspondence; attends and participates in professional meetings; maintains awareness of new trends and developments in the fields related to area of assignment; incorporates new developments as appropriate; ensures processes, policies, and practices are interpreted and applied consistently and effectively; ensures accountability and compliance with all current and applicable state and federal laws, Agency policies and procedures, rules and regulations.
  • Champions & models Sound Transit's core values and demonstrates values-based behaviors in everyday interactions across the agency.
  • Contributes to a culture of diversity, equity & inclusion in alignment with Sound Transit’s Equity & Inclusion Policy.
  • It is the responsibility of all employees to follow the Agency safety rules, regulations, and procedures pertaining to their assigned duties and responsibilities, which could include systems, operations, and/or other employees.
  • It is the responsibility of all employees to integrate sustainability into everyday business practices.
  • Other duties as assigned.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

Education and Experience: Bachelor’s degree in Architecture, Landscape Architecture, Planning, Engineering, Construction Management, or related field. Four years of experience providing project management support in planning, engineering, or construction including management of scope, schedule, and budget of small to mid-size projects, preferably in a public sector transit related organization; OR an equivalent combination of education and experience.

Required Knowledge and Skills:

  • Analyze situations accurately and adopt an effective course of action.
  • Work independently with minimal supervision.
  • Sensitivity to the political nature of public agencies. Maintaining confidentiality and communicating with tact and diplomacy.
  • Principles of business letter writing and basic report preparation.
  • Principles and applications of critical thinking and analysis. Operate office equipment including computers and know computer applications such as SharePoint, MS Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
  • Principles and practices of record keeping and records management.

  • Techniques to work effectively under pressure, meet deadlines, and adjust to changing priorities.

  • Establishing and maintaining effective working relationships with other department staff, management, vendors, outside agencies, community groups, and the general public.

Physical Demands / Work Environment:
