title: Senior Product Engineer
description:
At Clark Pacific, we don’t just build structures. We create innovative building solutions that are transforming the construction industry.

For more than 63 years, Clark Pacific has been a leader in prefabricated building systems, combining engineering, manufacturing, and design-build expertise to deliver smarter, more efficient construction solutions.

As we continue to grow, we’re looking for an experienced Senior Product Engineer who enjoys solving complex structural challenges, developing new products, and collaborating with clients and project teams.

This is an opportunity to influence the development of our building systems, contribute your technical expertise to project pursuits, and help turn creative engineering concepts into practical, cost-effective solutions.

Location: West Sacramento, CA

What You’ll Do

As our Senior Product Engineer, you’ll work closely with Product Management, Business Development, Engineering, and Manufacturing to design and develop prefabricated building solutions for current projects and future market needs.

Your responsibilities will include:

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals to perform the essential functions.

  • Design and develop productized building solutions that address current and future customer needs.
  • Evaluate technical feasibility, optimize structural designs, and resolve manufacturing and assembly challenges.
  • Develop cost-effective prefabricated building solutions, including gravity and lateral systems for semi-custom projects.
  • Design and analyze reinforced concrete and structural steel systems, with a strong focus on seismic lateral force-resisting systems.
  • Join Business Development in client meetings to develop initial structural concepts for prospective projects.
  • Prepare preliminary engineering schematics that support sales pursuits and meet project deadlines.
  • Collaborate with architects, engineers, owners, contractors, and design consultants to align structural solutions with architectural and building system requirements.
  • Transition successful project pursuits to design consultants and internal project management teams.
  • Evaluate how potential building code changes could affect existing and future products.
  • Apply design for manufacturing and assembly principles to improve constructability, efficiency, and product performance.
  • Help project teams resolve technical issues, evaluate alternatives, and meet commitments for schedule, cost, and quality.
  • Share technical knowledge, coach team members, and encourage constructive discussion and creative problem-solving.

What We’re Looking For

We’re looking for a collaborative engineer who brings strong structural design experience, sound technical judgment, and an interest in developing innovative prefabricated building systems. You should be comfortable working with clients, communicating design concepts, and coordinating decisions across multiple teams.

Required Qualifications

  • Registered Engineer licensure.
  • Minimum of eight years of structural design experience.
  • In-depth knowledge of reinforced concrete and structural steel lateral systems.
  • Ability to design and analyze concrete and steel building systems.
  • Familiarity with applicable building codes and design standards, including CBC, IBC, ASCE, AISC, and ACI requirements.
  • CAD proficiency and the ability to quickly communicate engineering concepts through sketches.
  • Proficiency with 3D modeling software such as SketchUp or Revit.
  • Familiarity with structural analysis software such as RISA, Visual Analysis, RAM, or ETABS.
  • A strong design for manufacturing and assembly mindset.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and Microsoft Office.
  • Strong analytical, mathematical, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
  • Excellent communication skills and the ability to build productive relationships with internal teams and external partners.
  • Ability to manage competing priorities and handle confidential or proprietary information with discretion.

Our Core Values

Determination: Meet challenges head on.
Innovation: Always look for better.
Well-Being: Seek the success, health, and happiness of all.

Benefits

Clark Pacific offers a competitive benefits package designed to support the health, financial well-being, and professional growth of our employees.

  • Competitive compensation paid weekly.
  • Health, Dental, and Vision Insurance, including Kaiser and VSP options.
  • Medical and Dependent Care Flexible Spending Accounts.
  • Employer-paid Life Insurance.
  • Voluntary Critical Illness, Accident, and Whole Life Insurance.
  • 401(k) with company match: 100% of the first 3%, then 50% of the next 2%.
  • Paid Time Off and Paid Holidays.
  • Professional development and career advancement opportunities.

Benefits are subject to a waiting period.

Work Environment

This position is based in West Sacramento, California, and works primarily in an in-person office environment, with periodic exposure to manufacturing facilities and outdoor conditions.

Occasional business travel of approximately 15% may be required.

Ready to Help Develop What’s Next?

If you’re passionate about structural engineering and want to help develop the next generation of prefabricated building systems, we’d love to hear from you.

Join Clark Pacific and help shape the future of prefabricated construction!

title: Training and Education Manager Southern European Hub
description:
Department: Global Clinical Affairs & Education, Southern European Hub
Location: Madrid (on-site)
Reports To: Global Head of Clinical Affairs & Education, Clear Correct
Reports: Yes (1-2 reports)


Job Summary:
The Training & Education (T&E) Manager plays a pivotal role in driving the adoption and success of ClearCorrect through impactful education initiatives. This role balances strategic cross-team activities with operational excellence, ensuring Southern European Hub education programs are aligned with global strategy while tailored to the local market needs. The position is critical to building credibility with healthcare professionals, accelerating clinical adoption, and positioning ClearCorrect as the partner of choice.


Key Responsibilities

Education Strategy & Programs
• Serve as the regional education strategist, translating the Hub market insights into global program design and priorities.
• Act as a thought partner to Global Education team, shaping long-term education strategies, KPIs, and investment decisions.
• Drive innovation by introducing and piloting new digital education formats (microlearning, AI-powered learning, gamification, hybrid workshops).
• Work closely with Sales leadership to embed education into commercial strategy, equipping the field force with learning tools to drive utilization.
• Define and track key education KPIs (learner outcomes, adoption impact, program ROI).
• Use CRM and analytics tools to demonstrate the value of education to leadership and commercial teams.
• Collaborate with Marketing to integrate education into campaigns and amplify reach across multiple channels.
• Partner with Clinical Research and R&D&I to translate innovations into education content for customers.
• Coordinate and deliver best-in-class local education events, webinars, and workshops, ensuring operational excellence and brand consistency.
• Partner with Global T&E to ensure curriculum consistency and scalability across regions.
• Lead post-event measurement and impact reporting to track ROI and influence business growth.

Key Customer & KOL Engagement
• Build and manage strong relationships with Key Opinion Leaders (KOLs), ensuring alignment with global strategy while addressing local needs.
• Support the creation of advisory boards with KOLs and speakers to shape future education programs.
• Expand partnerships with universities, dental schools, and professional associations to strengthen market influence.
• Act as a regional ambassador for global education initiatives, driving adoption and alignment across North America.
• Mentor and support regional team members, fostering a culture of excellence and innovation in education delivery.
• Champion changes by advocating for global standards, while tailoring execution to regional realities.

Minimal Qualifications
• Associate or Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field of work or an equivalent combination of dentistry, training education, or product management with work-related experience
• 4+ years’ work experience in oral health education industries.
• Track record in achieving challenging results.
• Good knowledge of computer operations and Microsoft Office tools.
• Language: English (Fluent) and Spanish (Fluent), French or Italian (Preferred).
• Expected travel 40%.


Personal attributes & cultural fit
• Energetic, straightforward, and performance-driven professionality with entrepreneurial spirit and strong marketing and commercial execution abilities.
• Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a matrix environment.
• Strong presentation and communication skills.
• Ability to celebrate successes and inspire a motivational team environment.
• Effective relationship builder.
• Enthusiastic about providing excellent support & service, always customer centric.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, or disability.

title: Director Solution Management
description:
Call to action

Are you ready to unlock your potential? At Straumann Group we’re on an exciting journey of growth, innovation, and impact - driven by our mission to improve oral health and transform millions of lives worldwide. United by purpose, we bring our best selves to work every day, embracing a high-performance, player-learner culture that inspires collaboration, curiosity, and ambition. Here, you’ll have the opportunity to take charge of your own career, harnessing your skills, passion, and enthusiasm for learning to continually grow and progress. Together, we’re not just shaping brighter smiles, we’re unlocking the potential of people everywhere, including our own.

About the role

As Director of Solution Management, you will define and own the strategy for integrated, end-to-end solutions across Straumann Group’s portfolio. This role connects individual product strategies into cohesive, scalable and customer-focused solutions that deliver measurable value for customers and the business.

Working as a peer to Product Management Directors, you will orchestrate complex, multidisciplinary solutions across domains such as data acquisition, surgical, restorative, manufacturing and digital platforms. You will bring a holistic view across product domains and business units, helping teams align priorities, manage dependencies and evolve products as part of one coherent solution ecosystem.

This is a strategic role for someone who can combine portfolio thinking, customer insight, solution design and cross-functional collaboration to shape how integrated solutions are delivered and adopted across the organization.

Your Role

In this role you will:

  • Define and own the strategy for integrated, end-to-end solutions across the portfolio, ensuring alignment with business priorities, customer needs and portfolio goals.
  • Translate customer needs, market opportunities and business priorities into clear solution strategies.
  • Connect digital products, services, manufacturing capabilities and the implant portfolio into integrated customer solutions.
  • Shape end-to-end solution concepts that support consistent customer experiences, scalable implementation and long-term portfolio evolution.
  • Identify gaps, overlaps and dependencies across the solution ecosystem and work with stakeholders to address them.
  • Influence product roadmaps from an end-to-end solution perspective, ensuring individual roadmaps support shared portfolio priorities.
  • Facilitate alignment and prioritization across Product Management, business units and relevant functions.
  • Support decision-making by bringing a holistic, cross-domain perspective to portfolio discussions.
  • Partner with commercial and customer-facing teams to support adoption, implementation and value realization.
  • Define and monitor measures for solution adoption, performance, customer value and business impact.
  • Identify opportunities for innovation that emerge from integrating products, technologies, services and capabilities.

Your Profile

You bring a combination of strategic product management, solution leadership, cross-functional orchestration and customer-focused business experience.

Essential requirements:

  • Postgraduate degree in Business, Marketing, Engineering, Dentistry or a related field.
  • Significant experience in Product Management, Solution Management or a closely related function.
  • Experience leading cross-functional initiatives, at least on a functional basis.
  • Proven experience working across complex, multidisciplinary portfolios and organizational structures.
  • Experience in medical devices.
  • Good understanding of software development and Agile ways of working.
  • Ability to influence across organizational and business-unit boundaries.
  • Well-developed strategic, analytical and decision-making skills.
  • Clear and effective communication skills, with the ability to align diverse stakeholders.
  • Business-fluent English.

Nice to have:

  • Experience in the dental industry.
  • Additional language skills.

What Makes You a Great Fit

You are successful in this role if you can create clarity across complexity and help teams move from individual product perspectives to integrated, customer-focused solutions. You are comfortable working across organizational boundaries, aligning stakeholders around shared priorities and turning strategic opportunities into actionable solution plans.

You bring curiosity, sound judgment and a collaborative working style. You focus on measurable customer and business outcomes, challenge existing boundaries when it improves value, and use feedback to continuously improve solutions. You will thrive in this role if you enjoy shaping strategy, connecting people and ideas, and enabling innovation across a broad solution ecosystem.


All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, or disability.

title: Shift Leader
description:
JOB SUMMARY:

The Shift Leader works productively and supervises restaurant Crew Members to ensure they perform their jobs responsibilities so the restaurant achieves customer satisfaction and profitability during their shift.


PERFORMANCE RESULTS:

1. Serves customers correct, complete orders within service time goals, according to the Customer Service Standards, the Priority Guidelines, the telephone and front counter station procedures and if necessary, the Remedy Process.

2. Prepares and ensures consistent, high quality products are served to customers as described in the Apricus Orientation and Training Handbook and as shown on the job station helpers.

3. Displays the proper image and follows Little Caesars policies, procedures and standards for conduct as outlined in the Apricus Orientation and Training Handbook.

4. Cleans and organizes work stations and ensures the standards for restaurant image are maintained as directed by management and as required by the local health department.

5. Performs cash management responsibilities and ensures compliance by Team members to all safety and security procedures as defined in the Apricus Orientation and Training Handbook as well as any other safety and security procedures issued.

6. Provides direction and feedback to Crew Members and follows up by coaching/counseling to ensure job duties are performed and all Little Caesar standards, procedures and policies are achieved.

7. Performs the task associated with food, paper, labor, and utility cost controls and monitors shift

activities to ensure compliance.

8. Completes all daily paperwork neatly and accurately as described by the Operational Resource Guide (ORG) or as directed by management.

9. Follows all procedures associated with opening the closing the restaurant, appropriately handles

unexpected occurrences, and notifies appropriate parties in a timely fashion.

Nature & Scope


The Shift Leader receives direction and training from the General Manager and Assistant Manager, the Shift Leader 4-week Training Plan, and other Little Caesars training materials and classes. The Shift Leader is responsible for supervising Crew Members and provides adult supervision to Crew Members less than 18 years of age. During each shift, they motivate, direct and coach Crew Members to work proficiently at their assigned stations and then follow-up to ensure tasks are completed in a timely manner according to Little Caesars procedures.

The Shift Leader must abide by all state and federal laws OSHA and EEOC requirements, as well as

practice and enforce all Apricus policies and procedures. They utilize all cost control tools and

processes ensuring the goals of food, paper, and labor are achieved during their shift. They ensure each shift is prepared to meet the needs of their customers and work diligently to ensure each customer is satisfied with the service and product they receive.

Please discuss the job responsibilities with your Assistant Manager. Detailed list of each station's

responsibilities and duties can be found in the "Operational Resource Guide" (ORG).

Your Assistant Manager will discuss the essential job functions, which are normally defined as fundamental activities conducted on regular basis that will affect the success of the restaurant. The Shift Leader will be scheduled to work according to our business needs and therefore no guarantee of hours can be made. This position requires a hands-on style of management and physical work

such as: lifting, squatting, and standing for long periods of time.


Task Analysis


To perform the functions listed in this job description, the following tasks will be required:

· The ability to lift and move 55 pounds.

· The ability to reach and move items from as high as 6 feet and as low as 6 inches off the ground.

· The ability to control and utilize equipment safely and correctly (sheeter machine, VCM, sauce

ladle, cheese cups, pan gripers, spatula, pizza and dough cutter, different types of knives, can

openers, pastry brush, scales, microwave, telephone, cash register, etc.).

· The ability to "Shakerboard" by working outside holding a sign as allowed by ordinance.

· The ability to apply pressure to cut through products and/or clean equipment/utensils.

· The ability to count, separate and weight all types of food products and inventory items.

· The ability to effectively communicate to customer and co-workers (reading, speaking, hearing, writing, etc.).

· The ability to understand directions, instructions and product specifications.

· The ability to process and complete customer orders.

· The ability to comprehend all training materials and practice standard operating procedures.

· The ability to successfully pass required training programs for certification.

· The ability to use mathematical skills to compute sales totals, percentages, inventory usage, food orders, employee work schedules, cash handling results and projected business needs.

· The ability to legally drive an automobile adhering to all state and local traffic laws.

· The ability to supervise a number of people at the same time and to motivate them to meet goals, duties and deadlines.

QUALIFICATIONS

1. Have previous experience in restaurants, retail or a position involving customer contact is preferred.

2. Be at least 18 years of age.

3. Possess a high school diploma, or equivalent, and possess basic math skills.

4. Possess excellent verbal communication and interpersonal relations skills.

5. Be dependable, hardworking and have the ability to work under pressure and in stressful situations.

6. Be able to work a standard schedule of approximately 20-30 hours per week and be able to perform all the essential functions of the job.

7. Have successfully completed the 4-week Shift Leader Training Plan and passed the solo open and close shift evaluations.

8. Possess a valid driver's license from the state of residence with a driving record maintained within

company guidelines. Possess a reliable vehicle and auto insurance as a primary to complete daily

banking and other responsibilities as directed by the Assistant Manager, General Manager or District Manager.

9. Meet Apricus Background Verification guidelines.

10. The US Department of Homeland Security (USCIS Division) requires that each Shift Leader provide documentation that proves their eligibility to work in the United States.

Please Note: Little Caesars reserves the right to change, modify, suspend, interpret, or cancel in whole, or in part, any of the duties outlined above, at any time, and without advance notice to the employee.

title: Electrical Panel Technician
description:
We are Proud to be SJE!

At SJE, we are more than a company — we are a family of brands with a shared vision and mission to provide industry-leading, innovative, and reliable control and monitoring solutions that improve efficiencies, protect the environment, and deliver dependable solutions to our valued customers. We are looking for an Electrical Panel Technician to support our engineered brands. This role will work out of our Lee, NH location.

As our Electrical Panel Technician, you will be responsible for assembling, fabricating, and wiring industrial electrical control panels for municipal and industrial applications. You will work from electrical drawings, wiring diagrams, and project specifications to ensure control panels are built accurately, efficiently, and in accordance with SJE quality standards and applicable UL 508A and UL 698A requirements.

In this role, you will perform hands-on panel assembly, component installation, fabrication, and wiring while maintaining a safe and organized workspace. You will collaborate with the Design Team to resolve technical questions, verify specifications, and ensure panels meet project requirements. You will also assist with quality inspections, document project progress, track incoming parts and materials, and maintain tools and equipment. Additionally, you may assist with the pickup and delivery of components and completed panels as needed.

The skills you need:

To succeed in this role, you should have experience with:

  • Assembling, fabricating, and wiring industrial electrical control panels using electrical drawings, wiring diagrams, and project specifications.

  • Working with electrical components, wiring methods, hand tools, and power tools used in control panel manufacturing.

  • Reading and interpreting electrical schematics, technical drawings, and assembly instructions.

  • Understanding electrical control panel construction practices, including UL 508A and UL 698A requirements, or the ability to learn through provided training.

  • Maintaining accurate documentation of project progress, materials, and completed work.

  • Strong attention to detail, mechanical aptitude, and commitment to quality and workplace safety.

  • Basic computer proficiency, including Microsoft Office applications.

  • Strong problem-solving, communication, and organizational skills, with the ability to work independently and collaboratively with a team.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Previous experience in electrical control panel assembly, fabrication, or wiring.

  • Familiarity with electrical circuit design, component selection, and equipment sizing.

  • Experience with industrial instrumentation and automation components.

  • Familiarity with drafting software such as Microsoft Visio, EPLAN, or similar applications.

  • Associate degree in Electrical Engineering Technology or a related technical field, or equivalent relevant experience

We will answer more of your questions during the first interview. Expect to hear about the next steps if you meet the job requirements.

Why Work With Us
At SJE, we believe in empowering our employees to grow professionally while making a real impact. We offer competitive pay, excellent benefits, and a collaborative culture that encourages creativity and problem-solving. Join us and become a part of something bigger. Join a company where you’re not just working—you’re building a legacy!

title: Commercial Cleaning Area Manager [s]
description:
Job Summary

As a CBRE, Government Services Commercial Cleaning Area Manager, you will lead custodial operations across multiple client sites within an assigned region, typically five to 10 locations in a single metropolitan area. You will set the operating standard for the region, manage the site supervisors and leads who run each location, own the region's budget and labor plan, and serve as the senior point of contact for client leadership at every site. You will spend most of your time in the field, moving between locations to audit quality, coach teams, and resolve issues before they reach the client.

Primary Job Functions

  • Provide formal supervision for site supervisors, leads, and cleaning staff across assigned locations, including performance management, coaching, hiring, and onboarding.
  • Establish regional operating standards, staffing models, work schedules, and task calendars, holding site leadership accountable for execution.
  • Manage the regional operating budget and P&L, including labor and supply forecasting, payroll, purchase orders, and variance review.
  • Maintain adequate staffing coverage across locations through workforce planning and cross-training.
  • Serve as the senior point of contact for client leadership, leading meetings, addressing escalations, and supporting contractual and service-related matters.
  • Conduct quality audits, monitor KPIs/SLAs, and ensure corrective actions are implemented and closed.
  • Standardize processes, training, tools, and best practices across the region to ensure consistent service delivery.
  • Resolve cleaning-related complaints and recurring operational issues by identifying and addressing root causes.
  • Ensure safety and compliance requirements are followed across all assigned locations, including incident investigation and reporting.
  • Manage regional equipment, supplies, inventory, and vendor relationships to support service delivery and cost control.
  • Support new site startups, contract transitions, and scope changes, including staffing, training, and equipment mobilization.
  • Lead by example and model behaviors consistent with organization values while influencing stakeholders to achieve business objectives.
  • Identify and resolve complex operational issues affecting multiple sites.

What you'll need:

Education:

  • Bachelor’s Degree
  • In lieu of a degree, a combination of experience and education will be considered

Experience

  • Required: Minimum of 5 years of job-related experience
  • Relevant experience in commercial cleaning or facilities operations, including at least two years supervising staff. Multi-site or area-level responsibility preferred.

License/Certification

  • Required: Valid driver's license with an acceptable driving record. Required for daily travel between sites.
  • Preferred: Microsoft certifications
  • Any relevant certifications in maintenance, safety, or facilities operations are a plus

Working Conditions:

  • Work is performed across multiple client sites within the assigned region, with regular travel between locations. Exposure to cleaning chemicals, noise, wet floors, and varying indoor and outdoor conditions. The schedule follows site operations and includes early mornings, evenings, weekends, and on-call response to emergencies or staffing gaps.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

  • Fulfill the physical requirements associated with this role. This includes stooping, standing, walking, and climbing stairs. Must be able to lift/carry heavy loads of 50 lbs. or more.
  • Experience in the areas of staffing, selection, training, development, coaching, mentoring, measuring, appraising, and rewarding performance and retention preferred.
  • Ability to guide the exchange of sensitive, complicated, and difficult information, convey performance expectations and handle problems.
  • Leadership skills to motivate team impact on quality, efficiency, and effectiveness of the job discipline and department.
  • Knowledge of Microsoft Office products. Examples include Word, Excel, Outlook, etc.
  • Extensive organizational skills with a strong inquisitive mindset.

Travel Requirements

  • Up to 50% local and regional travel between sites within the assigned region. A valid driver's license and reliable transportation are required.

When you join CBRE, you become part of the global leader in commercial real estate services and investment that helps businesses and people thrive. We are dynamic problem solvers and forward-thinking professionals who create significant impact. Our collaborative culture is built on our shared values — respect, integrity, service and excellence — and we value the diverse perspectives, backgrounds and skillsets of our people. At CBRE, you have the opportunity to chart your own course and realize your potential. We welcome all applicants.

title: Community Banker I - Float - Bakersfield Cal Ave
description:
JOB SUMMARY:

The Community Banker role is a progressive branch career path with increasing responsibility for customer service, teller transactions, account opening, operational controls, relationship support, and branch leadership. Each level reflects expanded technical skill, judgment, independence, coaching, and the ability to support branch goals and an elevated customer experience.

The travel/float Community Banker provides flexible branch coverage by traveling to various bank locations to support daily operations, maintain efficient customer service, and ensure consistent adherence to banking policies and procedures. This position fills staffing gaps as assigned by the Community Banking Regional Manager due to vacations, absences, increased customer traffic, and other operational needs while delivering a positive customer experience at every assigned branch.

ROLE LEVELING FRAMEWORK:

Responsibilities are cumulative by level. Advancement is based on demonstrated proficiency, policy and compliance adherence, sound judgment, customer service capability, and readiness to assume broader responsibility with greater independence.

Level

Primary Scope and Distinction

Community Banker I
Foundational Branch Service

Establishes an elevated customer experience by creating a welcoming environment, accurately processing routine teller transactions, opening basic consumer accounts, and recognizing opportunities to connect customers with appropriate bank solutions. Operates within defined procedures, demonstrates strong attention to detail, protects customer information, and escalates exceptions, risk concerns, or complex needs with sound awareness of policy and customer impact.

Community Banker II
Relationship and Account Solutions

Expands from transaction-focused service to relationship-based banking by independently opening and servicing consumer and business accounts, asking purposeful questions to understand customer needs, and recommending deposit, digital banking, Treasury Management, and other solutions. Resolves non-routine service matters with greater ownership, follows through on referrals, and uses judgment to balance customer experience, operational accuracy, compliance, and risk escalation.

Community Banker III
Advanced Operations and Branch Support

Serves as a senior branch resource who demonstrates deep knowledge of bank products and services, branch operations, complex account opening, customer service standards, operational controls, and risk requirements. Handles more sophisticated consumer and business banking needs, identifies Treasury Management and lending opportunities, supports vault, ATM, balancing, certifications, audit readiness, referral development, and sales initiatives. Evaluates risk, recommends practical solutions, and models the judgment and ownership expected in elevated customer and operational situations.

RESPONSIBILITIES INCLUDE, BUT ARE NOT LIMITED TO:

  • Provides professional customer service, processes teller transactions, resolves routine service requests, and refers customers to appropriate bank products, services, or business partners.
  • Opens and maintains deposit accounts, completes required documentation, explains account features, and supports customer needs through accurate and confidential handling of information.
  • Maintains cash drawer accuracy, supports vault, ATM, wire, callback, balancing, certification, and operational reporting activities as assigned and appropriate to level.
  • Follows bank policies, procedures, security practices, dual-control requirements, compliance expectations, fraud prevention standards, and confidentiality requirements.
  • Identifies customer needs, promotes relationship-building, supports referrals and cross-sell opportunities, and contributes to branch goals and a positive customer experience.
  • Performs other duties and provides support to other branches, retail network, community, training, or operational initiatives as needed.

REQUIRED KNOWLEDGE, SKILL, AND ABILITY:

  • Strong customer service, communication, professionalism, and ability to interact tactfully with customers and employees.
  • Accuracy, attention to detail, confidentiality, risk awareness, and adherence to policies, procedures, dual-control requirements, and regulatory expectations.
  • Ability to identify customer needs, explain products and services, make appropriate referrals, and deepen customer relationships.
  • Cash handling, teller operations, account opening, branch systems, quality assurance, and operational reporting knowledge appropriate to the level.
  • Ability to manage priorities, meet deadlines, support branch coverage, and contribute to a positive team environment.
  • Working knowledge of Microsoft Office Suite and ability to navigate multiple computer systems.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE:

  • High school diploma or equivalent required.
  • Related banking, branch operations, customer service, sales, account opening, cash handling, or leadership experience preferred based on level.
  • Level placement is based on demonstrated proficiency, operational knowledge, customer service capability, risk judgment, coaching ability, and readiness to assume broader responsibility.

WORK ENVIRONMENT:

This job operates in a professional office environment and routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, scanners, filing cabinets, and fax machines. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential functions.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to stand, use hands to handle or feel, reach with hands and arms, and talk or hear. The employee is occasionally required to walk and sit. The employee must frequently lift and/or move up to 10 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds. Specific vision abilities required include close vision and the ability to adjust focus. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential functions.

AT-WILL EMPLOYMENT NOTICE:

I understand that, if hired, my employment with Bank of the Sierra is at-will, meaning that either I or the Bank may terminate the employment at any time, with or without cause or advance notice, so long as the reason is lawful. By submitting this application, you understand and agree to the at-will notice.

Bank of the Sierra is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and is an affirmative action employer committed to equal employment opportunities regardless of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran, or disability status.

title: Batcher
description:
Job Overview:

The production Batcher is responsible for ensuring the preparation and mixing of appropriate ingredients required to produce finished products within our plumbing, HVAC and firestop products. Duties include performing all batching processes from performing initial calculations to completing premix/post-mix operations based upon number of cases and tanks scheduled for production each shift. This is an on-site hourly position that may require the employee to be in their assigned area prior to the start of the shift to stage work area. Additional work hours will be assigned during peak times and year-end. The standard schedule for this position is Monday through Thursday, 5:00 AM to 3:30 PM, with potential overtime as needed. We are looking for someone who is flexible with their availability and open to working additional hours or adjusting their schedule based on business needs.

RectorSeal manufactures and/or distributes a variety of mechanical products for the HVAC, electrical, and plumbing industries. For over 80 years, RectorSeal’s customers have depended on us for quality products with excellent value, shipped to them in a timely manner. This passion for excellent customer service is the reason RectorSeal has been growing at a very fast pace, and now requires additional shift capacity to meet customer demand.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Stage and prepare raw materials for efficient and safe mixing operations.
  • Monitor the mixture of raw materials according to written formulas.
  • Ensure all products are manufactured safely by following set manufacturing practices.
  • Partner with the QA/Lab to maintain the product specifications and ensure quality.
  • Maintain and track inventory accuracy using the ERP system.
  • Clean and disinfect mixing utensils, tools, buckets, and general work areas.
  • Monitor and inspect equipment to maintain proper condition and safety.
  • Accurately complete required production paperwork.
  • Able to unload tankers and store other raw materials.
  • Other related duties as assigned.
  • Support and operate production line as needed.
  • Required to operate a forklift and/or pallet jack.


Minimum Requirements:

  • High School Diploma/Equivalent or 6 months experience in chemical processing, manufacturing, or distribution environment in lieu of education.
  • Able to work 8 -12-hour shifts standing.
  • Reliable and punctual.
  • Available to work any shift and/or overtime as needed.

Preferred Experience:

  • Bilingual in Spanish.
  • Working knowledge manufacturing processes, environment, or equipment.
  • Prior experience with JD Edwards or other ERP systems.
  • HAZWOPER 40 training certification or equivalent.

Skills and Competencies:

  • Good communication and teamwork skills.
  • Computer knowledge to enter and track products in ERP system.
  • Strong logical decision-making skills.
  • Able to keep up in a fast-paced environment.
  • Able to read and comprehend instructions and labels.
  • Math skills to function in the role including add, subtract, multiply, and divide in all units of measure.
  • Able to operate and maintain equipment in alignment with safety standards.
  • Able to read Material Safety Data Sheets as well as raw material and finished goods container labels.
  • High-quality standards and degree of accuracy and organizational skills.
  • Solid work history that demonstrates reliability and ability to thrive in a team environment.
  • Ability to understand, take ownership, and ensure the follow-through of directives as planned.
  • Adaptable and easily adjusts to changing work conditions and responsibilities with a positive attitude.
  • Receptive to coaching and utilizes critical feedback to grow skills for self and others.

    Work Environment

title: Senior SAP Security & Authorizations Lead
description:
Introduction

As Senior SAP Security & Authorizations Lead, you'll play a key role in shaping the future of SAP security across Straumann Group's global technology landscape. Working within our Global Identity & Access Services team, you'll contribute to our S/4HANA transformation by designing and evolving secure, scalable authorization concepts that support business growth while meeting security and compliance requirements.

This is a highly collaborative role where you'll partner with business stakeholders, SAP specialists, audit and compliance teams, external service providers, and IAM experts around the world. Beyond maintaining a secure SAP environment, you'll help modernize and automate identity and access management processes, improving efficiency, transparency, and governance across our global SAP ecosystem.


Your Role

In this position, you will:

  • Help design and implement the SAP authorization concept for the S/4HANA transformation.
  • Develop and maintain SAP security, authorization, and governance standards.
  • Design and manage Segregation of Duties (SoD) controls and support ongoing risk management.
  • Collaborate with audit, risk, compliance, and business teams to ensure regulatory and governance requirements are met.
  • Lead SAP user access management, role provisioning, access reviews, and authorization support.
  • Identify opportunities to simplify, standardize, and automate SAP access management processes.
  • Drive integrations between SAP platforms, Identity Governance & Administration (IGA), and IT Service Management (ITSM) solutions.
  • Lead end-to-end service delivery, working closely with internal teams and external service providers to ensure high-quality support.
  • Coordinate SAP security activities for projects, including S/4HANA initiatives and M&A integrations.
  • Share expertise through stakeholder guidance, documentation, and knowledge-sharing sessions.
  • Stay current with SAP security trends, governance practices, and regulatory developments to continuously strengthen our security posture.

Your Profile

Must-have qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Information Security, or a related discipline.
  • Several years of experience in SAP Security with strong expertise in SAP authorizations, role design, and user access management.
  • Experience delivering SAP security services in a complex enterprise environment.
  • Knowledge of SAP Governance, Risk & Compliance (GRC), including Segregation of Duties concepts.
  • Experience managing external service providers and collaborating across global teams.
  • Experience supporting SAP transformation or implementation projects.
  • Strong stakeholder management, communication, and relationship-building skills.
  • Ability to balance business requirements with security, compliance, and operational needs.

Nice to have

  • Master's degree in a relevant discipline.
  • SAP Security or GRC certifications (such as C_AUDSEC_73, C_GRCAC_12, or C_SECAUTH_20).
  • Professional security certifications such as CISSP or CISM.
  • Experience with mergers and acquisitions (M&A) integrations.
  • Familiarity with SIAM platforms, including SIVIS.
  • Experience developing training or awareness programmes related to SAP security.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, or disability

title: Professional Engineer (PE) – Mechanical Engineering / Project Manager
description:

Core Facility Services is seeking an experienced **New York State Licensed Professional Engineer (PE)** to lead mechanical engineering, building infrastructure, and capital improvement projects throughout New York City and Long Island.

This position combines technical engineering expertise with project management responsibilities, including project planning, design coordination, budgeting, scheduling, contractor management, and construction oversight. The successful candidate will oversee projects from initial assessment and feasibility through design, permitting, construction, commissioning, and final closeout.

The ideal candidate will have extensive knowledge of commercial and institutional mechanical systems, a strong understanding of applicable New York City building and mechanical codes, and a proven ability to manage complex projects while maintaining quality, safety, budget, and schedule requirements.

- Extensive knowledge of commercial or institutional HVAC systems, boilers, chillers, pumps, piping, ventilation, controls, and central utility plants.

title: Dispatch Coordinator
description:
The Dispatch Coordinator is responsible for owning the day-to-day dispatching, scheduling, and workflow coordination of the service department. This role is highly hands-on and dispatch-forward, with a primary focus on assigning repair orders, managing technician capacity, reducing downtime, and ensuring jobs move through the shop efficiently and accurately. While this role partners closely with the Service Manager and Operations leadership, its core accountability is real-time execution: keeping the board clean, technicians productive, priorities clear, and communication flowing. This role is critical to shop throughput, technician efficiency, and customer satisfaction.

Key Objectives

  • Optimize technician productivity, efficiency, and shop throughput through effective dispatching
  • Own accurate, prioritized scheduling and real-time workflow adjustments
  • Reduce Repair Event Cycle Time (RECT) and technician downtime
  • Ensure clear communication across technicians, service advisors, and management
  • Support a consistent, high-quality customer experience through reliable execution

Core Responsibilities

  • Dispatch & Workflow Management
    • Assign repair orders (ROs) to technicians based on skill level, availability, and job priority
    • Maintain and enforce a clear priority system across customer pay, warranty, internal, and urgent work
    • Monitor job progress throughout the day and rebalance workloads as needed
    • Adjust assignments proactively to address delays, parts issues, or schedule changes
    • Review repair orders for clarity, accuracy, and readiness prior to dispatch
    • Communicate expectations clearly to technicians and service advisors
  • Shop Coordination & Support
    • Partner closely with the Service Manager to align daily priorities and staffing needs
    • Support technicians by ensuring work is staged, ready, and properly sequenced
    • Identify workflow bottlenecks and escalate operational issues when needed
    • Maintain awareness of individual technician strengths, limitations, and productivity trends
    • Assign repair orders (ROs) based on technician skill set, availability, and job priority
    • Monitor job progress and adjust assignments to minimize downtime or delays
    • Maintain an effective priority system balancing urgent, warranty, and routine work
    • Review repair orders for clarity and accuracy prior to assignment
    • Communicate expectations clearly with technicians and service advisors
  • Productivity, Metrics & Performance Tracking
    • Track technician productivity, efficiency, utilization, and RECT on a daily basis
    • Maintain accurate dispatching records and performance data
    • Report daily and weekly performance results to the Service Manager
    • Identify trends impacting throughput or cycle time and recommend adjustments
    • Use data to support coaching conversations and operational improvements
  • Customer Experience & Communication
    • Partner with service advisors to provide accurate timelines and job updates
    • Escalate service delays or customer-impacting issues as needed
    • Support high NPS and customer satisfaction through proactive coordination
    • Step in to manage customer experience issues when necessary
  • Operational Awareness
    • Support shop performance goals by aligning dispatch decisions with labor efficiency targets
    • Understand how dispatching impacts revenue, labor hours, and customer satisfaction
    • Communicate capacity constraints and performance risks to leadership proactively

What we're looking for

  • Strong dispatching, scheduling, and prioritization skills
  • Ability to make quick, confident decisions in a fast-paced environment
  • Exceptional organizational and time-management abilities
  • Clear and direct communication style
  • Strong problem-solving skills with a process-driven mindset
  • Ability to manage competing priorities without losing accuracy or urgency

Experience & Qualifications

  • Demonstrated experience in dispatching, scheduling, or service workflow coordination
  • Experience working directly with technicians in a service or repair environment
  • Familiarity with technician productivity, efficiency, and cycle time metrics
  • Proficiency with dispatching, scheduling, or service management software
  • Ability to work Saturdays as needed
  • RV or automotive service experience is a plus but not required
  • Ability to pass a background check and drug test

Expected Results

  • Technicians consistently dispatched to the right work at the right time
  • Reduced technician downtime and improved shop utilization
  • Improved Repair Event Cycle Time (RECT)
  • Clean, accurate, and prioritized dispatch board
  • Fewer delays caused by RO errors or misaligned priorities
  • Strong communication flow across the service department
  • Consistently positive customer experience tied to timely service delivery

Who we are:

Bish’s RV is one of the largest family-owned RV dealers in the country. We are dedicated to providing quality products and services that exceed the expectations of our customers and creating an atmosphere where our customers can enjoy a positive experience as friends of our family business.

Our company is currently experiencing record growth with more expansion on the way. The opportunities to grow within our organization are outstanding and our dedication to each employee’s success is unparalleled.

We are a goal-driven company with a high-performance culture and believe in setting ourselves apart by being “Different with a Purpose.” Our culture is built upon the foundation of our core values: We are Genuine, Fun, and Driven by Results.

title: Quality Assurance Manager
description:
Responsibilities

Regulatory Compliance and Inspection Readiness

  • Ensure compliance with FDA regulations, cGMP, DEA, DSCSA, applicable state licensing requirements, and client-specific quality requirements across all 3PL operations.
  • Maintain a constant state of inspection readiness for internal, client, and regulatory audits.
  • Lead and support regulatory inspections and client audits, ensuring timely, complete responses to observations and follow-through on commitments.
  • Support the internal audit (self-inspection) program and supplier/vendor qualification activities.

Quality Management System

  • Oversee and continuously improve core QMS processes, including:
    • Deviations and nonconformances (NCs)
    • Corrective and Preventive Actions (CAPA), including effectiveness checks
    • Change control
    • Document control and record retention
    • GMP training and qualification of personnel
    • Product complaints, returns, recalls, and temperature excursions
  • Ensure investigations are thorough, root causes are identified, and corrective actions are effective and sustainable.
  • Ensure data integrity and electronic record compliance in eQMS, LIMs and other GxP systems.
  • Exercise quality authority to quarantine, hold, and release product in accordance with approved procedures.

Cleanroom Sampling and Dispensing

  • Provide quality oversight of cleanroom sampling and dispensing, which is executed day to day under the Sampling and Dispensing Supervisor.
  • Ensure adherence to SOPs, cGMP, and aseptic practices; timely review of records, labeling, chain of custody, and line clearance; and thorough investigation and resolution of related deviations.

Environmental Monitoring (EM)

  • Oversee the cleanroom EM program, ensuring data are reviewed and trended, excursions receive timely investigation and CAPA, and cleanroom qualification, cleaning/disinfection, and monitoring requirements are maintained.

Continuous Improvement and Reporting

  • Lead initiatives that improve quality performance, reduce variation and deviations, and increase Right-First-Time (RFT) execution and operational efficiency.
  • Analyze quality trends, metrics, and KPIs to identify systemic issues and drive data-based decisions.
  • Report quality performance and improvement actions at management review.

Client Partnership

  • Serve as the primary quality contact for commercial clients, ensuring strong communication and partnership.
  • Address client concerns, deviations, and quality events with urgency and transparency.
  • Ensure client notification requirements are met in accordance with quality agreements and SOPs.
  • Support quality agreement development, maintenance, and compliance.

Team Leadership

  • Lead, coach, and develop a team of QA professionals, including the Sampling and Dispensing Supervisor, to ensure high performance and engagement.
  • Establish clear roles, responsibilities, and expectations for all direct reports, and participate in hiring, performance reviews, and development planning.
  • Drive a culture of accountability, ownership, and quality excellence across the organization.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications and Job Specifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Biology, Chemistry, Engineering, or a related field (equivalent experience may be considered).
  • Minimum of 5 years of quality experience in the pharmaceutical, medical device, or other FDA-regulated industry.
  • Minimum of 3 years of supervisory experience.
  • Working knowledge of state and federal laws and regulations governing warehousing and distribution of pharmaceuticals and medical devices, including FDA, DEA, PDMA, and DSCSA, with the ability to interpret and apply them.

Preferred

  • Experience in 3PL, warehouse, or distribution quality operations.
  • Experience with cleanroom operations, sampling and dispensing, and environmental monitoring.
  • Experience hosting regulatory inspections and client audits.
  • ASQ certification (e.g., CQA, CQM/OE, CPGP) and/or ISO auditor certification.

Technical Expertise

  • Excellent verbal and written communication and presentation skills.
  • Strong analytical skills, including investigation, root-cause analysis, and trending and presentation of quality metrics.
  • Sound critical thinking and attention to detail.
  • Strong organization and time management; able to prioritize in a fast-paced environment.
  • Ability to learn and use quality and warehouse management systems: eQMS, LIMS, Tecsys Elite, and WebCTRL (training provided).
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Outlook, Excel, Word, and PowerPoint.

Additional Employment Requirements

  • Must successfully pass preliminary employment requirements (e.g., background check and drug screen).
  • Must be able to travel up to 15%.
  • Must have a valid driver’s license.

Physical/Mental/Visual Demands

  • Physical: light to medium work with frequent walking and standing, and periods of sitting; occasional lifting of up to 50 lbs; ability to gown and wear PPE for cleanroom entry.
  • Mental: ability to analyze data, manage multiple priorities, make timely decisions, and communicate effectively under deadlines.
  • Visual: ability to read documents, screens, and labels, and to visually inspect materials and records.

Working Conditions

  • Work is performed primarily in an office environment, with regular time in warehouse and cleanroom areas as needed to oversee quality operations.
  • Warehouse areas may involve temperature variations, noise, and the presence of material-handling equipment.

Equipment Operated

  • Equipment: laptop computer, cell phone, copier, and desk phone.
  • Systems: Outlook, Excel, Word, PowerPoint, MQ1 (quality management software), Tecsys Elite, and WebCTRL.

title: State Government Relations Director - Wisconsin
description:
Position Summary:

The Wisconsin State Government Relations Director serves as the principal staff for state government affairs and chief lobbyist in Wisconsin, representing the Alzheimer’s Association before Wisconsin’s legislature, governor, relevant state agencies, coalitions and community partners, and on statewide task forces and work groups. This position serves as a registered lobbyist with the state and is responsible for developing and executing a strategy to implement the Alzheimer’s Association’s coordinated nationwide state policy priorities including issues related to insurance coverage, Medicaid, long-term care, training standards, workforce issues, aging policy, and other related issues. The State Government Relations Director reports to the Territory Government Relations Director.

Responsibilities:

  • Plan and execute a multi-year state legislative and regulatory agenda with a focus on implementation of the Association's state policy priorities, in collaboration with the National Public Policy Office.
  • Draft bills and regulatory language and secure bill sponsors.
  • Testify regularly before state legislative committees and train volunteer advocates and other Association staff to provide testimony on behalf of the Association as needed.
  • Develop and grow relationships with legislators, state government officials and community stakeholders, ensuring the Association is represented on relevant statewide task forces, workgroups, committees and coalitions.
  • Track state legislation utilizing the Association’s approved tracking system and monitor committee meetings and legislative action.
  • Report lobbying activities as required and ensure compliance with the Association’s approved lobbying compliance vendor and internal tracking system.
  • Collaborate with the local Grassroots Advocacy Manager to plan and execute the Association’s annual State Advocacy Day event at the state capitol.
  • Identify opportunities for grassroots engagement on state issues and assist as needed in the execution of state-level advocacy activities, including coordinating office visits, correspondence, and other activities.
  • Provide regular updates to the state Chapter Executive and other functional leaders; prepare reports and presentations for Chapter Board meetings and community events as requested.
  • Collaborate with Association staff across the state chapter regularly to advance mission priorities and provide policy expertise.
  • Participate in major events hosted by the state Chapter including Walk, galas, etc.
  • Performs other duties as assigned

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree required.
  • At least 5 years experience working in state government affairs setting; as a state legislative staff person; or as policy staff in the governor’s office or relevant state agency, preferably in Wisconsin.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

  • Has current contacts within the state legislature and executive branch, and with potential partners and collaborators in [State].
  • Understands, and has experience with the legislative, regulatory, and budget process in [State].
  • Familiar with Medicaid, aging, health, drug coverage, and long-term care issues.
  • Demonstrates the ability to anticipate, identify, organize, and analyze public policy opportunities.
  • Possess excellent written and oral communications skills.
  • Detail-oriented, adaptable, organized and able to successfully manage multiple projects and tasks.
  • Proven self-starter with excellent judgment and careful attention to detail.
  • Strong negotiation skills.
  • Ability to work effectively with diverse populations with a high level of integrity, diplomacy and initiative.
  • Must possess a valid driver’s license, good driving record, access to a reliable vehicle and proof of automobile insurance.
  • Must be able to lift 15 pounds.

Title: State Government Relations Director

Full Time: Based on 37.5 hours per week

Position Grade & Compensation: Grade 209 The Alzheimer's Association’s good faith expectation for the salary range for this role is between $85,000 – $95,000

Reports To: Territory Government Relations Director

Who We Are:

The Alzheimer’s Association is the leading voluntary health organization in Alzheimer’s care, support and research. Our mission is to lead the way to end Alzheimer's and all other dementia– by accelerating global research, driving risk reduction and early detection, and maximizing quality care and support.

The Alzheimer’s Association announced a landmark $100 million investment in research for 2023. This unparalleled commitment is illustrative of the momentum we are building in dementia research — our investments today will lead to breakthroughs tomorrow.

At the Alzheimer’s Association, our employees are at the core of all we do. Our network of more than 1,750 employees across the United States makes a difference each and every day for those impacted by Alzheimer’s and those at risk for the disease.

We warmly invite qualified applicants to consider this opportunity to make a life-changing impact on the millions living with Alzheimer’s, their caregivers and those that may develop the disease in the future. Read on to learn more about the role, then visit our website to explore who we are and why we've been recognized as a Best Place to Work for the last twelve years in a row.

At the Alzheimer's Association®, we believe that diverse perspectives are critical to achieving health equity — meaning that all communities have a fair and just opportunity for early diagnosis and access to risk reduction and quality care. The Association is committed to engaging underrepresented and underserved communities and responding with resources and education to address the disproportionate impact of Alzheimer’s and dementia.

The Alzheimer’s Association commitment remains steadfast in engaging all communities in our full mission. “Are you ready to unlock your potential? At Straumann Group we’re on an exciting journey of growth, innovation, and impact - driven by our mission to improve oral health and transform millions of lives worldwide. United by purpose, we bring our best selves to work every day, embracing a high-performance, player-learner culture that inspires collaboration, curiosity, and ambition. Here, you’ll have the opportunity to take charge of your own career, harnessing your skills, passion, and enthusiasm for learning to continually grow and progress. Together, we’re not just shaping brighter smiles, we’re unlocking the potential of people everywhere, including our own.”

About the job

As Senior Container Platform Engineer, you will design, automate, and operate secure, scalable Kubernetes-based platforms across campus, datacenter, and hybrid cloud environments. Working with Enterprise Architecture, Cloud, Security, Network, Platform Engineering, and application teams, you will help improve developer experience, platform reliability, and operational excellence.

Your Role

You will:

  • Design, build, and maintain enterprise container platforms using Kubernetes and related ecosystem tools.
  • Define standards for cluster architecture, multi-tenancy, workload isolation, upgrades, capacity, and lifecycle management.
  • Implement secure networking, ingress, load balancing, service mesh, DNS, certificate management, and traffic management.
  • Build hybrid connectivity across container platforms, cloud services, and on-premises environments.
  • Apply Kubernetes security controls, including RBAC, network policies, secrets management, image security, policy enforcement, and Zero Trust principles.
  • Automate provisioning and operations using Terraform, Ansible, Python, Git, REST APIs, and Infrastructure as Code.
  • Develop CI/CD and GitOps practices using tools such as Azure DevOps, GitHub Actions, Argo CD, or Flux.
  • Provide Level 3 support for complex incidents, including root cause analysis and problem management.
  • Manage upgrades, patching, backup and recovery, disaster recovery, and capacity planning.
  • Create documentation, reusable templates, engineering standards, and operational runbooks.

Your Profile

You bring:

  • Experience in infrastructure, cloud, platform, or systems engineering in an enterprise environment.
  • Hands-on Kubernetes and container platform engineering experience.
  • Practical knowledge of Kubernetes, container runtimes, Helm, and container orchestration.
  • Experience with AKS, EKS, OpenShift, Rancher, Tanzu, or similar platforms.
  • Good understanding of Kubernetes networking, ingress, service discovery, load balancing, network policies, and cluster security.
  • Experience with Azure and AWS cloud services, networking, identity, and hybrid connectivity.
  • Hands-on experience with Terraform, Ansible, Python, Git, REST APIs, and Infrastructure as Code.
  • Experience with CI/CD, DevOps practices, and observability tools such as Prometheus, Grafana, ELK/OpenSearch, Datadog, or similar.
  • Excellent written and spoken English.

Nice to have:

  • Kubernetes, Azure, AWS, or Terraform certifications.
  • Experience with Istio, Linkerd, Crossplane, Prisma Cloud, Aqua, Sysdig, Trivy, Snyk, API gateways, or developer platform tooling.

What Makes You a Great Fit

You enjoy solving complex technical problems and turning them into reliable, repeatable platform services. You communicate clearly, collaborate across global teams, and balance security, scalability, and developer experience. You bring a continuous improvement mindset and contribute to a learning culture by sharing knowledge and supporting the growth of others.


All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, or disability.

title: Surgical Tech Cert CST - Part-Time
