title: Event Producer - Hybrid (Project-Based)
description:
Position Overview

The Event Producer is primarily responsible for the successful planning and execution of corporate events, association events, keynotes, special events and branding activations. The Event Producer will lead and inspire event teams, manage expectations and work collaboratively to find creative solutions during the development of projects. The Event Producer will ensure that all the right steps/process are followed and that the results of the project are at the highest level of quality both creatively and financially. The Event Producer will provide design guidance, and oversight of the event production team. They will produce and stage all elements of a program, oversee show staff, forge positive relationships with client and verify final billing. The Event Producer is responsible for creating a Scope of Work relevant to the event in conjunction with Director or Associate Director of Event Production. The Event Producer will create programs that meet the client’s needs and are profitable for the company. This role is responsible for relaying all pertinent information to the Account Manager. The Event Producer reports to the Director, Event Production.

Important: This is a project-based role and not a permanent full-time position. Successful candidates will be considered for upcoming projects based on their experience, availability, and business needs. This position may be based out of any Encore market across Canada, including Montreal, Toronto, Calgary, or Vancouver. Candidates must be able to attend an Encore office and/or event site within their local market as business needs require.

Key Job Responsibilities

Organizational Leadership

• Properly reconcile events, specifically delivering a wrap report and ensuring that all administrative data and paperwork has been entered, submitted, cross checked, and reconciled across the entire project in conjunction with Project Coordinator.

• Develop and maintain strong relationships with clients at all levels of their organization and provide outstanding customer service while focusing on client retention.

• Responsible for compliance with established Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), Technical Standards and Production Standards.

• Communicate goals and objectives to Event Execution team members clearly and frequently.

• Lead by example in portraying a polished, professional image in accordance with the standards set forth in the Encore team member guidebook.

Sales and Marketing Support

• Partner with Sales during the proposal stage (including RFP assistance and/or proposal writing).

• Evaluate initial creative concepts, define deliverables and budgetary elements.

• Keep current with changing trends in event technology and design.

Event Pre-Production

• Maintain the event’s creative vision by bringing all elements/teams together from planning to execution.

• Consult with the Account Manager to prepare event budget, and review any scope changes throughout event pre-production.

• Collaboration with Encore Venue teams for any projects in Encore properties, if applicable.

• Participate in all project management elements, team meetings, benchmarks, etc.

• Arrange and attend client site inspections.

• Collaborate with Creative Producer to uphold event’s creative vision.

• Engage Media Lab to develop video, graphics and print materials.

• Engage Production Manager to oversee technical elements.

• Identify and mitigate risks to projects and solve issues before they affect production by collaborating with internal stakeholders.

• Partner with Production Manager on production schedule (provide information and recommendations where needed, etc.).

• Research and recommend suppliers, freelance support and talent where needed (i.e. build stage team, source greeters, registration supplier, etc.) Can include contract negotiation.

Event

• Maintain quality control throughout the entire show, while keeping event on scope.

• Ensure production budgets are well executed and remain profitable.

• Show call and assist in stage management as needed.

Post-Event

• Schedule and lead internal and client debriefs

• Collaborate with Account Manager, and Production Coordinator to review, approve and ensure any event POs have been submitted.

• Work with Account Manager, Production Coordinator, and finance on invoice approvals prior to client billing.

Relationship Management

• Assist in mentoring team members as necessary.

• Manage and build client relationships.

Job Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in relevant field preferred

• 5+ years of show production or audio visual experience required

• Onsite crew management experience

• Client relationship skills, strong written and oral communications skills, and detail oriented

• Knowledge of hospitality industry and sales processes required in addition to the ability to read and decipher financial reports and records

• Computer proficiency required including MS Office

Competency Group

Deliver World Class Service

• Hospitality

• Ownership

Do The Right Thing

• Demonstrates Self-Awareness

Drive Results

• Ensures Accountability

See The Big Picture

• Decision Quality

• Manages Complexity

Value People

• Collaborates

For more information on our Competency Group, refer to the Competency Based Talent Management page on Encore Connect by searching for the title or copy & pasting this URL Link (https://psav.sharepoint.com/sites/HR/SitePages/Competency-Supported-Talent-Management.aspx).

Hourly Pay Range: $40.00 - $80.00

The compensation offered for this role is determined based on the qualifications outlined in the job posting for the specified location. Final compensation is based on a number of factors including location, travel, relevant work experience, or particular skills and expertise. In addition, some positions may be eligible for other compensation such as potential overtime, bonuses or incentives.

We use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to help screen and/or assess applications for this role. These tools analyze information you provide (for example, your résumé or answers to questions using the chat to apply feature) to support our hiring team’s review. All hiring decisions include human judgment.

Work Environment

Hotel

Work is performed in a hotel/convention center environment with moderate exposure to outdoor temperatures and to dirt, sand and/or dust. The working conditions will vary between moderately quiet to noisy volumes. Team members will use high-end audio visual equipment and electrical components, and will be exposed to heights via lifts and ladders. Team members may be asked to work in multiple hotel locations. Working times will include irregular hours and on-call status including days, evenings, weekends and holidays. Team members must adhere to appearance guidelines as defined by PSAV based on an individual hotel or a representation of hotels in that city or area.

Office

Work is performed primarily in an office environment. Working times may include irregular hours and on-call status including days, evenings, weekends and holidays. Team members must adhere to appearance guidelines as defined by PSAV based in an office environment and when traveling, on an individual venue or a representation of venues in that city or area.

The above information on this description is not necessarily an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, skills, efforts, requirements or working conditions associated with the job. While this is intended to be an accurate reflection of the current job, management reserves the right to revise the job or to require that other or different tasks be performed as assigned.

Canada | Project-based engagements

Join our career network

We are building an ongoing roster of experienced Event Producers for project-based opportunities. This is an evergreen posting, not an advertisement for one specific assignment. Selected candidates may be contacted as needs arise based on project scope, location, timing, availability and relevant experience.


The opportunity

Event Producers lead the planning and delivery of live and hybrid event programs from early development through on-site execution and closeout. They bring teams, suppliers and creative and technical partners together around a clear vision, practical production plan and disciplined budget. The work requires confident client leadership, strong production judgment and the ability to solve issues calmly in fast-moving environments.


Typical engagement scope

  • Lead project planning and execution for corporate events, association events, keynotes, special events and brand activations.
  • Translate client objectives and creative concepts into a practical scope of work, production plan, schedule and budget.
  • Coordinate internal and external contributors, including technical production, creative, scenic, media, registration, talent and show-site teams.
  • Maintain the event’s creative vision while aligning deliverables, resources, timing, quality and financial parameters.
  • Provide clear, timely updates to the designated Encore project lead and relevant stakeholders throughout the engagement.
  • Lead or support client meetings, site inspections, production meetings, rehearsals, show calling, stage management and on-site execution as required.
  • Identify production risks early, recommend mitigation plans and resolve issues before they affect the event experience.
  • Complete agreed project closeout requirements, which may include debriefs, wrap reporting, invoice or purchase-order support, and final documentation.

What you may be responsible for

Pre-production

  • Contribute to proposals, RFP responses, creative development and preliminary estimates when included in the assignment.
  • Define deliverables, milestones, roles, dependencies and approval points with the project team.
  • Collaborate with account, project management, technical production, creative and venue teams.
  • Research and recommend qualified suppliers, freelance specialists and show personnel; support negotiations when authorized.
  • Develop or contribute to production schedules, run-of-show documents, staffing plans and client-facing production updates.

On site

  • Lead the assigned production workstream and maintain quality control, scope alignment and schedule discipline.
  • Direct show-site teams and vendor partners within the agreed chain of command.
  • Show call or provide stage-management support when required by the project scope.
  • Monitor changes, document decisions and escalate material impacts to schedule, cost, safety or client experience.

Post-event

  • Lead or participate in internal and client debriefs.
  • Provide complete, accurate project documentation and closeout materials by agreed deadlines.
  • Support reconciliation by validating assigned costs, supplier documentation and project records.


What you bring

  • Five or more years of event production, live show production or audiovisual production experience.
  • Demonstrated experience leading on-site crews, suppliers and multi-disciplinary project teams.
  • Strong client-facing communication, facilitation and relationship-management skills.
  • Experience developing production plans, schedules, scopes and budgets, with confidence reviewing financial information.
  • Sound knowledge of live-event workflows, hospitality environments and production standards.
  • Excellent organization, judgment, attention to detail and problem-solving skills.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office and common event-production and project-collaboration tools.
  • Relevant post-secondary education is an asset; equivalent practical experience is welcomed.


Engagement requirements

  • Ability to work flexible project schedules, which may include early mornings, evenings, weekends and holidays.
  • Ability to travel to event locations when required by the assignment.
  • Ability to work in offices, hotels, convention centres and other event environments where conditions and noise levels vary.
  • Compliance with site, client, safety, technical and production requirements applicable to each engagement.

Engagements arising from this posting are project-based and subject to a separate written agreement. The specific agreement will govern the services, fees, expenses, confidentiality, intellectual property, insurance and other terms applicable to the assignment. Reasonable accommodations are available during the selection process and, where applicable, in connection with an engagement.

title: Technical Graduate - Data Analysis & Data Science 2027
description:
• Deadline: Ongoing
  • Salary: Competitive
  • Location: Various locations
  • Degree required: 2:2 and above
  • Disciplines: Computer Science, Data, Analytics, Maths

At CGI, we empower the next generation of innovators to shape the future of technology and security. As part of #GenerationCGI, you’ll join a community of graduates who are turning ambition into action and possibility into progress.

As a Technical Graduate specialising in Data Analytics and Data Science, you’ll use data to uncover insights, solve complex problems and support better decisions. You could be analysing large datasets, developing data models, building data pipelines or exploring how artificial intelligence and machine learning can create meaningful outcomes.

You’ll be trusted with responsibility from the start, working alongside experienced colleagues on live projects across a range of industries. You’ll develop your technical expertise while helping clients transform data into practical solutions that make a real difference.

Your future duties and responsibilities:

In this role, you’ll apply your analytical and technical skills to help organisations understand their data, improve services and solve real-world challenges. The work will vary by project, giving you opportunities to develop experience across data analytics, data science and data engineering.

  • Analyse and interpret data: Explore complex datasets, identify patterns and communicate insights that support informed decisions.
  • Develop data models: Structure and model data so that it can be used effectively for analysis, reporting and operational services.
  • Build data solutions: Support the development of reliable data pipelines, analytical tools and software solutions.
  • Apply AI and machine learning: Explore technologies including machine learning, artificial intelligence and generative AI to address client challenges.
  • Present meaningful insights: Create reports and data visualisations that make complex information clear and accessible.
  • Collaborate across disciplines: Work with data engineers, software developers, analysts and client teams to design and deliver practical solutions.
  • Innovate alongside other graduates: Take part in early careers initiatives that go beyond your day-to-day role.

Every contribution you make will help deliver outcomes with lasting impact.

Locations

Opportunities are available in Aberdeen, Belfast, Edinburgh, Glasgow, Gloucester, London and Manchester.

As CGI is a consultancy, you may be required to work in different locations, so flexibility and a willingness to travel are key.

Required qualifications to be successful in this role:

We’re seeking ambitious graduates who are curious about data and excited by its potential to solve complex problems. You’ll bring an analytical mindset, an interest in technology and the willingness to keep learning as data, AI and cloud technologies continue to develop.

You should have:

  • A minimum 2:2 degree in data science, computer science, mathematics, statistics, engineering or a related STEM subject (some roles may require a 2:1).
  • Strong analytical thinking and problem-solving skills.
  • The ability to communicate technical information clearly, both verbally and in writing.
  • Curiosity and a willingness to research new technologies and approaches.
  • Flexibility to travel and work on projects across the UK.
  • Eligibility for Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) clearance, with many roles requiring higher National Security Vetting. This typically requires 5–10 years of continuous UK residency.

Technical skills we value include:

  • Data analytics and modelling: Experience exploring, analysing and structuring data to identify trends and generate insights.
  • Programming: Experience with Python or another language used for data analysis, software development or automation.
  • Data engineering: An understanding of data pipelines, data transformation, storage and data quality.
  • Data visualisation: The ability to present data clearly through reports, dashboards or visualisation tools.
  • Artificial intelligence: An interest in machine learning, artificial intelligence and generative AI.
  • Cloud technologies: Exposure to cloud computing platforms and cloud-based data services.
  • Software and operational practices: Familiarity with software development, version control or site reliability engineering would be beneficial.
  • Emerging technology: An interest in technology research, connected systems or the Internet of Things would be an advantage.

Why Join Us?

At CGI, you’ll be part of a culture that celebrates diversity, inclusion and collaboration, where your perspective is valued and your ideas contribute to meaningful outcomes.

Your journey starts with a structured Early Careers Induction Programme, giving you the foundations to succeed, along with 24/7 e-learning and opportunities to gain professional certifications that build your expertise. You’ll also join our Student Kick-start Initiative, where you’ll collaborate with other graduates on creative projects that deliver impact beyond your day-to-day role.

CGI is an unconditionally inclusive workplace where you are respected, your voice is heard and you can be yourself. We were recognised in the Sunday Times Best Places to Work List 2025 and named a UK ‘Best Employer’ by the Financial Times. We proudly hold a Gold Award in recognition of our support of the Armed Forces Corporate Covenant.

Benefits

Along with a competitive salary and a £1,000 joining bonus, you’ll enjoy benefits that support every stage of your journey. You’ll share in CGI’s success through our matched share scheme, have access to private healthcare, well-being programmes and professional training, and build financial security with a competitive pension. Beyond the day job, you’ll connect with others through graduate networks, diversity groups and social clubs that make your time at CGI both rewarding and enjoyable.

What you can expect from us:

Together, as owners, let’s turn meaningful insights into action.

Life at CGI is rooted in ownership, teamwork, respect and belonging. Here, you’ll reach your full potential because…

You are invited to be an owner from day 1 as we work together to bring our Dream to life. That’s why we call ourselves CGI Partners rather than employees. We benefit from our collective success and actively shape our company’s strategy and direction.

Your work creates value. You’ll develop innovative solutions and build relationships with teammates and clients while accessing global capabilities to scale your ideas, embrace new opportunities, and benefit from expansive industry and technology expertise.

You’ll shape your career by joining a company built to grow and last. You’ll be supported by leaders who care about your health and well-being and provide you with opportunities to deepen your skills and broaden your horizons.

That same commitment to fairness extends to how we use technology. To support our recruitment team, AI tools may be used to help assess applications though they never replace human judgement. All hiring decisions remain entirely in the hands of our recruitment professionals.

Come join our team—one of the largest IT and business consulting services firms in the world.

title: Senior Project Manager
description:
The Senior Project Manager leads complex industrial construction and service projects from planning through closeout, ensuring safe, timely, high-quality, and financially successful execution. This role directs project teams and subcontractors, manages schedules, budgets, scope, risk, documentation, and customer communication, and mentors Project Managers while protecting the Company’s operational and commercial interests.

Founded in 1989, Lee Industrial Contracting is a 100% employee-owned company based in Pontiac, Michigan. We are the premier industrial contractor of choice for a broad variety of equipment installation, construction, and service projects. As employee-owners, we all strive to demonstrate the core values of Safety, Teamwork, Integrity, and Dedication each and every day. As a team, our mission is to provide our customers with the finest people, material, and equipment available. We encourage anyone who shares our values to apply today!

We are proud to offer our employees:

  • Comprehensive Training Programs
  • Paid Holidays Upon Hire
  • Competitive Medical, Dental, and Vision Insurance
  • HSA with Employer Contribution
  • Paid Time Off
  • Company Paid Short-Term Disability & Life Insurance
  • Safety Bonus Program
  • Employee Stock Ownership Program
  • Work Travel Incentive
  • Holiday Bonus
  • And so much more!

Responsibilities:

  • Lead the planning and execution of complex industrial construction, service, and general contracting projects from preconstruction through closeout.
  • Direct multiple, concurrent projects by managing scope, schedules, budgets, logistics, engineering, safety, quality, risk, documentation, and financial performance.
  • Translate customer expectations into clear project objectives and coordinate effectively with estimators, department managers, safety, field supervision, subcontractors, vendors, and other stakeholders.
  • Develop and maintain detailed work breakdown structures, project schedules, milestones, budgets, forecasts, and performance analytics using Procore and related tools.
  • Manage project changes and scope control, prepare change-order proposals, assess project risk, and implement timely response strategies.
  • Coordinate self-performed work and subcontractor activities to ensure crews, materials, permits, and resources are scheduled and available to meet project commitments.
  • Monitor and communicate project costs, revenue, gross profit, cash flow, billing, collections, and overall financial outlook to key stakeholders.
  • Ability to develop project scopes and internal estimates or subcontractor support.
  • Protect the Company’s interests and legal rights through thorough documentation and timely communication with customers, subcontractors, vendors, and internal partners.
  • Lead the development of high-performance teams through effective supervision, training, coaching, and mentoring; serve as a peer coach or mentor as assigned.
  • Provide staff with regular, actionable feedback and complete employee performance appraisals accurately and on time.
  • Motivate the project team, promote accountability and collaboration, and maintain a positive, safe, and productive work environment.
  • Respond to after-hours emergency calls and coordinate the appropriate resources when required.

Job Requirements:

  • 10+ years of industrial and/or heavy commercial contracting project management experience.
  • Bachelor’s Degree in Construction Management, Engineering, or Architecture or equivalent industry experience.
  • Understand the sequencing and deliverable of trade disciplines including but not limited to electrical, pipefitting, rigging, foundations, structural steel, etc.
  • Well-organized, detail-oriented and ability to be self-directed to problem solve issues.
  • Proven experience managing multiple construction projects simultaneously.
  • Strong organizational skills applied to Document Control and Close Out.
  • Strong proactive positive attitude with commitment to Safety.
  • Proficient with Excel and Microsoft Project preferred.
  • Possess exceptional verbal and written communication skills.
  • Able to travel occasionally and work on-call.

Physical Requirements:

  • Mobility & Navigation: The ability to walk on uneven surfaces, climb stairs and ladders, stoop, kneel, and bend while traversing active construction sites.

About the Sacramento T-STRTP

The Sacramento T-STRTP (Transitional-Short Term Residential Therapeutic Program) serves children and youth ages 11–17 in a supportive, strength-based, culturally competent, youth-centered, family-driven, trauma-informed, family-like environment. The program provides short-term, individualized treatment designed to help children and youth stabilize at-risk behaviors that may interfere with permanency, with the goal of reducing re-entry into STRTP or higher levels of care. title: QMAP ~ Memory Care ~ Centennial - PT
description:
Med Tech

Part-time/PRN

Pay Range: $20.00 - $22.00

Non-exempt

Schedule to be discussed during interview.

Make a difference by providing great care and love for our treasured residents!

At MorningStar Senior Living, we talk a lot about culture. In fact, we rather obsess about it. For without a transformative culture, we cannot begin to elevate and celebrate the lives of our resident-heroes and be ourselves changed for the good in the process. So, we seek great hearts, other people like us, who care and want to do work that matters. We select people like us who believe that the most satisfying life is one that is outward-bound and rooted in servant-leadership.

JOB SUMMARY

The Med Care Manager/QMAP must administer, pour, pass, and document all routinely prescribed medications per physician orders under the direction of the Wellness Director and as approved by the State Medication Administration Regulations. You will quickly learn how each resident prefers to take their medication. Some may even play a game of hide and seek, pressing you to find where they may be in the community when it’s time for their medication.

BENEFITS

  • Health Insurance offerings such as medical, dental, and vision insurance
  • Other Insurance offerings such as life, disability, accident, and critical illness insurance
  • 401k plan with matching
  • HSA options
  • Employee assistance programs
  • Paid sick, vacation and birthday!
  • Career development programs and opportunity for advancement
  • Charitable and philanthropic opportunities
  • Tuition Reimbursement
  • Free shift meal!

POSITION OVERVIEW

  • Administer and document regularly prescribed medications per the Medication Administration record observing the five rights for safe administering of meds and per physician orders.
  • Order meds from the pharmacy when and as prescribed, 7 days prior to running out of meds, and as requested by the Wellness Director to ensure that residents always have medications available. Ensure these medications arrive, if not notify the Wellness Director within 24 hours.
  • Immediately after administering medication to a resident, document in the resident’s medical record those medications given. Date and initial the bubble pack after taking the medication from it.
  • Observe and report to the licensed nurse reactions and side effects of medication administered to the residents.
  • Take and record vital signs prior to administration of medications which could affect or change vital signs as ordered by the Physician or Wellness Director.
  • Administer PRN medications, per physician order.
  • Required to report any medication error to the Wellness Director immediately.
  • Assist with development and review of the resident’s care plan in conjunction with other disciplines
  • Ensure residents privacy, respect and dignity
  • Detect, correct, and report unsafe conditions which may result in harm to a resident
  • Assure physical comfort, safety, and mental well-being of residents
  • Assist in daily requirements and tasks in care and treatment of residents, such as toileting, grooming, bathing, feeding, dressing, observing intake of food, care of hair and nails, moving residents from area to area, responding to calls, etc.

QUALIFICATIONS

· Demonstration of our Core Values: Love, Kindness, Honesty, Goodness, Fairness, Respect.

· License/Certification: Successful completion of state approved Medication Administration training, First Aid certification as required by the ALF regulations. QMAP in the state of CO.

· Education/Experience: Minimum high school diploma or equivalent. Prefer some previous experience in health-care, must have experience working in Assisted Living or Memory Care with a good work record, and experience administering medication in an assisted living setting. Must be capable of making decisions with the interest of the residents at heart and supportive of company policies and decisions.

· Continuing Education: as required by law and must attend monthly in-service education and training within the community.

· Other: Must be able to read and write English. Must have the ability to read and interpret documents such as safety rules, operating and maintenance instructions, procurement manuals, etc. must have good communication skills and must be able to effectively communicate in English and understand and follow written and oral directions. Provide maximum resident-care services within limits defined by delegated tasks. Must show good judgement in recognizing symptoms indicative of a resident’s change in condition. Work with licensed nurses; be aware of limitations and not attempt to exceed these limitations.

· Job Knowledge: Perform the functions of medication administration. Knowledge of required Medication Administration Procedures. Good understanding of basis of universal precautions to avoid infection of residents and self or contamination of equipment and supplies.

· Industry Experience: Minimum three years’ experience in senior living preferred and a passion to work with seniors. Previous experience with an Assisted Living community.

*Team members who are scheduled to work 24 or more hours per week are eligible for benefits, families of said team members will also be eligible.

title: Global Head of DSO Education Services
description:
Are you ready to unlock your potential? At Straumann Group we’re on an exciting journey of growth, innovation, and impact - driven by our mission to improve oral health and transform millions of lives worldwide. United by purpose, we bring our best selves to work every day, embracing a high-performance, player-learner culture that inspires collaboration, curiosity, and ambition. Here, you’ll have the opportunity to take charge of your own career, harnessing your skills, passion, and enthusiasm for learning to continually grow and progress. Together, we’re not just shaping brighter smiles, we’re unlocking the potential of people everywhere, including our own.

The global dental industry is evolving rapidly. As dental practices increasingly join larger networks and Dental Service Organizations (DSOs), new opportunities are emerging to transform how oral healthcare is delivered.


At Straumann Group, our Global Enterprise Solutions team builds long-term strategic partnerships with leading DSOs worldwide, bringing together our comprehensive portfolio of dental solutions, technologies, and services to help our partners grow and deliver better patient outcomes.

The Global Head of DSO Education Services plays a pivotal role in defining and executing a cohesive global educational service strategy that’s robust, standardized, repeatable and scalable for our DSO customer target group. This individual will create and execute a clinical excellence strategy to establish Straumann Group as the partner of choice for clinical excellence in the field of Surgical Implantology, Restorative, Orthodontics and Digital Dentistry.

Your role


Set the strategy and value proposition

  • Define and champion the Enterprise Education vision, value proposition and global strategy, addressing the talent and capability challenges facing DSOs
  • Develop short- and long-term strategies to scale and commercialise education across clinical, business and leadership domains.
  • Translate DSO needs into differentiated propositions for C-suite leaders, providers, practice teams and platform teams.

Build the education architecture and customer offer

  • Create learning pathways that connect clinical excellence with business performance, leadership capability and effective team practice.
  • Develop customer segmentation and tiering strategies that make the offer relevant to different DSO needs and maturity levels.
  • Design scalable education concepts that combine in-person, digital and blended formats, working with the Education Architecture & Design team to ensure effective and efficient delivery.
  • Ensure the offer reflects the breadth of the Straumann Group portfolio, including digital solutions and new launches.

Create a scalable delivery and commercial model

  • Establish frameworks, processes and governance needed to design, contract, deliver and continuously improve education programmes for DSO customers.
  • Develop scalable delivery models especially focussed on in person/live patient training
  • Define how LMS platforms and other learning technologies can improve the customer experience and support future integration with top-tier customers.
  • Partner with regional and country organisations across NAM, EMEA and APAC to implement the global strategy while adapting delivery to local needs.

Shape the offer with customers and internal partners

  • Build strong relationships with DSO C-suite stakeholders, including Chief Medical Officers and CCOs across top- and mid-tier customers, to understand needs and shape relevant solutions.
  • Partner with the Consulting team to connect business education pathways with DSO network assessments and broader transformation priorities.
  • Work closely with Business Units and ITI to represent Enterprise needs and adapt relevant content for DSO environments.
  • Collaborate across Enterprise Solutions to keep education content current, portfolio-complete and aligned with customer priorities.

Enable the organisation to deliver

  • Define the capabilities and training requirements for internal Clinical Education Specialists (CES), including course content, training materials and web-based learning.
  • Equip regional and country teams to deliver the proposition consistently through clear frameworks, tools, training and implementation guidance.
  • Act as an internal advocate for Enterprise Education, building awareness and alignment across Straumann Group functions and markets.
  • Develop and manage Enterprise Key Opinion Leader relationships in support of the global education strategy.

Measure impact and improve performance

  • Establish education KPIs and reporting at global, regional, customer and programme levels.
  • Track adoption, learner experience and capability outcomes, and use evidence to refine the offer and demonstrate value to customers and the business.

Your profile

What you bring

  • Bachelor’s degree in education, business, healthcare or a related field, or equivalent experience.
  • 7+ years of experience in enterprise education, services, business development or programme management.
  • Proven ability to design and scale capability programmes or lead complex programmes from strategy through delivery.
  • Understanding of clinical education and how it connects to business, leadership and workforce needs.
  • Experience leading global, cross-functional initiatives and engaging senior stakeholders.

Nice to haves
Experience working in clinical processes in implantology, restorative and Orthodontics departments.


This role operates our hybrid working model 60% presence in office, 40% flexible working. Regular travel (30- 40%) is required.

What makes you a great fit?
You can combine strategic thinking with a focus on execution and are conformable navigating changing priorities in complex environments with an entrepreneurial mindset.
You are comfortable building trusted relationships across cross-functional business groups.
You are collaborative and take ownership of outcomes and use customer insights to improve solutions.

title: Overnight Guest Experience Associate (Luxury Butler Services)
description:
The compensation for this position includes a base rate of $16.00 per hour with the potential to earn $25.00 per hour after gratuity.

As a Butler at Nemacolin, you will become a trusted, highly personalized resource for guests throughout their stay, anticipating needs, orchestrating details, and creating an effortless sense of care from arrival through departure. As part of a resort that features Forbes Five-Star and AAA Five-Diamond-rated luxury accommodations, you will bring warmth, discretion, sophistication, and exceptional attention to detail to every interaction. By understanding individual preferences and coordinating seamlessly across the resort, you will transform requests into thoughtful experiences and ensure every detail of a guest’s journey feels considered, personal, and beautifully executed.

  • A seamless connection to the resort, giving guests confident access to accommodations, dining, spa, recreation, transportation, activities, entertainment, events, and surrounding attractions while coordinating the details that bring each experience together

  • A highly personalized hospitality role within a resort that features Forbes Five-Star and AAA Five-Diamond luxury accommodations
  • Meaningful daily interaction with discerning guests whose expectations call for intuition, discretion, warmth, and exceptional attention to detail
  • A dynamic environment where no two guest experiences are alike, requiring resourcefulness, composure, and the ability to coordinate multiple priorities
  • Close collaboration with departments throughout the resort, providing an opportunity to build broad hospitality knowledge and strong cross-functional relationships
  • A role that combines personalized service with hands-on guest support, including luggage assistance, accommodation preparation, deliveries, and other personal-service requests
  • A schedule shaped by guest needs and resort operations, including nights, weekends, holidays, and split shifts
  • A physically active role requiring the ability to bend and lift up to 25 pounds
  • Opportunities to deepen expertise in luxury hospitality, guest relations, service recovery, and personalized experience design

What You Bring

  • A naturally intuitive approach to hospitality, with the ability to recognize what a guest may need before being asked
  • Warmth, sophistication, discretion, and the confidence to build trusted relationships with discerning guests
  • Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively across departments
  • Strong organization and follow-through, particularly when managing multiple requests and highly individualized details
  • Sound judgment, composure, and resourcefulness in a fast-paced environment
  • A polished professional presence and genuine commitment to exceptional guest service
  • Adaptability and flexibility to respond to changing guest needs, resort priorities, and varied schedules
  • The desire to deepen a career in luxury hospitality through increasingly sophisticated guest-facing experiences

Qualifications

  • High school diploma or equivalent required, with at least two years of customer service or related experience preferred
  • Previous luxury hospitality, guest services, butler, concierge, or similarly personalized service experience preferred
  • Ability to communicate fluently in English and build professional relationships with guests, colleagues, and business partners
  • Ability to learn and confidently use Microsoft Office, HOST, and other systems required to document and coordinate guest experiences
  • Strong organizational, multitasking, and problem-solving abilities, with the capacity to remain effective in a fast-paced environment
  • Valid driver’s license and ability to work varied schedules, including nights, weekends, holidays, and split shifts based on guest needs
  • Must be at least 18 years of age and able to bend and lift up to 25 pounds

Additional Information

This job description reflects the primary responsibilities, expectations, and qualifications associated with the position. It is not intended to be a comprehensive list of all duties, responsibilities, or activities. Responsibilities may evolve or be assigned as needed to support operational excellence, business needs, and exceptional guest service.

Begin a Meaningful Career at Nemacolin

At Nemacolin resort in Pennsylvania’s Laurel Highlands, foundational roles form the heart of the guest experience and the beginning of many long-term careers. Each day brings the opportunity to learn new skills, build confidence, and contribute to a team that values hard work, kindness, and pride in service. Whether entering hospitality for the first time or continuing a professional journey, the environment encourages growth, connection, and steady advancement.

Associate team members from a wide range of experiences come together to create something exceptional, supported by leaders who provide guidance, recognition, and encouragement along the way. Many leaders within the resort began in hourly roles, building successful careers through dedication, mentorship, and continuous learning.

Growth & Development

  • Paid training and structured onboarding
  • Hands-on learning and cross-department opportunities
  • Clear pathways for advancement and internal promotion
  • Recognition through individual and team honors

Benefits & Everyday Perks

  • Competitive hourly wages and attractive 401(k) program
  • Medical, dental, and vision coverage for eligible associates
  • Paid time off and holiday compensation
  • Discounted associate meals and uniform services
  • Savings across resort dining, retail, spa, and activities
  • Exclusive access to The Rec Center, The Market, The Pub, and the Wisteria associate community

A role at Nemacolin opens the door to skill-building, meaningful relationships, and a future shaped through experience and opportunity.

Bring your passion. Grow your career. Create Real Life Magic.

About Nemacolin

A private, family-owned, and woman-owned luxury resort unlike anything else in the hospitality industry, Nemacolin spans more than 2,200 breathtaking acres in Pennsylvania’s Laurel Highlands. Recognized by Forbes Travel Guide, AAA, and Preferred Hotels & Resorts, this four-season destination blends refined hospitality with creativity, craftsmanship, and a spirit of adventure that defines every guest and member experience.

Distinctive accommodations, immersive experiences, and a culture grounded in artistry and service excellence come together to create a setting where guests, members, and associates find inspiration. Across the resort, Real Life Magic is brought to life through meaningful moments, genuine connection, and a shared commitment to delivering something truly exceptional.

Visit Nemacolin.com to step inside the story, explore the experiences, and discover what draws people to Nemacolin. Then, imagine where this opportunity could take you as part of your own remarkable journey.

title: Senior Manager Patient and Community Outreach
description:
How many people can answer the question, "What do you do for a living?" with the answer, "I help find cures for cancer." At Blood Cancer United, employees take our mission seriously. Whether you work in one of our regions, are an accountant at the national office or a specialist in our Information Resource Center, you work each day on making our bold goal a reality: to enable patients with blood cancer to gain more than one million years of life by 2040. Join us and give new meaning to the word, "job."

Summary: The role of the Patient & Community Outreach Senior Manager is to implement strategies in support of Blood Cancer United’s goals including: conduct outreach to raise awareness of and connect more patients with Blood Cancer United, as soon after diagnosis as possible, with an emphasis on reaching underserved populations; build community awareness of and trust in Blood Cancer United as a source of information and support; provide ongoing support and education and facilitate access to quality care for patients and caregivers; and develop local and regional collaborations with both healthcare professionals and community leaders to further these aims.

The Patient & Community Outreach Senior Manager will provide or coordinate information, services, community education, and outreach to patients, caregivers, survivors, and healthcare professionals in assigned coverage areas. This role will serve as a key mission leader in the region for which the Patient & Community Outreach Senior Manager is responsible.

Supervises: Volunteers; and/or Patient & Community Outreach Manager(s), Community Outreach Specialists, and/or temporary staff

Duties and Responsibilities:
Community Engagement and Health Equity

  • Promote Blood Cancer United as an essential resource for disease, treatment, and support information for blood cancer patients and families.
  • Design and implement outreach initiatives to expand Blood Cancer United reach, including conducting culturally tailored outreach within underserved communities across the local region.
  • Foster and maintain relationships with community-based organizations and healthcare delivery institutions.

Volunteer Engagement and Leadership

  • Engage volunteer leaders to better reach local oncology professionals and key stakeholders, to build relationships with Blood Cancer United region colleagues, and to assist with patient outreach and community events.
  • Recruit, train, and manage a volunteer infrastructure to support all aspects of the role.

Community Education and Services

  • Create resources and programs that allow for deeper patient engagement throughout the cancer journey.
  • Conduct community-based patient education programs in select markets, including underserved areas.
  • Assess the need for support, services, and education for patients and providers in the Region.

Mission Integration

  • Collaborate and partner with internal stakeholders, including other Education & Services staff, Region Executive Directors, and philanthropy colleagues to ensure joint planning, mutually beneficial support, and effective advancement toward overarching Blood Cancer United goals and strategies.
  • Partner with Blood Cancer United colleagues to provide information about the Blood Cancer United mission to internal and external stakeholders, including staff, potential volunteers, donors, and funders.
  • Partner with Blood Cancer United public policy and advocacy staff to identify advocates and patient stories and maintain engagement in policy initiatives.
    Staff and/or Project Management

    • Serving as a supervisor to Patient & Community Outreach Manager(s), Community Outreach Specialist, and/or temporary staff; and/or

#LI-Hybrid

title: Temporary Gig - Israeli Hebrew Research Participant, NYC
location: New York, New York, United States
description:
Mindrift is running a research study on how people use their phones, apps and everyday digital tools, and how that differs across languages and cultures. We’re looking for native Hebrew speakers in New York to join a paid, 3-day in-person study in Midtown Manhattan.

Why your language matters

Most technology is still designed with English speakers in mind. This study helps researchers understand how people who communicate in Hebrew actually use their devices, so future products work better for them.

What you’ll do

  • Spend 1-3 days with our research team in Midtown Manhattan.
  • Walk us through how you use your phone and favourite apps in daily life.
  • Share examples of your everyday phone activity with the research team. You decide what’s included.
  • Fill in a short questionnaire about your habits.

Who we’re looking for

  • 18+ and currently living in NYC.
  • A native Hebrew speaker who grew up in Israel.
  • You use Hebrew in everyday life: texting friends, email, notes.
  • You’ve used a smartphone as your main personal phone for 3+ years.
  • Comfortable communicating in English.
  • Available for 3 consecutive days (Mon–Wed or Thu–Sat), starting October 16 on Friday.
  • Not currently employed by a tech or AI company.

Great fit for international students, people new to NYC, and anyone between jobs or with a flexible schedule.

Compensation

$1,200–1,600 for the full study.

Simple and transparent

Participation is voluntary and covered by a signed consent form that explains exactly what’s involved. You can ask questions at any point and stop whenever you like.

How to apply

Register on Mindrift and complete a short screening questionnaire. We’ll confirm your session dates once you’re shortlisted.

Apply now

title: Your Voice Matters: Paid 90-Minute Research Session
description:
About the study

Mindrift is conducting an in-person research study exploring how people communicate and interact in everyday group conversations.
We're looking for adults in the Santa Clara Valley (South Bay) area to join a paid, guided conversation session.

We welcome people from all backgrounds, with different accents and first languages. No special experience is needed. Just come as you are!

What you'll do

  • Check in on site with our coordinator, who will guide you through every step.
    Join a small group of 2–4 people for a guided conversation led by a trained moderator.
  • Talk about everyday, non-sensitive topics, such as planning a birthday celebration or making everyday decisions.
  • Take part in a session of about 75 minutes. The conversation is recorded on video and audio for research purposes.

Who we're looking for

  • 18-64 years of age
  • Living in or able to travel to Santa Clara Valley (South Bay), California.
  • Comfortable holding a conversation in English. Non-native speakers and all accents are welcome!
  • Comfortable being recorded on video and audio during the session.
  • Able to attend one in-person session on a weekday between November 2026 and March 2027.
  • Have not taken part in this study before. Each person participates once.

Students, working professionals, and people from all walks of life are welcome to apply.
No previous experience is required.

Compensation

$110 for one 75-minute session, paid through Mindrift after you complete the session. Travel costs are not covered.

Simple and transparent

Participation is voluntary and covered by a signed consent form that explains exactly what's involved, including how recordings are used and stored. You can ask questions at any point and choose to withdraw from the study.

How to apply

Register on Mindrift and complete a short screening questionnaire. If you meet the eligibility requirements, we’ll invite you to book a session at a time that works for you.

Research sessions will take place from November 2026 through March 2027.

title: Associate Transportation Planner
location: Washington, District of Columbia, United States
description:
For nearly 40 years, Nelson\Nygaard has led the transportation planning field with our values-driven approach. We’ve always been guided by the principle of putting people first—designing transportation systems for people, not just cars. This also extends to how we operate as a firm. We were founded by two women who believed in the benefits of a more egalitarian workplace, where leadership and creativity can blossom at all levels and where diversity is a core strength. Today, we are 170 talented and dedicated people in 15 offices across the U.S. and Canada who continue to live by those values. What unites us at Nelson\Nygaard is our steadfast commitment to make the world more just, more sustainable, more connected, and more beautiful.

Nelson\Nygaard offers a dynamic and self-directed work environment that is fast-paced, collaborative, and fun. This is your opportunity to work with one of the most innovative groups of planners and engineers in North America, including highly talented junior and support staff. Our firm culture is built upon diversity and creativity.

About You

  • You’re resourceful, curious, communicative, and enthusiastic.
  • You’re passionate about how transportation can make the world a better, more equitable place.
  • You bring energy and commitment to your teams and clients to do great work, together.
  • You want to grow and evolve as a planning professional.

Responsibilities

Our Washington DC Associate Transportation Planner will focus on planning for municipalities, agencies, universities, and private clients. Depending on your skills and our project needs, responsibilities may include research, data collection and analysis, mapping, visual communications, writing and editing technical and public-facing reports, developing presentations and outreach materials, leading task work and client communication, and supporting business development tasks. You will work both independently and as part of a team.

Qualifications and Requirements

Above all, we are looking for someone who:

  • Has a passion for sustainable transportation planning;
  • Is an inquisitive self-starter and a natural problem solver;
  • Understands the connection between transportation and equity and is committed to incorporating equity, diversity, and inclusion into their work;
  • Is interested in working with our diverse clients and communities across the U.S. and Canada to create more equitable, livable, and sustainable mobility systems;
  • Has experience, exposure, and passion for transportation planning work.

Candidates must have one of the following prerequisites:

  • A master’s degree in planning or an equivalent degree with a specialization in transportation planning and 0-2 years of relevant experience; OR
  • A bachelor’s degree in a related field and 1-3 years of experience in transportation planning; other relevant degrees and concentrations include, but are not limited to, civil/traffic engineering, transportation operations, urban/city/regional planning, public health, urban design, geography, and landscape architecture.

The ideal candidate will demonstrate ability in at least three of the following areas:

  • Excellent skills in writing and storytelling, oral presentation, data analysis, and/or problem solving;
  • Experience incorporating equity, diversity, and inclusion into academic and/or professional work;
  • Familiarity with current and recent transportation, planning, and development issues in the DC region and/or another place important to you;
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, Word, and PowerPoint;
  • Experience with mapping platforms (GIS), graphics (Illustrator, InDesign, SketchUp), modeling (Synchro, TransCAD), and/or database analysis (R, Python);
  • Ability to manage multiple deadlines and communicate effectively with project managers, colleagues, and project partners;
  • Proficiency in Spanish or other foreign languages.

Strong candidates will have a passion for advancing equity and accessibility through community-based efforts, including engagement with BIPOC communities, and will demonstrate an ability to work effectively with diverse communities.

Salary and Benefits

The annual salary range equivalent for this position is $72,965 - $89,180, depending on qualifications and years of experience.

Benefits include medical, dental, and vision insurance; pre-tax transit and bicycling benefits; a 401k program; life insurance; and paid time off. Additionally, we offer opportunities for in-person and in-office collaboration as well as flexibility for work from home up to 2 days per week.

Applying for the Position

To apply, please click on the 'Apply Online' link. Qualified and interested candidates must submit the following items:

  • Cover letter
  • Resume
  • Work samples that highlight your skills. Please do not exceed 6 MB.

At Nelson\Nygaard we believe that inclusion spurs creativity, and that innovation is born from an engaged culture of diverse people and ideas. By moving beyond barriers and stereotypes of gender, race, color, religion, national origin, ancestry, age, medical condition, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, and veteran status, we are committed to building an organization that reflects the diversity of the communities and clients we serve. We strongly encourage applications from Black, Indigenous, People of Color (BIPOC), immigrants, LGBTQ individuals, people with disabilities, and members of ethnic minorities.   • Collaborate with internal teams, including disbursement and post-closing, to ensure a seamless transition from closing through funding and recording.

title: Order-to-Cash Solution Architect
description:
Call to action

Are you ready to unlock your potential? At Straumann Group we’re on an exciting journey of growth, innovation, and impact - driven by our mission to improve oral health and transform millions of lives worldwide. United by purpose, we bring our best selves to work every day, embracing a high-performance, player-learner culture that inspires collaboration, curiosity, and ambition. Here, you’ll have the opportunity to take charge of your own career, harnessing your skills, passion, and enthusiasm for learning to continually grow and progress. Together, we’re not just shaping brighter smiles, we’re unlocking the potential of people everywhere, including our own.

Intro

As our Order to Cash Solution Architect, you will shape the technology architecture that enables efficient, reliable end-to-end Order to Cash (O2C) processes across Straumann Group.

Working closely with Customer Service, Commercial, Finance, Supply Chain, and Technology teams, you will connect business needs with scalable solutions across SAP S/4HANA, customer-facing platforms, manufacturing systems, internal enterprise applications, and third-party solutions.

Your work will span customer and order workflows, master data, fulfillment, billing, intercompany processes, and system integrations. Success in this role means creating practical architecture that works across platforms, supports business continuity, and can evolve as our customer and operational needs change.

Your Role

You will:

  • Shape the technology strategy and architecture for end-to-end O2C capabilities, ensuring alignment with business priorities and enterprise architecture principles.
  • Partner with Commercial, Customer Service, Supply Chain, Finance, and Technology stakeholders to identify opportunities to simplify processes and improve technology-enabled outcomes.
  • Lead solution and integration design across SAP S/4HANA and connected customer, manufacturing, and enterprise platforms.
  • Design scalable integration approaches using application programming interfaces (APIs), interfaces, events, and workflow-based patterns where appropriate.
  • Support cross-entity and intercompany processes, including order flows, billing, settlement, reconciliation, and related financial data dependencies.
  • Translate complex business requirements into practical, scalable technology solutions and evaluate relevant platforms or vendor solutions.
  • Configure, implement, support, and continuously improve O2C solutions and their integration points.
  • Analyze recurring incidents and process inefficiencies, identify root causes, and develop sustainable improvements.
  • Lead customer technology integrations, digital-solution rollouts to new markets, and other customer fulfillment initiatives.
  • Coordinate delivery across business teams, Technology teams, external vendors, consulting partners, and contractors while minimizing operational disruption.

Your Profile

Essential

  • Hands-on experience designing and implementing SAP Order to Cash solutions covering order management, fulfillment, billing, and integration with other applications.
  • Good knowledge of SAP S/4HANA O2C processes and their underlying data dependencies.
  • Experience integrating SAP with customer-facing platforms, manufacturing or order-intake systems, or other enterprise applications.
  • Practical knowledge of integration technologies and formats such as IDoc, REST APIs, XML, and JSON.
  • Understanding of customer master data, account structures, order management, fulfillment, billing, and intercompany flows.
  • Experience translating business requirements into technology and integration architecture.
  • Experience leading technology implementations involving cross-functional business and technical stakeholders.
  • Ability to communicate complex technical concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.

Nice to have

  • Experience with workflow-driven customer platforms, manufacturing execution systems, order-intake systems, or make-to-order environments.
  • SAP Sales and Distribution certification.
  • Experience mentoring colleagues or guiding teams in both operational and strategic work.

title: Head Prosthetic Lab Business Unit - North America
description:
Commercial Head, North America PLBU

Prosthetics Lab Business Unit | North America

Department/Entity

PLBU

Reports to

Head of Region (solid line) and Head of PLBU (dotted line)

Region

North America

Travel

Regional and international travel as required

About Straumann Group

The Straumann Group is a leading global provider of dental technologies and solutions, dedicated to advancing oral health and restoring patients' smiles worldwide. Headquartered in Basel, Switzerland, the Group develops, manufactures and markets products and services across implantology, restorative dentistry, orthodontics, digital dentistry and biomaterials. Its solutions range from dental implants and CAD/CAM prosthetics to digital workflows and clear aligners, helping dental professionals deliver predictable, high-quality care.

Straumann Operations in North America

Straumann's North American organization plays a strategic role in delivering the Group's mission, supporting dental professionals and driving innovation in the U.S. and Canada. The region manages sales, distribution, manufacturing, training and technical support for a comprehensive portfolio of dental solutions, including implant systems, prosthetics, digital tools and practice-oriented services. Prosthetics is one of Straumann Group's most attractive growth opportunities.

Position Summary

The Commercial Head, North America PLBU leads the PLBU business and sales agenda across the region and is accountable for sustainable revenue growth, profitability, market development and customer adoption. The role translates PLBU and Commercial Enablement priorities into a clear mid- to long-term regional business and sales plan, co-creates the sales roadmap and go-to-market strategy, and leads disciplined commercial and strategy execution through the regional sales organization.

Reporting to the Head of Region with a dotted-line relationship to the Head of Commercial Enablement PLBU, the role is a member of both the Regional Lead Team and the PLBU Lead Team and serves as the primary commercial bridge between the region and the Business Unit. The role owns the regional PLBU business result and field sales execution in close collaboration with regional, hub and country leadership, while partnering with Commercial Excellence, Marketing and Customer Experience, Finance, Operations and other relevant functions.

Job Responsibilities

  • Co-create the PLBU commercial strategy, regional growth agenda, sales roadmap and go-to-market approach with Business Unit and Commercial Enablement leadership, ensuring customer, market and regional priorities are reflected in shared commercial choices.
  • Translate agreed PLBU strategy into mid- to long-term regional business and sales plans, annual targets, market priorities and resource choices that guide execution across countries, clusters and sales teams.
  • Own regional PLBU performance against revenue, growth, profitability, customer acquisition, adoption, market development and sales productivity objectives; identify performance gaps and lead corrective action.
  • Lead, coach and develop the regional PLBU sales organization, establishing clear objectives, accountabilities and performance expectations and building a high-performance, customer-focused and collaborative sales culture.
  • Drive disciplined field execution of launches, campaigns, portfolio priorities and customer activation plans, converting go-to-market strategies into customer engagement, pipeline, adoption and sustainable sales results.
  • Establish a robust regional sales operating cadence covering pipeline and funnel management, forecasting, account and opportunity reviews, performance management and use of agreed commercial tools and metrics.
  • Execute pricing and discount decisions within established frameworks, decision rights and profitability guardrails; drive price realization, deal discipline, portfolio mix and appropriate escalation of exceptions.
  • Lead regional channel and distributor execution within the PLBU framework, including partner priorities, performance, local activation and commercial follow-up, while identifying structural opportunities and capability gaps.
  • Deploy and reinforce PLBU commercial capabilities in the region, including Training and Education and Edge!Up for Sales, ensuring practical adoption by sales teams and connection to customer engagement and commercial outcomes.
  • Build and maintain strategic relationships with key customers, distributors, partners and external stakeholders to strengthen market insight, accelerate growth opportunities and support long-term value creation.
  • Provide timely voice-of-customer, competitive, channel and execution insight to the PLBU Lead Team, Marketing and Customer Experience, and Commercial Excellence to improve propositions, activation plans, commercial frameworks and investment choices.
  • Lead cross-functional alignment across regional and Business Unit stakeholders, including Marketing and Customer Experience, Commercial Excellence, Finance and Operations, to remove execution barriers and deliver the regional PLBU plan.
  • Make and recommend regional commercial trade-offs on priorities, resources and investments within agreed governance, balancing growth, profitability, customer impact and execution capacity and escalating structural issues when required.
  • Ensure all regional commercial and sales activities are conducted in line with company policies, quality and regulatory requirements, ethical standards, approved commercial governance and the Straumann Group Core Beliefs.

Key Skills and Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Marketing, Sales, Life Sciences or a related field; a Master's degree, MBA or relevant postgraduate qualification is preferred. An equivalent combination of relevant education and significant commercial leadership experience will be considered.
  • 10+ years of progressive commercial and sales experience, including significant leadership responsibility for business and sales performance across a country, cluster or region.
  • Experience in dental, medical device, healthcare or another complex B2B environment is preferred, with a proven record of delivering revenue growth and profitability through sales leadership, market development, go-to-market execution and disciplined commercial management across multiple markets.
  • Demonstrated ability to translate Business Unit strategy into mid- to long-term regional business and sales plans and lead execution through a complex, matrixed organization.
  • Strong people leadership experience, including leading and developing sales leaders and teams, setting performance expectations and building capability and accountability.
  • Strong commercial and financial acumen, with experience in forecasting, pipeline management, pricing and discount execution, portfolio mix, channel and distributor performance and resource allocation.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence senior regional and global stakeholders, build strategic customer relationships and use customer, market and performance insight to make sound commercial decisions.

Desired Skills and Attributes

  • Strategic and commercially driven, with strong ownership for regional business performance, sales execution and customer outcomes.
  • Dental laboratory domain knowledge or experience is desirable and will be considered a strong advantage, particularly experience serving dental laboratories, dental factories or lab-focused digital workflows.
  • Customer- and market-oriented, with the ability to translate external insight and competitive dynamics into focused commercial choices and field action.
  • A strong people-leader and coach who creates clarity, builds accountability and develops high-performing teams and future talent.
  • Decisive and pragmatic, able to solve complex issues, prioritize resources and make sound judgments within broad strategic and commercial guidelines.
  • Analytical and financially minded, with disciplined focus on growth, profitability, forecasting, price realization and performance management.
  • Influential and collaborative, able to align Regional Lead Team, PLBU Lead Team and cross-functional stakeholders around shared priorities and trade-offs.
  • Resilient, adaptable and improvement-oriented, role modeling the Straumann Group Core Beliefs and maintaining high standards of integrity and execution.

Work Environment and Travel

The role operates in a highly collaborative, matrixed environment spanning North American and global stakeholders. Regional and international travel is required as needed to support customers, partners, sales teams and Business Unit priorities. The expectation is that this role requires a regular onsite presence in Andover (HQ). We operate a hybrid work pattern.

Management Responsibilities

This position holds management responsibility and is expected to lead, coach and develop the regional PLBU sales organization.

Compensation

Annual base range $190 - 220k + variable 35% bonus + Long Terms Incentive (stock / stock options). Final base pay for this position will vary relative to candidate experience and what the company reasonably anticipates for this position.


All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, or disability.

title: Class A OH Distribution Lineman - Elizabethtown, KY
description:
5 Star Electric, LLC (5 Star) is a premier full-service provider of electrical construction, maintenance, and repair services with offices in Western Kentucky and Dallas/Fort Worth, Texas. 5 Star specializes in Distribution and Transmission Power Line work, Substation, Industrial, Commercial, Streetlighting, and Fiber installations.

Position Title: Overhead Distribution Lineman – A Class

Our Core Values: Guided by Safety. Focused on Communities. Powered by Care.

Classification: Non-Exempt

Essential Functions:

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential functions.

The Overhead Distribution Lineman – A Class is responsible for all Apprentice and Class B & C responsibilities in addition to working energized and de-energized lines and equipment.

Roles and Responsibilities:

  • Thorough knowledge of methods, practices and equipment of electrical line work.
  • Thorough knowledge of the hazards of electrical work and necessary safety precautions.
  • Ability to climb poles and perform strenuous duties in a variety of weather conditions
  • Ability to follow oral and written instructions and communicate effectively verbally and in writing.
  • Ability to work with angry or difficult customers.
  • Skill in operating listed tools and equipment.
  • Ability to accurately read and record data from various types of meter dials.
  • Ability to work in inclement weather.
  • Ability to operate service truck.
  • Digs holes and sets poles for electrical lines.
  • String wire on new construction or in repairing line breaks.
  • Sets and connects transformers and other electrical distribution equipment.
  • Climbs pole’s and makes necessary repairs.
  • Trim trees along electrical lines and perform related work as required.
  • Performs related work as required.
  • Responds to work orders for utility disconnections, reconnections, new orders, and other public works service.
  • Maintains are assigned tools and equipment.
  • You must stand on-call after working hours as needed and directed.
  • Class A Lineman is responsible for ensuring safety standards for himself and his crew and is responsible for his/her own safety at all times.
  • Safety should be the number one priority of any apprentice lineman.
  • It is the apprentice lineman’s responsibility to report and all accidents/incidents to the foreman immediately and to make the foreman aware of any known potential safety hazards that may exist.
  • Other duties as assigned.

Success Factors:

  • Must possess math skills along with basic knowledge of PMP and Electrical Theory.
  • Must be able to work outdoors in diverse terrain and in all weather conditions.
  • Physical capabilities required to safely operate a motor vehicle, in all driving conditions
  • Possesses sight, strength and coordination necessary to safely and effectively operate heavy and light equipment and tools.
  • Lifts up to 50 pounds.
  • Climbs poles and works at heights.
  • Duties entail full-body exertion, strenuous lifting, carrying, pushing and pulling. required to stand, walk; and use hands to finger, handle, feel or operate objects, tools, or controls.
  • Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision and the ability to adjust focus.

Experience and Education:

  • Four (4) years of experience or equivalent hours.

Additional Requirements/Licenses/Certifications:

  • Possession of, or ability to obtain, a valid State of Residence Driver License is required
  • Must have a Valid Class A CDL and current medical examiner card
  • Candidates must pass criminal and Motor Vehicle Record (MVR) background checks and pass a pre-employment drug screen.
  • Must be able to work outdoors in diverse terrain and in all weather conditions.
  • Must complete OSHA 10hr Safety Training Program within 60 days.
  • Completion of formal training program or at least four years of verifiable experience including three years of energized work
  • Successful test completions on rigging, grounding, transformers, hot sticks, weights, and torques.
  • Successful completion of appropriate knowledge and skills examinations.
  • Compliance with Safety Performance Standards
  • May be Employee Performance Tested to a higher level with testing and verifiable experience
  • Possesses sight, strength and coordination necessary to safely and effectively operate heavy and light equipment and tools. .
  • Completion of Insulate/Isolate Course Critical review and recommendations from Operations, Safety/Training
  • Must have ability for frequent travel on needed training requirements and potential for overtime including storm work.
